author: copilot
body:
This PR establishes the repository as a portable `.ai-instructions` module with a canonical `main` source and documented `tool/*` branch workflow for tool-specific outputs. It adds reusable instruction templates, tool mappings, and install/validation scripts so projects can switch branches and sync the correct files into the parent repo.

- **Repository architecture and workflow docs**
  - Replaced minimal root README with an operational guide covering:
    - submodule embedding
    - `tool/*` branch switching
    - install/sync flow into parent project
    - placeholder strategy (`{{PROJECT_NAME}}`, `{{TECH_STACK}}`, etc.)
  - Added `CONTRIBUTING.md` with rules for canonical-vs-tool branch ownership and low-duplication content practices.
  - Added `docs/branch-strategy.md`, `docs/install-workflow.md`, `docs/naming-conventions.md`, `docs/prompt-writing-guidelines.md`, and `docs/tool-mapping.md`.

- **Canonical instruction source on `main`**
  - Added reusable content under:
    - `instructions/common/` (base instructions, coding style, review checklist, context/architecture templates)
    - `instructions/stacks/` (.NET, Angular, Azure, Kubernetes)
    - `instructions/templates/` (new tool and new project scaffolds)
  - Added per-tool adaptation docs under `tools/` for:
    - GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code, ChatGPT, Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, VS Code, JetBrains.

- **Tool-branch output model examples**
  - Added `docs/tool-examples/` with concrete output layouts matching expected `dist/` targets for each tool to make branch output expectations explicit.

- **Cross-platform install/sync tooling**
  - Added `scripts/install-to-project.sh` and `scripts/install-to-project.ps1` with:
    - parent project auto-detection
    - recursive copy from `dist/`
    - directory creation
    - overwrite prompt (or `--force` / `-Force`)
    - dry-run mode (`--dry-run` / `-DryRun`)
    - copied/skipped/overwritten summary
  - PowerShell implementation includes hidden-directory file discovery (`-Force`) for paths like `.cursor` / `.github`.

- **Repository validation utilities**
  - Added `scripts/validate.sh` and `scripts/validate.ps1` to enforce required repository layout and script parse/sanity checks.

```bash
# expected usage in parent repo
git submodule add <REPO_URL> .ai-instructions
cd .ai-instructions
git checkout tool/github-copilot
./scripts/install-to-project.sh --dry-run
./scripts/install-to-project.sh --force
```

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->



<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

Create a repository for managing reusable AI instructions across different developer tools, IDEs, CLIs, and AI coding assistants.

The main goal of this repository is to be embedded inside other software projects, for example as:

  .ai-instructions/

This repository should allow a developer to switch to a tool-specific Git branch and then install or sync the correct AI instruction files into the parent project.

Example usage:

  cd .ai-instructions
  git checkout tool/github-copilot
  ./scripts/install-to-project.sh

After that, the parent project should receive the correct instruction files for GitHub Copilot.

Please design the repository around this workflow.

Repository goals:
- Act as a portable AI instructions repository.
- Be usable as a Git submodule or copied folder inside another project.
- Keep a canonical source of instructions on the main branch.
- Provide tool-specific branches for different AI tools.
- Each tool-specific branch should expose the correct output format and file layout for that tool.
- Include scripts to copy or sync generated instruction files into the parent project.
- Avoid hardcoding one specific project name.
- Use placeholders such as {{PROJECT_NAME}}, {{TECH_STACK}}, {{ARCHITECTURE}}, {{CODING_STYLE}}, {{DOMAIN_RULES}}, and {{CONSTRAINTS}}.

Branch strategy:
- main: canonical source of reusable AI instructions and templates.
- tool/github-copilot: GitHub Copilot-ready instruction layout.
- tool/cursor: Cursor-ready instruction layout.
- tool/claude-code: Claude Code-ready instruction layout.
- tool/chatgpt: ChatGPT-ready instruction layout.
- tool/gemini-cli: Gemini CLI-ready instruction layout.
- tool/codex-cli: Codex CLI-ready instruction layout.
- tool/vscode: VS Code-ready instruction layout.
- tool/jetbrains: JetBrains IDE-ready instruction layout.

Please create files that document this branch strategy clearly.

On the main branch, create this structure:

README.md
CONTRIBUTING.md
docs/
  branch-strategy.md
  install-workflow.md
  naming-conventions.md
  prompt-writing-guidelines.md
  tool-mapping.md
instructions/
  common/
    base-instructions.md
    coding-style.md
    code-review-checklist.md
    project-context-template.md
    architecture-template.md
  stacks/
    dotnet.md
    angular.md
    azure.md
    kubernetes.md
  templates/
    new-tool-template.md
    new-project-template.md
tools/
  github-copilot.md
  cursor.md
  claude-code.md
  chatgpt.md
  gemini-cli.md
  codex-cli.md
  vscode.md
  jetbrains.md
scripts/
  install-to-project.sh
  install-to-project.ps1
  validate.sh
  validate.ps1

The tool-specific branches should conceptually produce a dist/ folder like this:

dist/
  <tool-specific instruction files>

Examples:
- GitHub Copilot branch should produce GitHub Copilot instruction files.
- Cursor branch should produce Cursor rule or instruction files.
- Claude Code branch should produce Claude Code instruction files.
- Codex CLI branch should produce Codex CLI instruction files.
- ChatGPT branch should produce copy-pasteable custom instruction files.
- VS Code branch should produce VS Code-related instruction settings or documentation.
- JetBrains branch should produce JetBrains-related instruction settings or documentation.

The install scripts should:
- Detect the parent project directory.
- Copy files from dist/ into the parent project root.
- Create missing directories when needed.
- Ask before overwriting existing files, unless a --force flag is provided.
- Support dry-run mode.
- Print a clear summary of copied, skipped, and overwritten files.
- Work on macOS, Linux, and Windows where possible.
- Include both shell and PowerShell versions.

Please include documentation for these workflows:

1. Add this repository into a project as a submodule:

   git submodule add <REPO_URL> .ai-instructions

2. Switch to a specific tool branch:

   cd .ai-instructions
   git checkout tool/github-copilot

3. Install the instruction files into the parent project:

   ./scripts/install-to-project.sh

4. Update the instructions repository:

   git pull

5. Switch to another tool:

   git checkout tool/cursor
   ./scripts/install-to-project.sh

Important design constraints:
- Keep the canonical instructions reusable and tool-neutral.
- Tool-specific branches should adapt the canonical instructions to the target tool.
- Avoid duplicating too much content across branches.
- Prefer Markdown.
- Prefer clear and short instruction files over long essays.
- Use English for file names, folder names, headings, and primary documentation.
- Traditional Chinese comments or examples may be included only when useful.
- Make the repository suitable for a C# / .NET / Angular / Azure / Kubernetes developer, but do not make it exclusive to that stack.

Please generate:
1. A complete README.md.
2. A clear branch strategy document.
3. Tool mapping documentation.
4. Main branch instruction templates.
5. Tool-specific example instruction files.
6. Cross-platform install scripts.
...

</details>

author: kapridoo
body:
## Summary

Fixes the mobile (iPhone Safari) regression on `/cotizar` that persisted after PR #19, where the runtime behavior diverged from the static verify.

- **Stepper overflow (Bug 1)**: PR #19's `@media (max-width: 480px)` rules were insufficient — they kept `.stepper__label` ("PASO 01") visible and full padding, forcing horizontal overflow. Also its `overflow-x: hidden` was on `.quote-layout` (a sibling), not the stepper. This change: breakpoint widened to `≤640px`, `.stepper__label { display: none }`, compressed `.stepper__step` padding/gap, and `overflow-x: clip` on `.stepper__track` (the correct container).
- **Modality not selectable on iOS (Bug 2)**: added `touch-action: manipulation` + `-webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent` to `.mode-tile`, `.stepper__step`, `#btn-next`, `#btn-back` (eliminates iOS 300ms tap delay). Refactored `wizard.ts` listeners from `addEventListener(_, _, { signal })` to manual cleanup (`on()` helper + `cleanups[]` cleared on `astro:before-swap`) for iOS Safari < 15.4 compatibility.

## SDD pipeline trace

- Domain: `fix` · Fast path: `full` · Predecessor: PR #19
- Specs: 2 deltas (`forms-email/wizard-responsive-mobile-v2`, `forms-email/wizard-modality-tap-ios`) superseding the PR #19 specs.
- Judgment: 1 iteration, PASS (2 independent judges confirmed listener migration integrity + CSS root-cause fix).

## ⚠️ Validation required before considering closed

Static verify (build + bundle grep + adversarial review) is **PASS**, but touch behavior on iOS Safari can only be confirmed on a real device. **Please open the Cloudflare Pages preview deployment for this PR on your iPhone and confirm:**

- [ ] Stepper renders compact, no horizontal overflow (portrait, iPhone 8 → 15 Pro Max)
- [ ] Tap on any modality (Marítimo / Aéreo / Courier / Multimodal) selects it immediately
- [ ] "Siguiente" advances from step 01 to 02 after selecting modality
- [ ] Internal navigation (cotizar → home → cotizar) keeps the wizard working

## Known follow-ups (technical debt)

- A11y: `.stepper__label { display: none }` hides step text from screen readers in mobile (preexisting pattern; mitigated by each panel's `<h2>`). Tracked in memory observations.

author: mottihoresh
body:
## Summary

- **New library: `STM32Board`** — shared STM32F103 hardware init (CAN at 500 kbps with SJW=4, USART1 DiagSerial, PC13 status LED). Defines `HAL_CAN_MspInit` once, eliminating duplication across all STM32 firmware. Debug output is opt-in via `setDebug(true)` — no string formatting or UART transmission when disabled.
- **New library: `PanelGroup`** — CAN sub-node domain layer. Reads node ID from PA0 strap at boot. Self-registering `OutputBase`/`InputBase` linked lists dispatch `ControlPacket` frames to `LED`, `IntegerOutput`, and `Switch2Pos` objects declared at global scope — mirrors DCS-BIOS exactly.
- **New library: `PanelBridge`** — CAN master / UART bridge. Transparent `ControlPacket` passthrough between RP2040 UART and CAN bus. Forwards heartbeat and echo frames back to RP2040 as 8-byte DIAG frames. 3-second heartbeat watchdog with `onNodeAlive`/`onNodeDead` callbacks.
- **New library: `SimGateway`** — RP2040 USB HID + DCS-BIOS gateway. Sets USB identity (VID 0x2E8A / PID 0x4134), initialises Joystick HID composite device, and manages the UART link to PanelBridge. Parses incoming DIAG frames and dispatches to registered RTT/heartbeat/error callbacks.
- **New file: `CANProtocol/HIDControls.h`** — extracts `CTRL_ROLL`/`PITCH`/`THROTTLE`/`RUDDER`/`BRAKE_L`/`BRAKE_R`/`ZOOM` constants from `CANProtocol.h` into a dedicated HID controls header.
- **Prototype refactors** — all three prototype `main.cpp` files rewritten to use the new libraries. Each is now 15–35 lines of sketch-level application code; all infrastructure has moved into the libraries.
- **Doxygen docblocks and README** added to all four libraries following the OpenHornet style guide.

## What a reviewer should know

- `STM32Board::begin()` and `PanelGroup::setup()` take **no arguments** — all hardware pins are fixed constants on the OpenSkyhawk STM32 boards (PA11/PA12 CAN, PA9/PA10 USART1, PC13 LED, PA0 strap).
- `#define DCSBIOS_DEFAULT_SERIAL` **must** appear in the sketch's translation unit before `#include <DcsBios.h>`. SimGateway does not include DcsBios.h — sketches own the DCS-BIOS lifecycle.
- DiagSerial UART (`_diag.begin(115200)`) is always initialised in `begin()` (peripheral config is negligible). The `_debugOn` flag gates all `print()` calls so there is zero CPU cost when debug is disabled.
- All three prototype builds pass `pio run` — SubNode 12% flash / 7.6% RAM, Master 12% flash / 9.5% RAM, RP2040 3.2% flash / 3.8% RAM.

## Test plan

- [x] Flash `CAN_Test_SubNode` + `CAN_Test_Master`: confirm heartbeat + echo on DiagSerial (`STM32Board::setDebug(true)`) — no regressions vs. validated 500 kbps soak
- [x] Flash `CAN_Test_RP2040_PIO`: confirm `PONG` RTT responses at expected cadence via USB serial
- [x] Confirm `STM32Board::setDebug(false)` (default): zero serial output, LED blink pattern intact
- [x] `pio run` on all three projects passes cleanly

author: copilot
body:
Runtime verification/self-test was executing through the same lifecycle surfaces as production inference, causing post-self-test instability (state resets, listener churn, and runtime invalidation loops). This change separates verification execution/state from live runtime orchestration while preserving native inference semantics.

- **Verification lifecycle isolation**
  - Added a dedicated verification scope in `AndroidFfiRuntimeProvider` (`_runInVerificationScope`) with explicit boundaries:
    - `[VERIFICATION_SCOPE_ENTER]`
    - `[VERIFICATION_SCOPE_EXIT]`
    - `[VERIFICATION_STATE_ISOLATED]`
  - Verification-scope transitions are prevented from mutating production `LocalRuntimeMonitor` and `RuntimeStateMachine` (`[VERIFICATION_UI_IGNORED]`).

- **Dedicated verification monitor**
  - Introduced `RuntimeVerificationMonitor` + `RuntimeVerificationState` with verification-only phases:
    - `loading`, `running`, `passed`, `failed`
  - Verification state now tracks independently from production `LocalRuntimeMonitor.state`.

- **Self-test execution/session isolation**
  - Added `streamVerificationInference(...)` for isolated verification inference.
  - `runtime_self_test` no longer participates in `activeInferenceSessions` collision/cleanup paths used for user inference.
  - Self-test service routes Android verification through isolated APIs (`validateRuntimeInVerificationScope`, `streamVerificationInference`).

- **Verification reuse / storm prevention**
  - Added verification reuse guard keyed by verified model path + ABI + manual reset flag.
  - Reuse path skips redundant re-verification and emits:
    - `[RUNTIME_VERIFICATION_REUSED]`
    - `[VERIFICATION_REUSE]`
  - ABI drift invalidates prior verification and forces re-verification only when required.

- **Behavioral guardrails kept intact**
  - No FFI binding rewrites.
  - No token polling semantic changes.
  - No GGUF load behavior changes.
  - No model hardcoding/lockout policy changes beyond lifecycle isolation.

```dart
await _runInVerificationScope(
  modelPath: selectedModel?.localPath,
  action: () async {
    verificationMonitor.update(RuntimeVerificationPhase.loading);
    final snapshot = await super.validateRuntime(selectedModel: selectedModel);
    verificationMonitor.update(RuntimeVerificationPhase.running);
    return snapshot; // production monitor/state machine untouched in this scope
  },
);
```

author: juanpq1812-maker
body:
## Resumen

3 mejoras independientes que enriquecen la experiencia sin tocar auth, colores ni la lógica de `outfit_uses`.

---

## Mejora 1 — Generar outfit desde una prenda específica

**Archivos:** `ClothingCard.tsx`, `OutfitGenerator.tsx`, `outfits/page.tsx`, `outfits/actions.ts`, `lib/ai/generateOutfits.ts`

Cada card del armario ahora tiene un botón `✨ Crear outfit con esta prenda` que:
- Navega a `/outfits?prenda=<id>&nombre=<nombre codificado>`
- La página `/outfits` lee esos params y se los pasa al `OutfitGenerator`
- El generador muestra un banner **"Basado en: [nombre]"** y dispara la generación automáticamente al montar
- El prompt de la IA incluye una **regla obligatoria**: ese item debe aparecer en los 2 outfits
- El botón "Regenerar" del banner respeta la prenda fija
- Los 3 modos (ocasión, descripción, sorpréndeme) pasan `lockedItemId` a la Server Action

## Mejora 2 — Prenda olvidada con outfits sugeridos

**Archivo:** `DashboardView.tsx`

La sección "Prenda olvidada" en el Dashboard pasó de mostrar solo el nombre a:
```
😴 Olvidada hace X días
[foto]  Nombre de la prenda
        La IA puede armar outfits con esta prenda
        Ver outfits sugeridos →
```
El link usa el mismo flujo de la Mejora 1 (`?prenda=ID&nombre=NOMBRE`), incentivando rescatar prendas olvidadas.

## Mejora 3 — /impact reencuadrado a "Tu consumo inteligente"

**Archivo:** `app/impact/page.tsx`

| Antes | Después |
|-------|---------|
| "Tu impacto positivo" | "Tu consumo inteligente" |
| Héroe: `43 kg CO₂ evitados` | Héroe: `85% de tu armario activo` |
| Secundarias: agua + usos | Secundarias: outfits únicos, usos promedio/prenda, prendas sin usar |
| Proyección con ONU | Estado vacío con CTA directo |

Cálculo del % activo: `(prendas en outfits usados / total prendas) × 100`. Se eliminaron todas las referencias a CO₂, árboles, agua y ONU.

---

## Cómo probar cada mejora

### Mejora 1
1. Ir a `/wardrobe` — cada card de prenda tiene el botón `✨ Crear outfit con esta prenda`
2. Hacer clic → debe navegar a `/outfits?prenda=...&nombre=...` y auto-generar
3. Verificar que el banner verde muestra "Basado en: [nombre de la prenda]"
4. Verificar que los outfits generados contienen esa prenda
5. Hacer clic en "🔄 Regenerar" del banner → outfits nuevos, siempre con la misma prenda
6. Cambiar de tab (por ocasión / descripción / sorpréndeme) y generar → prenda fija en todos

### Mejora 2
1. Ir al Dashboard `/` con una cuenta que tenga prendas y al menos una con más de 30 días sin usar
2. Verificar que la sección "😴 Olvidada hace X días" muestra el texto y el link
3. Hacer clic en "Ver outfits sugeridos →" → debe llevar a `/outfits` con la prenda pre-seleccionada

### Mejora 3
1. Ir a `/impact`
2. Sin usos: ver estado vacío con ícono 👗 y CTA "Generar mi primer outfit →"
3. Con usos: ver el % del armario activo como número animado + 3 métricas secundarias
4. Confirmar que no hay ninguna mención a CO₂, árboles, agua ni ONU

---

## Edge cases detectados

- **Armario con < 2 prendas:** el botón de ClothingCard lleva a `/outfits`, donde el `EmptyWardrobeCallout` existente maneja el caso sin romper nada
- **Prenda eliminada después de hacer clic:** la IA valida todos los IDs contra el armario real (lógica anti-alucinación existente); si el ID no existe, el outfit se descarta y se muestra el error normal de "no outfits válidos"
- **Nombre de prenda con caracteres especiales:** se usa `encodeURIComponent` al construir la URL y `decodeURIComponent` al leerla en el Server Component
- **`lockedItemId` inválido (ID que no pertenece al usuario):** RLS de Supabase bloquea la lectura, la IA recibe el armario normal y simplemente no puede incluir el item; el outfit se genera sin él (el usuario no nota diferencia)
- **% armario activo con 0 prendas:** se muestra `0%` sin dividir por cero (guard explícito `totalItems > 0`)
- **Dashboard sin prenda olvidada:** el bloque es condicional, no renderiza nada (`prendaOlvidada` puede ser `null`)
- **Outfit generado con prenda fija pero < 3 prendas válidas:** el validador existente (`cleanIds.length < 3`) descarta ese outfit y la IA genera el siguiente; si no hay outfits válidos, aparece el error normal

---

## Archivos modificados

| Archivo | Cambio |
|---------|--------|
| `src/lib/ai/generateOutfits.ts` | `lockedItemId` en input + regla obligatoria en el prompt |
| `src/app/outfits/actions.ts` | `lockedItemId` en `GenerateActionInput`, pasa al lib |
| `src/app/outfits/page.tsx` | Lee `?prenda` y `?nombre`, pasa a `OutfitGenerator` |
| `src/components/outfits/OutfitGenerator.tsx` | Props `lockedItemId/Name`, `LockedGarmentBanner`, auto-genera |
| `src/components/wardrobe/ClothingCard.tsx` | Link `✨ Crear outfit con esta prenda` |
| `src/components/dashboard/DashboardView.tsx` | Sección prenda olvidada mejorada con link |
| `src/app/impact/page.tsx` | Reescritura completa: consumo inteligente, sin CO₂/ONU |

## Summary

Repairs **4 pre-existing test failures** — two unrelated test-harness
defects. Test files only; no production code.

### 1. `test_risk_memory_embedding_service.py::TestRealModelSmoke` ×3

The class is gated by `@skipif(not _MODEL_CACHE_AVAILABLE)`, but that
guard checks only the BGE-M3 **model-cache directory** — not whether the
`sentence-transformers` **library** is importable. With the cache
present but the library absent, the 3 tests *ran* and crashed on
`import sentence_transformers` (`ModuleNotFoundError`) — **fail, not
skip**, defeating the whole point of the skip guard.

**Fix:** add `_sentence_transformers_installed()` and
`_REAL_MODEL_READY = cache AND library`; the `skipif` now gates on the
complete precondition. The 3 tests skip cleanly when the library is
absent (their *designed* behavior) and run for real when it is present.

### 2. `test_platform_skeleton.py::test_platform_import_has_no_side_effects`

The subprocess `import backend.qm_platform` ran with only repo-root on
`sys.path`. The codebase **mixes two import styles** — `from engines...`
(top-level, needs `backend/` on path) and `from backend.qm_platform...`
(needs repo-root) — so the subprocess hit `No module named 'engines'`.

**Fix:** pass `PYTHONPATH` containing **both** repo-root and `backend/`,
replicating the real runtime `sys.path` (production mounts `backend/`
via a `.pth` file).

## Verification

- `pytest tests/test_platform_skeleton.py tests/test_risk_memory_embedding_service.py`
  → **84 passed / 3 skipped / 0 fail** (was 4 fail). The 3 skips are
  `TestRealModelSmoke` (library absent — designed skip).
- `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` → clean.

To make `TestRealModelSmoke` *run* for real: `pip install
sentence-transformers` (the BGE-M3 model cache is already on disk).

## Test plan

- [x] 4 failures → 0 (1 pass, 3 clean skip)
- [x] ruff clean
- [x] code-reviewer pass

author: yedianyang
body:
## 概述

Audio Input Layer：电影同期录音流水线的音频输入层。从声卡 / 虚拟声卡 / USB 接口 / 录音机 line-out 实时采集，或读取音频文件，统一输出 16kHz int16、各声道独立的 AudioChunk，供下游 take 检测与 Cactus ASR 消费。

## 输入 / 输出契约

### 输入

- 音频源，二选一：
  - 实时设备 `DeviceSource(device, config)`，device 为声卡 / 虚拟声卡 / USB 接口 / 录音机 line-out 的索引（int）或名称（str）
  - 音频文件 `FileSource(path, config)`，path 为 WAV / BWF / AIFF / FLAC 文件路径（str）
- `config: AudioConfig`（frozen dataclass）：chunk_ms（默认 200）、max_channels（默认 2）
- 层内部接纳的原始音频：源原生采样率（任意，如 44.1k / 48k）、任意声道数、float32

### 输出

用法 `with <Source> as src: for chunk in src:` —— 上下文管理器 + AudioChunk 迭代器。每次迭代产出一个 AudioChunk（frozen dataclass）：

| 字段 | 类型 | 含义 |
|---|---|---|
| seq | int | 从 0 单调递增的块序号 |
| channels | list[np.ndarray] | 各声道独立数组，见下 |
| n_frames | int | 本块每声道的帧数 |
| start_frame | int | 本块在 16kHz 输出时间轴上的累计起始帧 |
| sample_rate | int | 恒为 16000（Cactus ASR 硬约束） |

- channels[i] 是第 i 路：一维 np.int16 数组，单声道、16kHz。各声道不交织、不混音 —— 是分开的独立信号，纯序号标识（无 Boom / Lav 名）
- 声道数为 1 或 2 = min(源声道数, max_channels)；源超过 2 声道时取前 2 路，其余静默丢弃，不报错
- 块大小约 chunk_ms（200ms）；n_frames 因 soxr 滤波延迟逐块抖动（16k 下约 2936~3426）；文件源 EOF 时额外吐一个小的尾部排出块

## 内容

- AudioSource：拉取式抽象，上下文管理器 + 迭代器，模板方法三钩子
- DeviceSource：sounddevice 阻塞式实时采集
- FileSource：soundfile 批处理读取（WAV / BWF / AIFF / FLAC）
- ChannelProcessor：每声道 soxr 流式重采样到 16kHz，转 int16
- 多声道规则：处理前 2 路，超出丢弃不报错，设计上可扩展为 N 路
- 设计 spec 与实现 plan（docs/）
- soxr GIL 释放与并行实验（experiments/）
- scripts/audio_smoke.py：交互式手动验证封装

## 验证

- 24 个自动化测试全过（pytest）
- 真机采集已验证：Babyface Pro（14 声道截断为 2、实时信号 peak 跟随）、BlackHole 2ch、MacBook 麦克风（含说话时 peak 上升）
- 文件路径已验证：2s 立体声 48k 输出正好 32000 帧 = 2s × 16000，重采样滤波尾部零丢失
- ruff、mypy 通过

## 为什么是 Draft

- 待同事 review
- 后端 venv 标准化未定：当前依赖借 cactus venv，requirements.txt 仅含 4 个运行时依赖，pytest / ruff / mypy 未钉版本
- 与下游（Cactus ASR、take 边界检测）的对接是后续独立工作

## 合并方式

转 Ready、review 通过后 squash and merge 到 main。

author: mtrifilo
body:
## Summary
A backend **stage** deploy failed Railway's healthcheck and wasn't promoted — `1/1 replicas never became healthy` within the **30s** retry window — despite a clean build, a clean + current DB, and **no crash** in the container logs. Verified via Railway CLI that it wasn't a code regression (frontend-only / request-time merges; `schema_migrations` clean and at HEAD; the active deploy stayed healthy throughout). The container just didn't bind `:8080` within 30s on a contended cold start.

The server initializes ~8 background services + a DB pool on boot, so `healthcheckTimeout = 30` is tight — especially under deploy churn (three deploys landed within ~1 minute, each triggering a backend redeploy). This raises it to `120`.

- A healthy app answers `/health` in <1s, so the wider window only matters during slow/contended cold starts — pure downside protection, no runtime cost.

## Test plan
- [x] N/A — single config-value change in `backend/railway.toml` (`30` → `120`); no code, no test references this file.

## Manual repro / verification
Verification is the next stage deploy promoting cleanly (this config only takes effect once merged + deployed). A manual `railway redeploy` of the failed commit was also triggered separately to clear the immediate stuck deploy.

## Simplify
N/A — one-line config value change; nothing for the reuse/quality/efficiency reviewers to assess.

## Out of scope
Moving migrations to a dedicated release phase or trimming boot-time work — the timeout bump is the minimal targeted fix.

Closes PSY-805

author: copilot
body:
Self-hosted Hydra Cloud was still tied to config-time server values, which made switching servers cumbersome and opaque from the app. This updates the self-host flow so the active cloud server can be selected in the GUI and the app can surface whether the expected cloud endpoints are reachable.

- **Runtime cloud server configuration**
  - Added a persisted `cloudServerUrl` user preference.
  - Refactored self-host config resolution into a runtime config object instead of static env-only values.
  - Derived API, auth, checkout, Nimbus, and WS endpoints from the selected base URL.

- **Main-process reconfiguration**
  - Applied the selected cloud server during startup from stored preferences.
  - Reconfigured `HydraApi` when the server changes instead of requiring a rebuild/relaunch path through env config.
  - Reset auth/session state and closed WS connections on server change so the app does not keep stale credentials or sockets against the previous server.

- **Renderer / IPC surface**
  - Added IPC to read the current resolved cloud server config.
  - Added IPC to check connectivity for the selected server and report per-endpoint status.
  - Extended renderer declarations so the new config/connectivity types are available end-to-end.

- **Settings UI**
  - Added self-host-only account/settings controls to edit the cloud server URL from the GUI.
  - Added explicit **test** and **apply** actions.
  - Surfaced per-check status for API/auth/checkout reachability so server issues are visible before/after switching.

- **Connectivity behavior**
  - API checks now prefer `/health` and fall back to the API root, avoiding a hard dependency on a single health endpoint shape.
  - Auth and checkout pages are checked directly since those are part of the self-host flow used by the app.

```ts
await window.electron.updateUserPreferences({
  cloudServerUrl: "http://my-selfhosted-hydra:4000",
});

const result = await window.electron.checkCloudServerConnectivity(
  "http://my-selfhosted-hydra:4000"
);
```

## Summary
This PR enhances security and data integrity by properly escaping HTML special characters in dropdown options and fixing the CSV export format for currency amounts.

## Key Changes

- **Enhanced HTML escaping in `escapeHtml()` function**: Extended the function to escape quotes (`"` and `'`) in addition to the standard HTML entities. This ensures the result is safe when used inside HTML attributes, not just text content.

- **Applied escaping to all category/subcategory dropdowns**: Updated six locations where category and subcategory names are rendered in `<option>` elements to use `escapeHtml()`, preventing potential XSS vulnerabilities if category names contain special characters.

- **Fixed CSV export amount formatting**: Modified the CSV export to properly convert amounts from stored integer cents to decimal dollars using the `fromCents()` function, ensuring exported data matches the expected currency format.

## Implementation Details

- The `escapeHtml()` function now chains `.replace()` calls to escape both double and single quotes after `div.innerHTML` handles the standard HTML entities.
- All dropdown population functions (`showEditCategory`, `populateCategoryDropdowns`, `updateRuleSubcategoryOptions`, `renderActivityItems`) now consistently escape user-provided category names.
- CSV export logic now identifies the `amount` column index and applies currency conversion only to that column while preserving the existing CSV quoting and escaping behavior.

author: bpamiri
body:
## Summary

Fixes the root cause behind #2773. The user's `Fresh installation of Wheels 4.0.1 → wheels new hello → wheels start → The key [WO] does not exist.` cascade traces back to a one-line packaging bug: the .deb / .rpm contents rule unzipped `wheels-core-VER.zip` (which carries a top-level `wheels/` directory) into `./build/framework/`, then pointed nfpm `type: tree` at the outer directory. Result on disk after `dpkg -X` / `rpm2cpio`:

```
ACTUAL    /opt/wheels/module/vendor/wheels/wheels/Injector.cfc   ← double-nested
EXPECTED  /opt/wheels/module/vendor/wheels/Injector.cfc
```

The wrapper-side sync (`/opt/wheels/module/*` → `~/.wheels/modules/wheels/*`) and the `wheels new` framework copy both faithfully propagate the misnesting, so Lucee's generated `/wheels` mapping points at an empty outer directory and `new wheels.Injector("wheels.Bindings")` in `public/Application.cfc` throws `could not find component or class with name [wheels.Injector]` on the very first request. The cryptic `[WO]` error in the issue is the secondary cascade.

The brew formula doesn't hit this because it explicitly re-introduces the wheels/ wrapper at stage time:

```ruby
# homebrew-wheels/Formula/wheels.rb:62
resource("wheels_core").stage do
  (share/"wheels/framework/wheels").install Dir["*"]
end
```

This PR brings the .deb / .rpm staging in line by pinning nfpm `src` at `./build/framework/wheels/` (the inner directory) in both `nfpm-wheels.yaml` and `nfpm-wheels-be.yaml`. Comments in each file cross-link to the brew handling and to #2773 so the reasoning is preserved in-tree.

I confirmed the bug against the actually-published GA artifacts (the .deb and .rpm currently sitting on the v4.0.1 release):

```
$ tar -tf data.tar.gz | grep Injector
./opt/wheels/module/vendor/wheels/wheels/Injector.cfc

$ bsdtar -tf wheels-4.0.1.x86_64.rpm | grep Injector
/opt/wheels/module/vendor/wheels/wheels/Injector.cfc

The change is build-config only — no framework / CLI / template code is modified, and the existing `wheels-core-VER.zip` / `wheels-module-VER.tar.gz` artifact builders stay unchanged.

## Related Issue

Closes #2773

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Enhancement to existing feature
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Refactoring

## Feature Completeness Checklist

- [x] **DCO sign-off** — `Signed-off-by:` trailer present
- [x] **Tests** — new `it()` block per channel in `vendor/wheels/tests/specs/cli/LinuxPackageStagingSpec.cfc` asserts the `src` + `dst` pair lands at the correct flatten-friendly path. Follows the existing structural-assertion pattern from #2700 (the file already pins four other packaging invariants the same way).
- [ ] **Framework Docs** — left unchecked; no user-visible behavior change once the rebuilt artifact ships. `bot-update-docs.yml` can follow up if anything in the installing guide needs nuance.
- [ ] **AI Reference Docs** — left unchecked.
- [ ] **CLAUDE.md** — left unchecked; the cross-engine invariants and anti-patterns sections aren't affected.
- [x] **CHANGELOG.md** — new `[Unreleased] → Fixed` entry added above the 4.0.1 header.
- [ ] **Test runner passes locally** — structural verification was done via equivalent grep + perl POSIX patterns over both YAMLs (positive match for the fixed form, zero matches for the buggy form, src+dst still paired). Running the new spec through the CFML runner on this Mac was blocked by a port-8081 collision with two stale `wheels server` processes from prior dev sessions — the CI compat-matrix will run the spec across every engine × DB on this PR.

## Test Plan

- [ ] CI compat-matrix runs `vendor/wheels/tests/specs/cli/LinuxPackageStagingSpec.cfc` on every engine × DB combination
- [ ] After merge + 4.0.2 tag, the rebuilt `wheels_4.0.2_amd64.deb` and `wheels-4.0.2.x86_64.rpm` artifacts should place `Injector.cfc` at `/opt/wheels/module/vendor/wheels/Injector.cfc` (not `.../vendor/wheels/wheels/Injector.cfc`). Quick verification:

ar x wheels_4.0.2_amd64.deb && tar -tzf data.tar.gz | grep -E '/Injector.cfc$'
# Expect exactly one line ending in /opt/wheels/module/vendor/wheels/Injector.cfc
```

## Release impact

The published v4.0.1 .deb / .rpm artifacts are baked-broken (the fix lives in build config, not in any framework/CLI code that's also in the artifact). Need to tag **4.0.2** to deliver the fix to Linux users — `apt install ./wheels_4.0.1_amd64.deb` will continue to ship the broken layout until the new patch release is cut.

## Follow-ups (separate PRs)

- [PR #2774](https://github.com/wheels-dev/wheels/pull/2774) (already open from wheels-bot) — defensive `application.wo` guard in `onError` so future init failures surface the underlying exception instead of the WO cascade. Worth landing alongside this fix; independent.
- The current `tools/ci/smoke-test-module.sh` bypasses the nfpm-assembled layout via `WHEELS_FRAMEWORK_PATH`, which is why this regression escaped. Worth adding a sibling smoke step that extracts the built .deb and asserts on the on-disk framework path — separate scope, separate PR.

body:
## Summary
This PR introduces a new "Swap Items" modal for exchanging contents between drawers in the visual storage interface, along with significant UI improvements, permission refinements, and database schema updates.

## Key Changes

### New Features
- **Swap Drawer Items Modal**: Added new modal (`swapItemsModal`) in `visual_storage.html` that allows users to swap all items and batch overrides between two drawers, with optional thumbnail/metadata swapping
- **Batch QR Sticker Generation**: New template `batch_qr_sticker.html` for generating QR/barcode stickers for item batches
- **Batch Data Extraction**: Added `get_batch_data()` function in `qr_utils.py` to extract printable data from `ItemBatch` objects with support for batch-specific placeholders
- **Share Files Scanning**: Added "Scan for Changes" button in system settings to sync Share File directories with the database

### Database & Models
- Added `user_uid` column to `users` table (VARCHAR(6)) with auto-generation logic in `init_db.py`
- Backfill logic for existing users without `user_uid` values
- User UID generation function: `_generate_user_uid()` creates unique identifiers in format `UXXXXX`

### Permission & Access Control
- Changed `move_drawer_items()` endpoint permission from `location_management.edit` to `items.edit_info`
- Removed `is_admin()` checks in favor of explicit permission checks in:
  - QR template preview/print endpoints
  - Location QR sticker generation
  - System logo/company logo deletion
- Added `can_view_costing` permission check in projects view

### UI/UX Improvements
- **Drawer Grid Enhancements**: 
  - Added legend showing drawer states (Empty, Has Items, Merged, Group, Unavailable, Source)
  - Improved grid styling with better visual hierarchy
  - Added scrollable container for large grids
  - Enhanced cell styling with gradient backgrounds and better spacing
- **Move Items Modal**: Refactored layout with improved legend display and grid scrolling
- **Project Form**: Updated hardcoded colors to use CSS variables (`var(--bs-border-color)`, `var(--bs-tertiary-bg)`, etc.)
- **Contacts Settings**: Expanded to show users section with profile pictures and user information
- **User Management**: 
  - Pre-select "Viewer" role as default for new users (safer default)
  - Display user names instead of usernames in lending/return logs
  - Added user UID display in contacts

### Data & Template Updates
- Added `all_racks_data` to visual storage context with comprehensive rack metadata (rows, cols, merged cells, drawer info)
- Updated QR template placeholders to include batch-specific fields
- Improved rack option data attributes in move items modal
- Enhanced project detail and form templates with CSS variable usage

### Code Quality
- Removed unused data attributes from rack options in move items modal
- Improved form validation and user creation defaults
- Better separation of concerns with explicit permission checks

## Notable Implementation Details
- Swap functionality mirrors move functionality but exchanges items bidirectionally
- User UID generation uses cryptographically secure random selection
- Batch data extraction supports both main location following and independent batch locations
- Permission system now consistently uses `has_permission()` instead of `is_admin()` checks
- Share file scanning integrates with existing file management infrastructure

author: raajkumars
body:
Fixes qwickapps/exo#18

## Summary

`mp.Process.is_alive()` raises `ValueError("process object is closed")` when the process has already entered the closed state — which happens after an ungraceful subprocess exit under heavy load. `_check_runner` and `_watch_runner` call `is_alive()` without guarding for this, causing an unhandled crash.

## Change

Introduced a single helper method:

```python
def _is_runner_alive(self) -> bool:
    """Return runner_process.is_alive(), treating a closed process as not alive."""
    try:
        return self.runner_process.is_alive()
    except ValueError:
        return False
```

Replaced all 6 `self.runner_process.is_alive()` call sites with `self._is_runner_alive()`:

| Line (pre-patch) | Location | Vulnerability |
|---|---|---|
| 249 | `_watch_runner` — 5s background poll | reported crash path |
| 256 | `_check_runner` — main reported site | reported crash path |
| 134 | shutdown teardown | reachable if process closes before teardown |
| 141 | shutdown teardown | same |
| 149 | shutdown teardown | same |
| 158 | shutdown teardown while-loop | same |

## Behaviour

No change on the normal path. A closed process is treated identically to a dead process — the supervisor proceeds with its restart/teardown logic rather than crashing with an unhandled `ValueError`.

## Files changed

- `src/exo/worker/runner/runner_supervisor.py`: +13 −6 lines (1 new method, 6 call-site replacements)

| `src/utils/deterministicHash.ts` | FNV-1a 32-bit hash + deterministic JSON stringify (sorted keys). Used for stable content-addressable hashing in the browser renderer. |
| `src/levels/roomCacheManifest.ts` | `RoomCacheManifest` types, `validateManifest()`, `ExportProgressEvent` union — shared between editor and game. |
| `src/editor/editorExportProgressModal.ts` | Live progress modal DOM component shown during Electron export. Auto-dismisses on success; shows a Close button on error. |
| `docs/campaign-room-cache-architecture.md` | Full architecture documentation covering file layout, manifest format, export flow, stale-cache detection, and next steps. |

### Modified files

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `electron/main.cjs` | Added `dw:export-campaign-with-progress` IPC: streams progress events, writes enhanced `manifest.json` with per-room SHA-256 hashes, selective room updates (skip unchanged rooms), supports both official and custom campaigns. Enhanced `dw:save-official-campaign` to also write the new manifest format. Added `dw:read-room-cache-manifest` IPC for runtime cache validation. Added `deterministicStringify` + `computeContentHash` helpers. |
| `electron/preload.cjs` | Exposes `exportCampaignWithProgress`, `onExportProgress`, `offExportProgress`, `readRoomCacheManifest` alongside the existing `saveOfficialCampaignToProject`. |
| `src/electron.d.ts` | TypeScript types for the full new IPC surface. |
| `src/editor/editorExport.ts` | `exportMainCampaignJson` and `exportCampaignJson` accept an optional `progressRoot` parameter. When in Electron with a root element, they use `exportCampaignWithProgress` IPC + progress modal. Legacy Electron path (no progress root) falls back to `saveOfficialCampaignToProject` + `window.alert`. Browser path is unchanged. |
| `src/editor/editorController.ts` | Passes `uiRoot` as `progressRoot` to export callbacks. |
| `src/build-info.ts` | BUILD_NUMBER bumped to 380. |

---

## How Electron export works now

1. User clicks **Export Campaign** in the Electron editor.
2. `exportMainCampaignJson(pendingEdits, uiRoot)` is called.
3. A progress modal appears over the editor UI.
4. `dustweaverElectron.onExportProgress(cb)` registers a listener.
5. `dustweaverElectron.exportCampaignWithProgress(exported, { isOfficialCampaign: true })` is invoked.
6. The main process streams `dw:export-progress` events as it writes each room.
7. The modal updates in real time: `"Exporting room 12 / 84: Marble Cavern"`.
8. On completion the modal shows `"✅ Export Complete"` and auto-dismisses after 2 s.
9. On error, the modal shows `"❌ Export Failed"` with a Close button.

Each room's `SavedRoomV2` content is hashed. Only rooms whose hash changed since the last export are rewritten; unchanged rooms are skipped.

The written `manifest.json` contains per-room hashes, campaign hash, schema version, and export timestamp — enough to detect staleness on next load.

---

## How browser export behaves

Unchanged from before. `window.dustweaverElectron` is `undefined`, so the code falls through to the download path:
- Main campaign → triggers download of `DustweaverCampaign.dwcampaign.json`
- Custom campaign → triggers download of `<id>.dwcampaign.json`

No room files are written in browser mode.

---

## How runtime room loading works

Not changed at BUILD 380. The runtime still loads rooms from TypeScript bundles (official campaign) or from the packed `.dwcampaign.json` (custom). The new `dw:read-room-cache-manifest` IPC provides the infrastructure for lazy room loading from cache files in a future pass.

See `docs/campaign-room-cache-architecture.md` → "Runtime Room Loading" for the full plan.

---

## How stale cache detection works

`validateManifest(manifest, campaignId, campaignHash)` in `roomCacheManifest.ts` checks:

1. Campaign ID matches.
2. `roomCacheVersion === 1` (current format version).
3. Campaign content hash matches (computed over rooms + worldMap + campaign metadata, excluding volatile timestamps).

Any mismatch returns `{ isValid: false, reason: '...' }` triggering regeneration.

---

## Limitations / next steps

- **Lazy runtime loading from room files** (gameplay) is not yet wired up. The infrastructure (IPC, manifest types, `validateManifest`) is in place. Integration into the game loop is the next step.
- **Custom campaign cache generation on first load** (when a user places a `.dwcampaign.json` and opens it in Electron) needs a hook in `game.ts` / `campaignSource.ts`.
- The `deterministicStringify` in `main.cjs` is intentionally duplicated from the TypeScript source because `main.cjs` cannot import TypeScript directly. Both must be kept in sync.

author: heymaikol
body:
Fixes #5929.

## Summary

- Adds an opt-in, time-based nightlight schedule managed through a gum TUI
- Repoints the toggle menu's Nightlight entry **and** the `SUPER+CTRL+N` keybinding at the TUI
- Removes the standalone manual `omarchy toggle nightlight` (redundant with the schedule's enable/disable)
- Settings (intensity / start / end) persist across reboots; off by default; user's pre-enable `hyprsunset.conf` is preserved and restored on disable

## What changes

Both the Trigger → Toggle → **Nightlight** entry and the `SUPER+CTRL+N` keybinding now open a floating terminal running `omarchy-tui-nightlight`. The TUI shows current status, intensity (K), and the start/end times, and lets the user:

- Enable / disable the schedule
- Pick intensity from presets (3000–5500K) or a custom Kelvin value
- Set start / end times from presets or `HH:MM` input

When enabled, the schedule writes the chosen warm + identity profiles to `~/.config/hypr/hyprsunset.conf` and adds `hyprsunset` to autostart. Both the post-Lua-migration `autostart.lua` and the pre-migration `autostart.conf` formats are supported. The user's pre-enable `hyprsunset.conf` is copied to `~/.local/state/omarchy/hyprsunset.preauto.conf` so a customized config isn't lost — on disable it's moved back into place; if no backup is present (state wiped, fresh install) the Omarchy default is used as a fallback. The autostart entry is removed on disable.

State lives in:

- `~/.local/state/omarchy/toggles/nightlight-schedule` — enabled flag
- `~/.local/state/omarchy/nightlight-schedule.conf` — `TEMPERATURE`, `START_TIME`, `END_TIME`
- `~/.local/state/omarchy/hyprsunset.preauto.conf` — backup of the user's pre-enable config (transient; removed on disable)

Defaults: disabled, 4000K, 20:00 → 07:00.

## New commands

| Route | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `omarchy tui nightlight` | The TUI manager (also reached via menu / `SUPER+CTRL+N`) |
| `omarchy nightlight schedule status\|enable\|disable\|toggle\|apply` | Headless control |
| `omarchy nightlight schedule set-intensity <K>` | Update temperature (validated 1000–6500) |
| `omarchy nightlight schedule set-start <HH:MM>` / `set-end <HH:MM>` | Update schedule times |
| `omarchy toggle nightlight-schedule` | Thin wrapper for the toggle |

## Removed

- `omarchy-toggle-nightlight` (the standalone manual 4000K ↔ 6000K toggle). Anything that used to call it should now use `omarchy nightlight schedule enable` / `disable`, or open the TUI.

## Test plan

- [ ] `SUPER+CTRL+N` opens the TUI; panel shows defaults (Disabled · 4000K · 20:00 · 07:00) on first launch
- [ ] Trigger → Toggle → Nightlight opens the same TUI
- [ ] Enable from the TUI → user's previous `hyprsunset.conf` is copied to `~/.local/state/omarchy/hyprsunset.preauto.conf`; live config is replaced with managed content; autostart line is added; `hyprsunset` starts
- [ ] Change intensity / start / end while enabled → `hyprsunset.conf` re-renders with new values
- [ ] Disable → previous `hyprsunset.conf` is restored from the backup, backup is removed, autostart line stripped, `hyprsunset` killed
- [ ] Re-enable preserves prior settings from the state file and captures a fresh backup
- [ ] Disable with no backup file (e.g. wiped state) falls back to the Omarchy default `hyprsunset.conf`
- [ ] Invalid input (temp outside 1000–6500, malformed time) is rejected with a flash error in the TUI / non-zero exit in the CLI
- [ ] Reboot with schedule enabled → `hyprsunset` autostarts and schedule is active
- [ ] `omarchy commands` lists the new routes; `bash test/omarchy-cli-test.sh` still green

author: james-miller-93
body:
## Summary

Adds version-aware npm IoC detection for compromised releases of otherwise legitimate packages. This complements the existing name-only malicious package list, which works well for typosquats and packages that are malicious in their entirety, but is too blunt for incidents like debug@4.4.2, chalk@5.6.1, @bitwarden/cli@2026.4.0, and the malicious Nx releases, where only specific versions are compromised.

## Why

Recent npm supply-chain incidents typically compromise a legitimate package for one version or a small set of versions. Flagging by package name alone would produce high-impact false positives for common packages such as debug, chalk, and nx. This change adds exact resolved-version matching so vsix-audit can identify known-bad releases without treating every version of those packages as malicious.
  
## Implementation

  - Adds zoo/iocs/malicious-npm-versions.json with structured advisory metadata per entry:
    - package name
    - exact affected versions
    - advisory ID, campaign, reason
    - references
  - Extends ZooData and the zoo loader to expose versioned npm advisories. If the file is absent, the loader
  falls back to an empty set, so the feature degrades gracefully rather than erroring.
  - Adds a new MALICIOUS_NPM_PACKAGE_VERSION finding (critical) emitted from package analysis.
  - Extracts resolved/bundled package evidence from:
    - the packages map of a lockfile (package-lock.json / npm-shrinkwrap.json, lockfile v2/v3 layout)
    - the recursive dependencies tree of a lockfile (v1 layout)
    - bundled node_modules/*/package.json manifests inside the VSIX
    - Note: the parser reads whichever of these keys is present rather than branching on lockfileVersion.
  - Emits a low-severity PARSE_FAILURE_PACKAGE_LOCK finding when a lockfile cannot be parsed; version-aware
  checks for that file are then skipped.

## Behavior and scope
  
A few decisions worth knowing before reviewing:

  - Matching is exact literal string comparison of the resolved version against affectedVersions — not
  semver-aware. There is no range matching or version normalization.
  - Dev-only lockfile entries are skipped unless the package is actually bundled in the VSIX. A bundled
  node_modules/*/package.json overrides this and is treated as authoritative evidence.
  - One finding per unique package@version. Evidence is deduplicated by name@version, and bundled-module
  evidence is preferred over lockfile evidence, so a package present in both a lockfile and bundled
  node_modules yields a single finding citing the bundled file.
  - Version-aware checks run only when the extension's root package.json is present and parseable. They are
  part of the existing package.json-gated dependency checks; a missing or malformed root package.json skips
  them (alongside typosquatting and lifecycle-script checks), consistent with current behavior.

## What to review
  
The code surface is small. The content most worth scrutiny is the IoC data in zoo/iocs/malicious-npm-versions.json — the affected version lists and advisory identifiers. Each entry carries references for verification. Note that some identifiers are not GHSA IDs (@bitwarden/cli uses Bitwarden-2026-04-22; the @nx/key and @nx/enterprise-cloud entries cover 3.2.0), since no GHSA was available for those at the time.

## Validation

  - Added unit coverage for: exact malicious-version matches, patched-version non-matches, scoped packages,
  dev-only lockfile handling, bundled dependency manifests, package-lock v1 traversal, malformed lockfiles,
  and integration through checkPackage.
  - npm run check (typecheck + lint + test) — passes.
  - npm run build — passes.

author: k13-projects
body:
## Summary

Two generation cleanup fixes from the alt-line engine smoke-test (the engine itself worked — 7 clean deep-line locks at 85–90%).

- **Supersede stale picks**: when the engine regenerates a game, prior pending picks for that game not in the new set are voided. Today's game had 7 new picks stranded among **44 stale** main-line picks. Guarded to only touch games that produced ≥1 fresh pick.
- **Fix duplicate Bet of the Day**: reset `is_bet_of_the_day` by `game_id` instead of a `generated_at` window — picks generated yesterday for today's game escaped the reset and kept a stale BotD flag.

Pending → void is a no-op on the engine score ledger.

body:
## Summary

P1 第 1 個 PR（共 3 個拆）：落地 spec 02 §1 的 4 個 Haiku 4.5 judge、全部 sit on top of `_base.js`（P0 已 ship）。每個 judge prompt 含 **Damon 體系判斷標準**（不是泛用 sentiment / depth judge）。

| Judge | A 編號 | Damon 校準 | 消費端 |
|---|---|---|---|
| sensory-detail | A1 | 時/地/人/動作 markers + self-evidence + derived | E1c / E2 door 4 / E3 cascade / CP1 Turn 1+2 |
| depth-signal | A4 | worth-fiction 深度（「我不夠好」）+ body metaphor | E3_opening_branch_router 分支 C / E3_deep_signal_detector |
| containment-logic | A5 | 存在依賴測試 + Linear Thinking Error | E3_top1_determination Step 5 / E3_cascade_down |
| takeaway-sentiment | A6 | A001「無力」= negative（不是 neutral） | E4_takeaway_planter / finalize-day.js |

## sensory-detail.js 3-dim output（spec 02 §1）

```json
{
  "has_time_marker": boolean,
  "has_location_marker": boolean,
  "has_person_marker": boolean,
  "has_action_marker": boolean,
  "sensory_detail_score": 0-4,
  "evidence_attribution": "self" | "others" | "ambiguous",
  "derived_from_another_value": boolean
}
```

消費端各取所需子集：E1c/E2/E3 只看 dim 1（score >= 2）；CP1 Turn 1 P7 + dim 2；CP1 Turn 2 P20 + dim 3。`isStrictClearance()` helper 提供 spec 02 strict gate（全 3 dim 通過）。

## 共用 helper

- `_json.js` 內 `extractJSON()`：handle markdown fence + explanation text + nested object + 字串內 brace
- `_json.js` 內 `assertShape()`：欄位存在 + 型別 + enum 嚴格驗證

## 測試（121/121 pass，node:test 內建、無新 dep）

```
$ npm test
ℹ tests 121
ℹ pass 121
ℹ fail 0
```

| File | tests |
|---|---|
| _json.test.js | 21 |
| sensory-detail.test.js | 15 |
| depth-signal.test.js | 13 |
| containment-logic.test.js | 16 |
| takeaway-sentiment.test.js | 11 |
| **新增小計** | **76** |
| 既有（state-manager / day-boundary / _base） | 48 |

⭐ 關鍵 test：
- `SYSTEM_PROMPT covers A001 無力 = negative calibration`（takeaway-sentiment）
- `SYSTEM_PROMPT covers Damon 3 dimensions`（sensory-detail）
- `SYSTEM_PROMPT covers Damon containment vs linear thinking distinction`（containment-logic）
- `judge: linear thinking error detected`（containment-logic、A001-style edge case）
- `isStrictClearance` 4 個 cases（spec 02 §1 strict gate）

## 範圍邊界

- ✅ P1 PR-3a：4 judges + JSON helper + tests
- ❌ 未含：requires-typing / cumulative-score / handoff-escalation（PR-3b）/ phase-machine（PR-3b）/ detector registry（PR-3c）
- ❌ 未含 P0 deep_signal_flags explicit init 改動（你 5/21 決策、放在 PR-3b 一起改）

## Test plan

- [ ] Patrick review parse() schema validation 嚴謹度
- [ ] 確認 `npm test` 121/121 pass

author: dayglojesus
body:
## Summary

Post-migration catalogue cleanup so installs resolve against `textmatelives` and the bundle-side `main` rename. Two commits:

**1. Update fork references: `textmatelives` org and `main` branch** (`d5f2ec3`)

- Catalogue URLs (`DefaultBundles.plist`, `AvailableBundles.plist`, `MandatoryBundles.h`): `github.com/dayglojesus` → `github.com/textmatelives`.
- Catalogue `ref` values in plists: `remove-legacy-ruby` / `python3-port` / `arm64-binaries` → `main`, matching the bundle-side rename.
- `MandatoryBundles.h` `// branch:` comments updated; pinned SHAs unchanged (still reachable from each bundle's `main`).
- `CLAUDE.md`, `bin/build_filetype_index.rb`, `bin/reset_bundles.sh`, `bin/generate_available_bundles.rb`: doc and local-dev-path references updated to `textmatelives`.

**2. Bundles catalogue: stale `ref=master` → `ref=main`** (`e6677d1a`)

The first pass only touched the explicit fork-branch refs. But the bundle-side cleanup mass-renamed `master` → `main` across all 157 textmatelives bundles, leaving 80 catalogue entries pointing at a branch that no longer exists. App `BundleFetcher` 404'd silently — fresh-install test attempted 153 entries and 80 failed with no log signal. Sweeps both plists:

```
<key>ref</key><string>master</string>  →  <key>ref</key><string>main</string>
```

## Verification

CI green. Local fresh-build verified the embedded plists:

| Plist | stale `master` refs | `main` refs | `dayglojesus` URLs | `textmatelives` URLs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DefaultBundles.plist | 0 | 39 | 0 | 39 |
| AvailableBundles.plist | 0 | 110 | 0 | 110 |

## Test plan

- [x] CI (`build-test`) green on `e6677d1a`.
- [x] Local from-scratch rebuild after full TextMate state scrub (prefs, caches, Application Support, HTTPStorages, WebKit).
- [x] Embedded catalogue plists show 0 stale refs, 0 dayglojesus URLs.
- [ ] Post-merge: launch fresh app and confirm bundle installs complete without silent 404s.

body:
## Why

[`/ja/videos/v062/`](https://sgai.md/ja/videos/v062/) and several others rendered the dev-targeted "No readable content for this video yet. Run \`npm run fetch:video-transcripts\` to refresh." message in production.

Root cause: 5 videos (v022, v040, v044, v061, v062) were missing entirely from \`src/data/video-transcripts.ts\`. 3 because YouTube never produced any captions and \`emit\` silently filtered them via \`.filter((r) => r.paragraphs.length > 0)\`, 2 because they were added post-cron. The page logic \`!digest && transcriptParagraphs.length === 0\` then fell back to the dev message — same fallback regardless of locale, no distinction between "captions truly unavailable" and "developer hasn't run fetch yet."

Also discovered while building the eval: v024 had \`paragraphsJa\` with 5 entries against a 1-paragraph \`paragraphs\` / \`paragraphsEn\` — a quieter drift class my new \`paragraph-count-mismatch\` rule catches.

## Structural changes

1. **New eval \`scripts/evals/video-transcript-coverage/check.ts\`**
   - Every videos.ts entry must have a videoTranscripts record (or explicit \`source: 'unavailable'\` placeholder)
   - \`paragraphs\` / \`paragraphsEn\` / \`paragraphsJa\` triple-aligned (if any is non-empty, all must be)
   - \`digest\` / \`digestEn\` / \`digestJa\` triple-aligned
   - Paragraph counts match across locales
   - zh/ja fields actually contain CJK
   - Wired into PR diff mode (CI) + weekly cron historical sweep + \`npm run check\`

2. **\`scripts/videos/fetch-transcripts.ts\` hardened**
   - \`emit\` no longer filters unavailable records — emits explicit placeholder so the page can render a friendly "captions unavailable" UX
   - Per-record merge preserves \`paragraphsJa\` / \`digest*\` on refetch (was: full overwrite that risked wiping the ja translation)
   - Refuses to downgrade an existing rich record to \`unavailable\` on transient yt-dlp failure
   - Auto-chains en→zh→ja translation post-emit; single \`npm run fetch:video-transcripts -- --ids=…\` reaches triple-aligned state. \`--no-translate\` / \`--emit-only\` opt-out (also prevents recursion since translate-transcripts.ts internally calls fetch --emit-only)

3. **Page UX — three-language fallback distinction**
   - \`src/pages/{videos,[lang]/videos}/[id].astro\` now branches on \`transcript?.source === 'unavailable'\` to show a localized "this video has no captions on YouTube" message (zh / en / ja) instead of the dev-targeted "run npm run …" message
   - Drops a 2-locale ternary; source-i18n baseline shrinks by 2

## Data backfill (in this commit)

| ID | Why missing | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| v022 | zaobaosg — no captions | source:'unavailable' placeholder |
| v040 | YTL PowerSeraya — no captions | source:'unavailable' placeholder |
| v044 | AIAP video — no captions | source:'unavailable' placeholder |
| v024 | paragraphsJa drifted to 5 vs 1 | joined ja into 1 to match en/zh |

## Pending on same branch (separate commit incoming)

- v061 / v062: AI Engineer Singapore Day 1 / Day 2 (8h livestreams each). YouTube *does* serve auto-captions; en→zh→ja translation is running locally and will land as a separate commit. PR-time diff-mode CI passes since neither id is newly added on this branch; \`npm run check:video-transcripts:full\` flags them until backfill lands.

## Test plan

- [x] \`npm run check\` (includes diff-mode \`check:video-transcripts\`)
- [x] \`npm run eval:source-i18n\` — baseline re-snapshotted (506 → 503)
- [x] Manual: \`curl /videos/v022/\` (en), \`/zh/videos/v022/\`, \`/ja/videos/v022/\` — all render the new localized "captions unavailable" message
- [x] Manual: \`curl /ja/videos/v055/\` — triple-aligned video still renders the readable transcript section in Japanese
- [x] \`fetch-transcripts.ts --emit-only\` on full set — \`paragraphsJa\` of existing records (e.g. v055) preserved through re-emit (merge-not-overwrite)
- [ ] After v061 / v062 backfill: \`npm run check:video-transcripts:full\` exits 0

## What changed

Closes #71

- **`spec/schema.go` + `spec/secrets.go`**: Added `api_key` and `api_key_secret_type` fields to `RegistryConfig`; new `ResolveSecret()` resolves credentials from env var, file, or inline value. `registry.go` now passes the resolved key to the server client for all server-mode commands.
- **`registry/server/server.go` + `handlers.go`**: Extended `Store` interface with API key management (`CountAPIKeys`, `CreateAPIKey`, `ListAPIKeys`, `RevokeAPIKey`) and webhook admin (`ListWebhooksAdmin`, `DeleteWebhook`) methods with full SQL implementations. Added new REST endpoints: `GET /v1/health`, `POST /v1/admin/keys` (bootstrap-aware), `GET /v1/admin/keys`, `DELETE /v1/admin/keys/{id}`, `GET /v1/webhooks`, `DELETE /v1/webhooks/{id}`. Updated `GET /v1/audit` to accept `limit`, `since`, `until`, `entity`, and `user` query params. Added `parseExtendedDuration` supporting `90d`/`1y` syntax for key expiry.
- **`registry/server/client/client.go`**: Added `Status`, `CreateAPIKey`, `ListAPIKeys`, `RevokeAPIKey`, `RegisterWebhook`, `ListWebhooksAdmin`, `RemoveWebhook`, and `ListAuditLog` methods; added matching `APIKeyRecord`, `CreatedAPIKey`, `WebhookRecord`, `AuditEntry`, and `StatusResponse` types. `decode` now handles HTTP 204 No Content.
- **`cmd/event-spec/publish.go`, `admin.go`, `admin_status.go`, `admin_keys.go`, `admin_audit.go`, `admin_webhooks.go`**: Full CLI implementation for `event-spec publish` (with `--dry-run`) and the `event-spec admin` subcommand tree; all commands read credentials from workspace config via `openAdminClient()`.

## How to test

```bash
# Build
go build ./cmd/event-spec

# Start a server (separate terminal)
event-spec serve --db file:./test.db

# Bootstrap first admin key (no auth required on zero-key server)
event-spec admin keys create --role admin --name ci-key

# Export the key, then set in event-spec.yaml:
#   registry.api_key: "${EVENT_SPEC_API_KEY}"
#   registry.api_key_secret_type: env_var
export EVENT_SPEC_API_KEY=<key from above>

# Check server health
event-spec admin status

# Publish a spec

event-spec publish --dry-run specs/ecommerce/product_viewed/1-0-0.yaml

# List/revoke keys
event-spec admin keys list
event-spec admin keys revoke <id>

# Audit log
event-spec admin audit --limit 10 --format json

# Webhooks
event-spec admin webhooks add https://example.com/hook
event-spec admin webhooks list
event-spec admin webhooks remove <id>

# Automated tests
go test ./...
```

author: conxlgtm
body:
## Summary

- Projects graphics-preview capabilities from the live surface runtime so `WaylandGraphicsPreview` can report display advertisements, pending optional metadata support, and runtime fallback state from the same capability snapshot used by window surfaces.
- Preserves the advertised dmabuf protocol version after surface-specific feedback is installed, so a compositor advertised as v6 still projects as v6 instead of being reduced to the feedback minimum.
- Expands `GPUPreviewSmokeClient` into a pasteable runtime-path report covering display, compositor, window result, dmabuf, GBM, EGL, explicit sync, pacing, metadata, presentation feedback, and backing/fallback facts.
- Adds live graphics-preview fact tests that run against a compositor without requiring GPU hardware, plus optional render-node reporting and managed software fallback submission coverage.
- Adds a renderer-neutral managed preview submission API under `WaylandGraphicsPreview` with configuration policies, a managed window backing, single-use frame leases, clear-frame submission, cancellation, typed metadata values, and machine-matchable preview errors.
- Rejects unsupported managed preview policies before backing creation, preserves default metadata submission under `.preferAvailable`, and reports unimplemented managed GPU submission as `managedGPUSubmissionUnavailable` instead of claiming GBM was probed.
- Models managed frame lease state as open, submitting, or closed so close/submission interleavings have an explicit public lifecycle result.
- Rechecks backing closure after actor suspension points in `nextFrame()` and `submit()`, so `backingClosed` wins after `WaylandGraphicsWindowBacking.close()` even when close interleaves with window checks or submission effects.
- Moves failed submissions from `submitting` back to an open state without marking the frame submitted, so callers can retry or receive the documented terminal error.
- Checks active lease identity before frame payload validation so stale or wrong leases report `frameLeaseConsumed` instead of payload-specific errors.
- Replaces string-only submission failures with `submissionFailed(WaylandGraphicsSubmissionFailure)`, preserving window lifecycle transitions, window errors, display errors, client errors, unexpected failure descriptions, submission operation, and submission stage as typed values.
- Changes the executor read-failure regression test to wait on a pipe signal from the owner thread and read probe state only after shutdown, avoiding the TSan Swift access race from polling shared test state.
- Adds deterministic tests for managed policy validation, lease/cancel/submit transitions, in-flight submission rejection, failed submission recovery, stale lease errors, closed-window error mapping, non-closed submission failure mapping, dmabuf surface-feedback projection, and the surface capability snapshot bridge into public graphics capabilities.
- Adds headless live tests that prove `backing.close()` makes `nextFrame()`, active lease submission, close-during-next-frame, and close-during-submit paths throw `backingClosed`; direct window closure still reports `windowClosed`; and a typed submission-effect failure allows a later clear-frame retry.
- Extends the external graphics preview client tests so downstream packages compile against capability queries, runtime-path queries, backing decisions, managed backing creation, frame leases, clear-frame submission types, structured submission failures, and error values.
- Updates graphics-preview documentation, the compositor matrix, release guidance, roadmap, README, and public API baseline to describe the new evidence flow and preview submission boundary.

## Why

- The graphics preview product needs compositor evidence that distinguishes registry advertisement from actual usable runtime paths before it can be treated as credible preview surface area.
- Surface feedback is a surface-scoped dmabuf state, not a downgrade of the negotiated global version. Keeping the advertised version prevents callers from disabling paths that the compositor actually supports.
- Smoke output should be directly useful for maintaining `docs/compositor-matrix.md`, including optional protocol absence, advertised-but-unusable paths, and software fallback reasons.
- The preview product was previously mostly descriptive. The managed clear-frame path adds the smallest useful effectful API without exposing raw Wayland, GBM, EGL, DRM, sync, or protocol handles.
- Managed preview policy values should not imply support that is not implemented, and runtime diagnostics should not convert an unimplemented public GPU submission path into a false hardware or GBM failure.
- Closed backing and externally closed window are separate lifecycle states; public operations need stable `backingClosed` and `windowClosed` errors so clients can recover without parsing strings.
- Actor methods can resume after other actor operations run. The backing lifecycle is checked after those suspension points so close/submission races do not return stale success or the wrong terminal error.
- Submission failures must not leave the backing in an implicit in-flight state. A failed first submission remains a first-frame path on retry, while failures after a submitted frame preserve redraw sequencing.
- Non-closed submission failures need machine-readable cause, operation, and stage data so callers can distinguish retryable lifecycle failures, display failures, window failures, and unexpected infrastructure failures.
- Lease validity is the outer invariant for submission. Dead leases should always report lease consumption before frame metadata is inspected.
- The executor test needed a synchronization point that does not race the owner thread under ThreadSanitizer.
- The API remains renderer-neutral: it does not add a scene graph, widget layer, renderer abstraction, shader interface, or public color-management image-description surface.
- GPU availability remains capability-gated. Headless Weston and non-GPU environments can still validate projection and software fallback behavior instead of failing ordinary preview checks.

## Validation

- `make lint`
- `make test-tsan`
- `bash ./scripts/safety/verify-unsafe-allowlist.sh`
- `./scripts/ci/verify-target-imports.sh`
- `./scripts/ci/verify-public-api-audit.sh`
- `./scripts/ci/test-graphics-preview-client.sh`
- `./scripts/dev/swift.sh build --disable-index-store -Xswiftc -strict-concurrency=complete -Xswiftc -warn-concurrency`
- `./scripts/dev/swift.sh test --filter 'WaylandGraphicsPreview|SurfaceRuntimeTests|WaylandThreadExecutorTests/readEventFailureDoesNotCancelResolvedReadIntent'`
- `git diff --check`
- `git diff --check main...HEAD`

body:
## Summary

- **4 utility agents promoted off `model: inherit` to explicit AgDR-0050 § Axis 2 baselines**: Rex (`code-reviewer.md`) inherit → opus per Axis 2 line 50 (PR diff review + handbook reasoning depth); Munir (`dependency-auditor.md`) inherit → sonnet per line 63 (pattern-matching across package files); Tariq (`pr-manager.md`) inherit → sonnet per line 64 (tool-call-heavy + PR body narrative quality); Idris (`ticket-manager.md`) inherit → sonnet per line 65 (schema-conforming output + interactive interview). Hakim was already promoted to opus in PR #360 as part of the Hatim→Hakim consolidation, completing the 5/5 utility-agent matrix.
- **Each frontmatter carries the `# routing-config:override` escape-hatch comment** inside the YAML frontmatter so `block-agent-routing-drift.sh` accepts the intentional inherit→<model> framework-default change rather than blocking it as adopter-leak. The comment names the agent, the AgDR line number, and the rationale — visible + auditable per AgDR-0040's escape-hatch convention. Each commit landed cleanly through the drift guard on the first attempt (no PR-3-style "wrong comment style" retry).
- **`test_agent_wrap_shape.sh` extended with a `UTILITY_AGENTS` array and a new "Invariant 4b" block** that asserts each utility agent has (a) explicit `model:` matching Axis 2, (b) correct `persona_name`, and (c) the escape-hatch comment in YAML frontmatter. Locks in the post-PR-4 baselines so a future revert-to-inherit trips the test instead of silently slipping. Bonus fix: the new awk uses POSIX `[[:space:]]` / `[^[:space:]]` instead of `\S` — `\S` isn't portable across awk implementations (macOS BSD awk silently treated it as a literal, masking the regex bug). Other awk blocks in the test file already use POSIX classes, so this is a one-time gotcha that's now closed.
- **`test_agent_routing_sync_and_drift.sh` extended with a ticket-manager fixture in `make_fork` + new CASE 8** that exercises a utility-agent override (ticket-manager sonnet → opus). Proves the routing-sync mechanism doesn't distinguish utility from role-derived agents — same hook, same rewrite, same snapshot path. 8/8 cases PASS.

## Testing

- [x] `bash .claude/agents/tests/test_agent_wrap_shape.sh` — PASS at 13 ROLE_AGENTS + 5 UTILITY_AGENTS + 19 ROLE_CLASSES.
- [x] `bash .claude/hooks/tests/test_agent_routing_sync_and_drift.sh` — PASS at 8/8 cases (case 8 new this PR).
- [x] Drift guard accepted both commits (`0961572` model changes + `637f2d9` test extensions) without blocking — verifies the escape-hatch comment placement is correct on all 4 utility files.
- [ ] Manual smoke (operator, post-merge): start a fresh session, observe Rex's review tone for any visible-model-bump effect on code-reviewer output quality. Not blocking this merge.
- [ ] Manual smoke (operator, post-merge): apply an `agent-routing.yaml` override (e.g. `ticket-manager: model: opus`) and confirm SessionStart sync rewrites `.claude/agents/ticket-manager.md`'s `model:` to `opus`; `git checkout` then restores `sonnet`. Not blocking.

## Glossary

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| **UTILITY_AGENTS array** | New companion to `ROLE_AGENTS` in `test_agent_wrap_shape.sh`. Format `"<slug>:<expected_model>:<expected_persona_name>"`. Locks in AgDR-0050 § Axis 2 baselines for the 5 utility agents (Rex, Hakim, Munir, Tariq, Idris). Different from `ROLE_AGENTS` because utility agents don't have a canonical `roles/<dept>/<slug>.md` file — they're framework primitives, not role-derived personas. |
| **`# routing-config:override <reason>` escape hatch** | YAML-frontmatter comment recognised by `block-agent-routing-drift.sh` (regex `^[[:space:]]*#[[:space:]]*routing-config:override[[:space:]]+\S`). Used for intentional framework-default changes — e.g. this PR's 4 inherit→<model> bumps. The comment ships with the PR and makes the deliberate change visible. HTML `<!-- -->` form does NOT match — only the `#`-prefixed YAML comment form does (footgun from PR #360 is now documented in the test). |
| **Axis 2 baseline vs adopter override** | AgDR-0050 § Axis 2 ships per-agent default models in the framework (this PR makes the utility-agent defaults explicit). Adopters override per-agent via `agent-routing.yaml` in their private portfolio repo (or gitignored single-fork). The SessionStart sync hook (`apply-agent-routing.sh`, from #357) rewrites the agent file's `model:` line at session start; the drift guard prevents that rewrite from leaking into a commit. |
| **POSIX awk vs `\S`** | macOS BSD `awk` and other POSIX-strict implementations don't support `\S` (the Perl-style non-whitespace shorthand). They silently treat `\S` as a literal "S" character. The new test code uses `[^[:space:]]` instead — same semantics, portable across all awk implementations. |

Refs #347 (4/5 PRs now landed; PR 5 — role-trigger integration — is the last)
Refs #348 (Idris is one of three candidates for the local-routing feasibility spike)

## Note for the next reviewer

This PR keeps strictly to scope: 4 frontmatter promotions + 2 test extensions. No drive-by cleanups, no doc rewrites, no CLAUDE.md / site / AGENTS.md changes (agent count is unchanged — only model values change). Rex's 5 non-blocking suggestions on PR #360 (consolidation-exception test, stale Hatim in test file comment, AgDR-0018 lines 51+92 doc-debt, prose inaccuracy at security-reviewer.md:17, HTML-comment drift-guard footgun docs) are intentionally NOT included in this PR — they're tracked as follow-ups for a Wave-3 cleanup PR or discrete chore tickets.

author: benhillis
body:
## Summary

Minimal cherry-pick of #40612 for the 2.7 release branch.

Fixes an `Exec format error` bug where Windows interop breaks in all running distros when a peer distro with systemd shuts down.

## Root Cause

`/proc` is mounted with `MS_SHARED`, so `binfmt_misc` inherits shared mount propagation. When a peer distro's systemd shuts down and unmounts `binfmt_misc` in its namespace, the unmount propagates back through the shared peer group to init's namespace, wiping ALL registrations globally.

## Fix

One additional `mount()` call with `MS_PRIVATE` immediately after mounting binfmt_misc. This is the minimal version — the master branch PR also extends `UtilMount` to handle propagation flags generically.

## PR Checklist

- [x] Builds cleanly
- [x] Includes regression test (`InteropSurvivesPeerDistroShutdown`)
- [x] Passes clang-format

Fixes #13885

author: tsiditam
body:
## Summary

Brings `src/components/AuthScreen.jsx` onto the v3 token surface that the rest of the app moved to in PR #193. Two real fixes, not just visual polish:

### 1. Theme break (functional bug)

Pre-v3 AuthScreen had hardcoded hex constants at the top of the file:

```js
const BG = '#07080C'
const CARD = '#111318'
const BORDER = '#1C1E26'
const ACCENT = '#22D3EE'
const TEXT = '#ECEEF2'
const SUB = '#8B93A5'
const DIM = '#6B7380'
```

These ignored the light/dark toggle that v3.2 (commit `1036997`) added to the rest of the app. A user who flipped to light mode would see the entire app in light **except the auth flow**, which stayed permanently dark.

Routed through theme-aware V3 tokens that resolve to CSS custom properties (`var(--bg)` / `var(--card)` / `var(--border)` / `var(--text)` / `var(--sub)` / `var(--dim)`) defined in `index.html`.

### 2. Three competing button treatments in one flow

| Mode | Pre-v3 fill | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Sign In | `var(--accent-fill)` (cyan) | V3.btnPrimary |
| Create Account | `linear-gradient(135deg, #059669, #22C55E)` (green) | V3.btnPrimary |
| Send Reset Link | `linear-gradient(135deg, #0891B2, #22D3EE)` (darker-cyan) | V3.btnPrimary |

The green CTA was a "GO!"-style consumer affordance and the cyan gradient was redundant with the accent. v3 standardizes on a single accent fill across modals, primary actions, and field-app CTAs — three different button styles in the auth flow broke that consistency.

Collapsed to a single `V3.btnPrimary` with a size override (`width:100%`, `padding:16px 0`, `fontSize:17`, `minHeight:54`, `borderRadius:14`) so the larger field-tap target the auth context warrants is preserved while inheriting the rest of `btnPrimary`'s spec.

## Secondary fixes (co-located)

- Brand wordmark → `V3.T.display` (was hand-tuned 36/800)
- Wrapper `fontFamily` was malformed: `"'inherit', system-ui"` treats `inherit` as a quoted font name. Replaced with bare `'inherit'` which actually inherits from the body's Inter stack.
- Subtitle / supporting copy → `V3.T.bodyDim` tokens
- Footer → `V3.T.micro` shape with overrides back to sentence case for legal-fine-print register
- `input::placeholder` in `<style>` block: `#525A6A` → `var(--dim)` so placeholders respect the theme too

## What was deliberately *not* changed

- All auth logic (`handleLogin` / `handleRegister` / `handleForgot` / `handleGoogleSignIn`), Supabase calls, `trackEvent` calls, ToS gate
- Google sign-in button styling — preserved per Google's brand requirements for "Sign in with Google" affordances
- Engine, scoring, calibration gating, narrative, billing
- `I` icon import is still in place (unused pre-existing dead import; left per "no drive-by refactors")

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run build` — 11.68s, only pre-existing dynamic-import warnings
- [x] `npm test` — 1048 pass / 5 skipped / 0 fail (86 test files)
- [x] `npm run accept:prod-ready` — 34/34 pass
