author: philsphicas
body:
PR4 of the test-restructuring workstream. Closes the workstream
opened by PR1–PR3.

The shared e2e scenario harness gains a Performance suite that runs
as testing.T (alongside the existing testing.B benchmarks in
bench.go). Two connect-latency scenarios assert per-backend
thresholds; a third short-session scenario logs per-iteration
timings as an observation-only baseline that a follow-up will
promote to a gate once CI history establishes a realistic
ceiling.

Changes:

- `e2escenarios.Backend` gains `ConnectLatencyThreshold() time.Duration`.
  Both backend implementations (`MockBackend` and `azureBackend`)
  return 3 s — generous to absorb CI scheduling noise, tight enough
  to catch regressions on the order of seconds. Differentiating
  per-cell (e.g. SAS vs Entra) is straightforward when data
  justifies it but not done now.
- New `internal/testharness/e2escenarios/performance.go` contains
  `RunPerformanceScenarios` plus the three scenario functions
  (`ConnectLatency_Serial_PortForward`,
  `ConnectLatency_Serial_SOCKS5`, `ShortSession_Serial`) and a
  shared `timeOneConnect` helper. Reuses `benchDial`, `writeFull`,
  `StartPlainEcho`, and `AssertNoLeaks` from the existing harness.
- `RunAllScenarios` calls `RunPerformanceScenarios` last in each
  cell, so the new suite runs against every (backend, auth) cell
  in CI: `TestE2E_Mock/<scenario>` in the mockrelay test job and
  `TestE2E_Azure/<auth>/<scenario>` in the e2e workflow.
- Each ConnectLatency iteration's wall time is logged via
  `t.Logf`, so a threshold failure makes the offending iteration
  obvious in CI output without needing per-iteration metric
  scraping.

CI integration: no new workflow file. The existing `test` job
(mockrelay) and `e2e` workflow (Azure) already fail on test
failure; threshold violations now surface there as plain
sub-test failures (rendered paths `TestE2E_Mock/<scenario>` and
`TestE2E_Azure/<auth>/<scenario>`, consistent with the existing
Core/Topology/Reliability/Observability scenarios — no
`Performance/` wrapper layer).

author: technooptics
body:
## Summary
**The actual root cause of the persistent Maps 503.** `next.config.ts` sets a strict Content-Security-Policy. `script-src` listed Stripe, Plaid, and Vercel — but **not** `maps.googleapis.com`. Chrome was blocking the Maps script load before the request ever reached Google, and surfacing the block as a generic 503 in the network panel.

Proof: a server-side `curl` with the exact same `Referer`/`Origin` headers as the browser returned **HTTP 200** + real Maps JS. Only browser script-tag loads were 503'd, because only the browser enforces CSP.

We chased referrer restrictions → billing → API enablement → service workers → an HTTP-cache theory for hours before `curl -I` on the page showed the CSP header with `maps.googleapis.com` nowhere in `script-src`.

## CSP additions
```
script-src    + https://maps.googleapis.com
style-src     + https://fonts.googleapis.com     (Maps Roboto)
img-src       + https://maps.gstatic.com
              + https://maps.googleapis.com      (static map tiles)
              + https://streetviewpixels-pa.googleapis.com
font-src      + https://fonts.gstatic.com
connect-src   + https://maps.googleapis.com
              + https://maps.gstatic.com
```

Subdomain-specific (not wildcard `*.googleapis.com`) so the allow-list stays tight to surfaces the loader actually hits — Places search results, tile metadata, place autocomplete, etc.

## Test plan
- [ ] After Vercel rolls, `/mileage` and `/mileage/business` render actual Maps polylines
- [ ] Trip thumbnails on the trip list show
- [ ] Address autocomplete on Business Profile lights up
- [ ] Browser console no longer has "Refused to load the script" errors

## Follow-up
Re-lock the API key's website restrictions (currently set to "None" for the diagnostic) — once Maps is confirmed working, set it back to `https://taxottic.com` + `https://*.taxottic.com`.

## Summary

- `ClassifyHeadingTag` (extracted in #1573) walks a four-tier cascade: PART → h1, ITEM → h2, bold/uppercase/center-aligned → h3, italic → h4. A span often satisfies multiple tiers — an "Item 1." span rendered with `font-weight:bold` matches both h2 and h3 — and the contract requires the higher-precedence tier to win.
- Pins that cascade ordering. A refactor that reordered the branches (e.g. moving the cheaper bold predicate ahead of the ITEM check) would silently demote Item headings to h3.

- `tests/Equibles.UnitTests/Sec/Normalizers/HeadingConversionStepClassifyHeadingTagCascadePrecedenceTests.cs` — one `[Fact]` invoking the private `ClassifyHeadingTag` with a bold span whose text is "Item 1. Business" and asserting the returned tag is `"h2"`.

body:
## Before/After UX
Adds 6 new parameters to the Space v1.1 template to match the upstream workspace operator CRD (`workspace.jupyter.org/v1alpha1`):

- `--access-type` — who can connect to the workspace (Public/OwnerOnly)
- `--env` — environment variables for the workspace container
- `--access-strategy` — reference to a WorkspaceAccessStrategy
- `--pod-security-context` — pod-level security context
- `--container-security-context` — container-level security context
- `--init-containers` — init containers to run before the workspace container

Also adds an addon version compatibility warning: when users create/update a space, the CLI checks the installed `amazon-sagemaker-spaces` addon version via `eks:DescribeAddon` and warns if it's below the minimum required version (`0.1.6` for v1.1 template).

**Before:**

New workspace fields (accessType, env, etc.) were not available through the CLI or SDK. Users had no way to set them without manually crafting K8s YAML.

**After:**

```bash
hyp create hyp-space \
    --name my-space \
    --display-name "My Space" \
    --access-type OwnerOnly \
    --env '[{"name": "MY_VAR", "value": "hello"}]' \
    --access-strategy name=my-strategy,namespace=default \
    --pod-security-context '{"runAsNonRoot": true}' \
    --container-security-context '{"allowPrivilegeEscalation": false}' \
    --init-containers '[{"name": "setup", "image": "busybox", "command": ["sh", "-c", "echo init"]}]'
```

If the addon version is too old, users see:
```
UserWarning: The installed 'amazon-sagemaker-spaces' addon version is 0.1.1,
but this operation requires addon version >= 0.1.6. Some space parameters may
be ignored or rejected by the operator.
```

## How was this change tested?

- Unit tests: 135 space-related tests pass
- Manual CLI validation: confirmed all 6 parameters parse correctly and serialize to the expected K8s spec fields
- Addon version warning tested against a live v0.1.1 cluster in eu-north-1

## Are unit tests added?

Yes - 14 new tests added to `test/unit_tests/test_space_utils.py` covering `_parse_version`, `get_spaces_addon_version`, and `warn_if_addon_version_incompatible`.

## Are integration tests added?

No - integration test not required for this change

## Reviewer Guidelines

‼️ **Merge Requirements**: PRs with failing integration tests cannot be merged without justification.

One of the following must be true:
- [x] All automated PR checks pass
- [ ] Failed tests include local run results/screenshots proving they work
- [ ] Changes are documentation-only

author: justinschier
body:
This PR was opened by the [Changesets release](https://github.com/changesets/action) GitHub action. When you're ready to do a release, you can merge this and the packages will be published to npm automatically. If you're not ready to do a release yet, that's fine, whenever you add more changesets to main, this PR will be updated.


# Releases
## @loworbitstudio/visor@1.3.0

### Minor Changes

-   4923865: VI-437 feat(sandbox): `visor sandbox init` accepts a `--from-html-prototype <path>` flag that imports a Phase 1.5 HTML prototype directory into the generated sandbox.

    The flag copies the prototype tree into the sandbox's `public/prototype/` directory and pairs each numerically-prefixed `screen-N-*.html` source file with the matching screen in the design-handoff manifest, in order. The generated `app/screens/[name]/page.tsx` swaps the operator-edit placeholder for an iframe that loads the paired HTML — so the sandbox boots with the real Phase 1.5 composition as the baseline, not a placeholder. `sandbox.json` records the source directory and the resolved screen-to-html map so downstream tooling can re-pull when the prototype changes.

    Unblocks the retro-fit pattern for pattern builds whose Phase 1.5 cleared before the sandbox CLI shipped (PL-1570, organization-management). Greenfield Phase 1.5 runs without an HTML prototype still hand-build sandbox compositions; the flag is opt-in.

-   17fd70e: VI-438 feat(sandbox): when `--from-html-prototype` is set, `visor sandbox init` now auto-discovers state-coverage screens — any `screen-N-*.html` files beyond the manifest's named-screen count are appended to the sandbox as `state-coverage` screens with predictable slugs derived from the filename suffix.

    Example: a prototype directory with `screen-1-list.html`, `screen-2-detail.html`, `screen-3-menus.html`, `screen-4-feedback.html`, `screen-5-edge-states.html` and a handoff that names two screens produces the two named routes plus `state-coverage-menus`, `state-coverage-feedback`, `state-coverage-edge-states`. Each state-coverage screen iframes its source HTML and is recorded in `sandbox.json` under `fromHtmlPrototype.stateCoverageScreens`, restoring per-state baseline coverage for the Phase 4 state-coverage diff gate. `ScreenEntry` gains an optional `kind: 'named' | 'state-coverage'` field that surfaces in the runtime `sandbox-manifest.ts` module so downstream tooling can filter by category.

-   560a929: VI-439 feat(sandbox): `visor sandbox init` now resolves brand themes from a private themes directory via `VISOR_THEMES_PRIVATE_PATH` env var, and accepts an explicit `--theme-file <path>` override.

    When the operator passes `--theme entr`, the CLI now walks a layered candidate list before falling back to the placeholder `globals.css`: `--theme-file <path>` wins if set, then `theme` interpreted as a direct path on disk, then `${VISOR_THEMES_PRIVATE_PATH}/themes/${theme}/theme.visor.yaml` when the env var is set (the canonical path for brand themes kept in `visor-themes-private`), then the existing `cwd/themes/${theme}.visor.yaml` and `cwd/custom-themes/${theme}.visor.yaml` fallback. If every candidate misses, the warning now lists the exact paths searched and prints the `npx visor theme apply` command the operator should run, instead of a generic "leaving placeholder" message that pointed at the wrong docs. Closes PL-1570 finding #3 — operators no longer have to run a second CLI invocation pointing at a private repo path after `init`.

-   149b6da: VI-441 feat(sandbox): `visor sandbox approve` now writes captures to `captures/pending/` by default and adds an `--approve` flag that promotes pending → approved after operator review.

    The capture flow becomes a three-state review loop — capture into pending (auto-diffed against any existing approved baseline), eyeball pending + diffs, promote with `--approve` once the captures look right. Approved captures are no longer overwritten on every run; the baseline only changes via a deliberate operator action.

    The legacy `--diff` flag becomes a deprecated no-op since the default capture already pixel-diffs against the approved baseline. Pending and diff directories are cleared at the start of each capture run so stale artifacts can't sneak into the review set.

    Fixes the auto-approve foot-gun from PL-1570 where first-run captures landed straight in `captures/approved/` (documentary chrome included) and required manual deletion to re-capture cleanly.

-   79cf443: VI-443 feat(sandbox): `visor sandbox init` now accepts `--strip-chrome` and `--strip-chrome-additional` to remove Phase 1.5 documentary chrome (state callouts, section headers, proto-nav, mint-styled annotation chips) from imported prototype HTML.

    Bare `--strip-chrome` enables stripping with a default selector list shipped by the CLI: `.state-callout`, `.state-section__header`, `.proto-nav`, `[data-documentary-chrome]`, and inline-styled mint chips matching `[style*="mint"]`. Pass `--strip-chrome "<selectors>"` (comma-separated) to REPLACE the defaults with a custom list, or `--strip-chrome-additional "<selectors>"` to MERGE extras with the chosen base. The stripper runs over each `.html` file copied into `public/prototype/` before the sandbox boots, so the resulting screen routes — and any Phase 4 captures — never render those labels. The resolved selector list is recorded in `sandbox.json` under `fromHtmlPrototype.stripChromeSelectors` for traceability. Closes PL-1570 post-mortem finding #7 (operators had been hand-rolling `strip-chrome.mjs` in each sandbox dir).

### Patch Changes

-   d4326c6: VI-440 fix(sandbox): generated `next.config.ts` now bakes `turbopack: { root: __dirname }` so Next.js doesn't misdetect the workspace root in multi-lockfile setups.

    When `visor sandbox init` scaffolded `.lo/sandbox/{name}/` inside a parent repo that already had its own `package-lock.json`, Next.js 16.2.6 chose the parent repo as the turbopack root and broke `@/lib/...` module resolution — routes 500'd on first request. The generated config now anchors `turbopack.root` to the sandbox dir via `fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)`, matching the manual workaround from PL-1570 finding #4.

-   d0b82fa: VI-442 fix(sandbox): the auto-generated `playwright.capture.mjs` now sets `deviceScaleFactor: 2` so retina captures look crisp on review.

    File size cost is roughly 4x but PNGs stay in the low-megabyte range. Pixel-diff is unaffected (compares per-pixel either way).

-   88f818f: VI-444 fix(sandbox): handoff entries declared "shipped" but missing from the Visor registry are now auto-reclassified as `compose-recipe` (consumer-side compositions of existing primitives) instead of being skipped with a warning.

    `visor sandbox init` now treats a Gate 3 miss on a `shipped` or `gap-inflight` entry as a signal that the handoff is describing a consumer-side composition. The entry's `status` is rewritten to `compose-recipe` and its `viTicket` is cleared before the scaffold runs, so both `sandbox.json` and `lib/sandbox-manifest.ts` surface the correct classification, no stub is generated, and `npx visor add` is not invoked for it. A softer informational warning (`'X' declared shipped in the handoff but absent from the registry — reclassified as compose-recipe`) is emitted in place of the prior skip warning. Mirrors PL-1570 finding #8.

author: mwerneburg
body:
## Summary

Two independent bugs in AI.cs that both produce a tight game loop when the AI controls Settlers:

**Bug 1 — validRoad condition is inverted**

tile.Road == true means a road *already exists*. So validRoad was only ever true on tiles that do not need a road built. BuildRoad() returns false on those tiles without touching MovesLeft, leaving the Settler stuck with MovesLeft=1 — and the game re-enqueues Turn.Move every tick.

Fix: !tile.Road && !tile.RailRoad (only true when a road is actually needed).

**Bug 2 — missing SkipTurn() after improvement orders**

FoundCity calls SkipTurn() before returning, but the three improvement cases (BuildRoad, BuildIrrigation, BuildMines) did not. Without it MovesLeft stays at 1 and Game.Update re-enqueues Turn.Move in the same tick the improvement order is enqueued, producing the same infinite loop.

Fix: call unit.SkipTurn() in each improvement case before returning.

## Test plan

- [ ] AI Settlers on a tile without a road no longer cause the game to hang
- [ ] AI Settlers correctly build roads, irrigation, and mines over multiple turns rather than looping on one turn
- [ ] AI Settlers on a tile that already has a road move on rather than attempting to rebuild it

Contributed from mwerneburg/CivOne where these were found and fixed during gameplay.

Closes #1216.

## Why

Today users must manually configure their AI agent to discover archigraph. This makes archigraph self-describing: any agent that reads `AGENTS.md` learns the dashboard URL, endpoint counts, and MCP config without any manual setup.

## How

**New package** `internal/agents/inject_map.go`:
- `InjectArchitectureMap(repoPath, stats)` — public entrypoint; resolves target file, renders block, upserts atomically
- `resolveTargetFile` — prefers `AGENTS.md` > `CLAUDE.md` > `GEMINI.md`; creates `AGENTS.md` if none exist
- `detectAITools` — scans for `.claude/` and `.cursor/` to tailor the MCP config hint
- `renderBlock` — builds the marker-wrapped Markdown; includes dashboard URL, entity/relationship/endpoint/flow/topology counts, timestamp, MCP JSON snippet
- `upsertFile` — atomic tmp+rename write; replaces existing block in-place or appends with separator

**Registry** (`internal/registry/registry.go`):
- Added `Features.AutoInjectAgentsMD bool` field (`json:"auto_inject_agents_md,omitempty"`) to `GroupConfig`; default `false` (opt-in only, no surprises)

**Daemon** (`cmd/archigraph/daemon.go`):
- Import `internal/agents` and `internal/graph`
- `daemonRebuildFunc` calls `agents.InjectArchitectureMap` per repo after a successful `Index()` when `cfg.Features.AutoInjectAgentsMD` is true
- `buildAgentsMapStats` reads the just-written `graph.fb` via `graph.LoadGraphFromDir` and assembles the `Stats` struct
- Failure is logged to stderr and never fails the rebuild (best-effort)

## Testing

16 unit tests in `internal/agents/inject_map_test.go`:
- Marker round-trip (start/end markers present)
- Group-scoped vs. no-group rendering
- Timestamp formatting
- Claude / Cursor hint detection
- Binary path in MCP snippet
- File creation, append-to-existing, idempotent in-place update
- `resolveTargetFile` preference order
- `detectAITools` coverage
- End-to-end `InjectArchitectureMap` (prefers CLAUDE.md, creates AGENTS.md)

All existing registry and CLI tests continue to pass.

## Default: off

`AutoInjectAgentsMD` defaults to `false`. Users opt in by adding `"auto_inject_agents_md": true` to `features` in their `<group>.fleet.json`.

### Motivation
- Improve locomotion realism and stability by reworking the creature physics and joint control limits.
- Adjust genetic algorithm ranges and fitness weighting to favor meaningful progress and penalize immobility.
- Add UI status reporting and controlled replay of best individuals to aid debugging and observation.

- Update gene specs in `ia/chromosome.js` and add new config options `bestReplaySteps` and `generationReplayPauseMs` in `ia/config.js` to tune replay and generation pacing.

## Summary

- Remove `ALLOWLIST` from `packages/boxel-cli/scripts/build-skills.ts` so cards in the pinned `cardstack/boxel-skills` tag are automatically packaged. Refactor the script around a pure `computeEmissionPlan(cards)` so the dedup logic is unit-testable, and add `updatePluginReadme()` which keeps a fenced auto-gen block in `plugin/README.md` in sync with the emission set.
- Curate via an explicit `EXCLUDED_IDS` set: the `boxel-environment` aggregator, all 9 of its references, and the two host-only top-level `env-*` leaves (`env-creating-and-editing-cards`, `env-sim-boxel-environment-guide`) are dropped. They teach the boxel **host AI assistant's** tool-call JSON shape (`{name, payload: {description, attributes}}`) and reference host-only commands (`switch-submode_dd88`, `set-active-llm_1887`, `patch-fields_3e67`) that don't exist in Claude Code / Codex. The exclusion is explicit (no `env-*` prefix rule), so future env-* upstream additions still ship by default.
- Manifest-based stale-dir sweep (addresses Codex P2 on `build-skills.ts`): each run records emitted IDs to `packages/boxel-cli/scripts/.boxel-skills-manifest.json`; on the next run, `plugin/skills/<id>` dirs that dropped out of the emission plan are deleted. CLI-authored skill dirs are never written by the script and so are never in the manifest — the sweep can't touch them.
- Soften the previous throw-on-unknown-`kind` to a warn-and-skip so a future additive card type upstream does not brick the build.

author: jmbattista
body:
Fixes #178.

Three predicates that were extracted into the **async** sense-I/O were carried over verbatim from the **synchronous** legate-loop `.mjs` (where calling them without `await` was correct). In the async world each one silently no-ops, dormant since the PR0 extraction. This is a focused, tested fix.

## Bugs fixed
1. **`discoverPrForSlice`** (`src/observe/sense-io.ts`) — filtered candidates on the raw `Promise` returned by `prMatchesSliceBranch` (always truthy), so every open PR "matched" and the newest one — possibly on the **wrong branch** — was adopted. Now `await Promise.all(...)`, then filter on the resolved booleans.
2. **`agentDeckSessionHoldsWorktree`** (`src/legate/loop/runtime.ts`) — did not `await listSessions()`, so `Array.isArray(Promise)` was always `false` → the function **always returned false** and a live session holding a worktree never blocked removal. Made `async`, awaited the list, and updated **both** callers (`tryRecoverBranchCollision`, `tryRecoverStrandedLeftover`).
3. **`tryAdoptOpenPr`** (`src/legate/loop/runtime.ts`) — picked candidates with `Array.find` over the un-awaited async `prMatchesSliceBranch` (same Promise-truthy bug), adopting the first candidate regardless of branch. Now resolves all predicates first, then picks the match.

## Test coverage for the now-active paths
- `src/observe/sense-io.test.ts` — a **newer wrong-branch PR is NOT adopted**; `discoverPrForSlice` picks the branch match (and returns `null` when nothing matches).
- `src/legate/loop/runtime.test.ts` — a **live session holding a worktree BLOCKS removal** (across `worktree_path`/`path`/`worktreePath` field variants; `{error}` → false), and `tryAdoptOpenPr` adopts the **matching-branch** PR rather than blindly the first candidate.

A small `__test` seam on the `@ts-nocheck` `runtime.ts` injects a fake `senseIo` so its dormant recovery paths get direct coverage without standing up Castra or git. Each test was confirmed to fail against the pre-fix code.

> **Base branch:** `feature/issues-herald` — the Herald PR0/PR1 work these files come from is not on `main` yet.

## Verification
`npm run typecheck && npm run build && npm test` — all green (692 tests).

author: shikiroot
body:
## Why
Recent changes after the earlier novel blacklist and search back-navigation work focused on a different set of usability problems in search and novel browsing. Search history interactions could stop responding, multi-tag queries were easy to mis-handle, the result filter area felt cramped, and some navigation entry points such as history taps and novel comment access had regressed.

At the same time, several novel surfaces presented metadata inconsistently, with dense layouts, awkward stat wrapping, and row structures that were harder to scan than they needed to be.

## What changed
- restored browse history taps and novel comment navigation
- streamlined the search result filter area and tightened the related result handling flow
- stabilized search history clearing, rendered history entries as plain queries, and anchored the clear confirmation sheet to the correct UI context
- fixed multi-tag search composition so space-separated input is handled as a normal text query while still producing the intended Pixiv tag search behavior
- removed a stale search suggestion callback that could interfere with the updated search flow
- unified the main novel list surfaces around the same stacked presentation, including a fixed title area, cleaner stat rendering, and more consistent thumbnail-to-text alignment
- introduced a shared row component for the updated novel information layout and applied it across ranking, detail-related lists, and author novel lists

## Result
- search interactions are more reliable: history items open correctly, clearing history behaves consistently, multi-tag queries are interpreted more naturally, and the filter area is easier to use on iPhone
- novel comment entry points work again
- novel list surfaces are easier to scan because title, author, tags, and stats now follow the same structure without awkward wrapping

## Testing
- passed GitHub Actions CI build on the fork branch for the final patch set
- manually verified search history interactions, multi-tag search behavior, filter changes, novel comment navigation, and the updated novel list/detail surfaces on iPhone

author: robmoore
body:
## Description

**Summary:**
Splits the monolithic transcription pipeline into a modular, serverless GCP Cloud Function transcription service and a separate audio normalization service under issue [GOO-455].

**Context & Motivation:**
Previously, audio normalization (heavy DSP/VAD logic running on Apache Beam) and audio transcription (I/O-bound GCP Speech-to-Text API calls) were coupled together. This caused severe container bloat, package size contention (e.g. TEN-VAD C++ binaries vs Google Cloud SDKs), and massive Cloud Function cold-start penalties. By splitting them into isolated, stateless microservices, we optimize memory consumption, enable independent scaling limits, and achieve pristine separation of concerns.

**Future Work / Out of Scope:**
Configuring Pub/Sub Dead Letter Queue (DLQ) retry and routing configurations via Terraform in GCF/PubSub infrastructure resources is out of scope for this PR and will be completed in a separate IaC pull request.

---

author: copilot
body:
This PR addresses the reported security/quality findings by tightening validation and outbound-call safety on public API routes, and by moving core frontend dependencies to patched ranges where possible. The goal is to eliminate exploitable input paths and reduce known advisory exposure without broad behavioral changes.

- **Dependency remediation**
  - Upgraded vulnerable frontend/security-relevant packages to patched versions (`next`, `postcss`, `autoprefixer`, `tailwindcss`) and refreshed lockfile.
  - Reduced advisory surface; remaining risk is limited to upstream/transitive constraints in the current `next` dependency chain.

- **API boundary hardening**
  - Enforced strict HTTP method gating and clear `Allow` behavior.
  - Added structured validation for access codes, Telegram handles/messages, and website URLs.
  - Removed internal exception detail leakage from client-facing API responses.

- **SSRF and network egress protections**
  - Normalized user-supplied website URLs before use.
  - Blocked local/private targets (localhost, RFC1918 IPv4, loopback/ULA/link-local IPv6) for external analysis requests.

- **Webhook and outbound message safety**
  - Added optional Telegram webhook secret-token verification.
  - Normalized Telegram identifiers before validation/use.
  - Removed HTML parse mode for user-influenced Telegram messages to avoid rendering injection paths.

- **Runtime resilience and header safety**
  - Replaced `AbortSignal.timeout(...)` usage with explicit `AbortController` timeout handling for broader runtime compatibility.
  - Sanitized CSV filename components used in download headers.

```ts
function isPrivateOrLocalHost(hostname: string): boolean {
  const normalized = hostname.trim().toLowerCase();
  if (normalized === "localhost" || normalized.endsWith(".local") || normalized === "0.0.0.0") return true;
  if (isIP(normalized) === 4) return /^10\.|^127\.|^192\.168\.|^169\.254\.|^172\.(1[6-9]|2\d|3[0-1])\./.test(normalized);
  if (isIP(normalized) === 6) return normalized === "::1" || /^f[cd][0-9a-f]{2}:/.test(normalized) || /^fe[89ab][0-9a-f]:/.test(normalized);
  return false;
}
```

body:
**Beads:** \`ccsc-00f\` (3rd of 5 server-wiring follow-ups)
**Continues:** \`ccsc-0jj\` (PR #186) — admin dispatcher wired

## Summary

Activates the multi-agent defenses in production. The dispatcher wired in \`ccsc-0jj\` mutates the mute store; the gate now reads from it. The rate limit shipped in \`ccsc-gyt\` is now consulted on every peer-bot message.

| Layer | What's now live |
|---|---|
| Rate limit | Two peer bots in a channel exceeding 10 msgs/60s → second bot's messages drop with \`rate.cross_bot_loop\` |
| Mute | Operator types \`!mute @<bot>\` → dispatcher writes to \`adminMuteStore\` → next inbound message from that bot in that channel drops with \`admin.muted\` |
| Reaper | 60s interval prunes \`adminMuteStore\`, \`peerBotRateLimitStore\`, and \`adminNonceStore\` so memory stays bounded under sustained load |

## What changed in server.ts

- New import: \`createPeerBotRateLimitStore\` from \`peer-bot-rate-limit.ts\`
- New module-level singleton: \`peerBotRateLimitStore\`
- \`gate()\` wrapper passes \`muteStore\` + \`peerBotRateLimitStore\` into \`libGate\`'s options
- Reaper interval (60s) extended to call \`prune\` on all three in-memory stores

## Shared state diagram

```
                      ┌─────────────────────┐
                      │  adminMuteStore     │  ← !mute writes here (admin.ts dispatcher, ccsc-0jj)
                      │                     │  → gate reads here (this PR)
                      └──────────┬──────────┘
                                 │
                                 ▼
                      ┌─────────────────────┐
   handleBotEvent ─→  │  gate() checks      │
                      │  - muteStore        │  drop with 'admin.muted'
                      │  - peerBotRateLimit │  drop with 'rate.cross_bot_loop'
                      └─────────────────────┘
                                 ▲
                      ┌──────────┴──────────┐
                      │ peerBotRateLimit    │  ← gate appends timestamp on allow
                      └─────────────────────┘
```

## Tests

No new tests. The stores + gate-integration have 50+ tests from \`ccsc-gyt\` and \`ccsc-gjm\` (PR #182 + #183) covering threshold behavior, mute beats rate-limit ordering, TTL expiry, per-bot/per-channel isolation. This PR is the integration glue.

## Test plan

- [x] \`bun run typecheck\` — passes
- [x] \`bunx @biomejs/biome check .\` — passes
- [x] \`bun test\` — **962 pass** (no count change)
- [x] \`scripts/coverage-floor.sh 95\` — line=96.94% func=97.75%
- [x] \`bunx depcruise --config .dependency-cruiser.js .\` — clean (16 modules / 48 deps; +1 edge from server.ts to peer-bot-rate-limit.ts)
- [x] \`scripts/harness-hash.sh --verify\` — OK

author: jaidensy
body:
## Summary

Three silent bugs found in a full product audit, fixed before they hit real users:

- **BUG-A — Vault secret name validation** (`vault.py`): `SecretCreate.name` now enforces `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$` via Pydantic `field_validator`. A secret named `MY-KEY` or `my.secret` would silently fail to inject into tool calls because the proxy regex only matches `[A-Za-z0-9_]+`. Now rejected at the API with a clear message pointing to the placeholder syntax.

- **BUG-B — Org-scope on permission history** (`tool_permissions.py`): `list_permission_history` filtered `ToolPermissionEvent` by `agent_id` only. Added `org_id == current_user.org_id` as a defense-in-depth guard on both count and data queries. The existing agent lookup already enforces org ownership, but the event queries are now explicitly scoped.

- **BUG-C — Stripe webhook idempotency** (`billing.py`, `billing_service.py`): Stripe retries webhook delivery on timeout — subscription events could process twice, causing double billing or corrupted plan state. Endpoint now checks Redis for `stripe_event:{event_id}` before dispatching, marks the key on success with a 72h TTL. Extracted `dispatch_event()` from `handle_webhook()` to support the new flow.

## Test plan

- [ ] Create vault secret with name `MY-SECRET` → expect 422 with clear error about underscores
- [ ] Create vault secret with name `MY_SECRET` → expect 201
- [ ] Create vault secret with name containing spaces or dots → expect 422
- [ ] `GET /agents/{id}/permissions/history` — verify only events for current org's agents are returned
- [ ] Replay the same Stripe webhook event ID twice → second delivery returns `{"status": "ok"}` without re-processing (check Redis key `stripe_event:{id}` is set after first delivery)

author: tya5
body:
**[tui-coder]** — wave-5 partial (E1 honest scope narrow)

## Summary

- Sanitize multi-line strings in event-hint and chain-reply preview before substituting into Rich markup, so a stray ``\n`` never orphans a closing ``[/]`` tag.
- Per-line catch + plain-text fallback inside ``_PanelContent.render`` so a single broken markup row degrades to monochrome instead of blanking the entire tab.

## Observation (wave-5 E1)

Sub-agent reported "Events tab \`all\` filter renders blank list despite events existing" and pinned it to scroll arithmetic. Drove the TUI directly and reproduced the blank panel at the default tail=200 (= ``_event_tail_idx=3``).

Investigation found a real but **partial** root cause: chain-reply previews for ``user_message_received`` events can carry multi-line bodies (e.g. ``"The available tools are:\n\n*   \`agent.peer__default\`…"``). The renderer substitutes that text into the line template ``[#444444]       ↳ [/][#777777]{short}[/]``, so the trailing ``\n`` splits the markup across two output lines and the next ``[/]`` lands without an opener. ``Text.from_markup`` raises ``MarkupError`` on that orphan, the existing outer ``except`` in ``_PanelContent.render`` returns ``""``, and the whole Events tab goes blank.

Python repro confirmed the markup crash (line 65: ``'*   \`agent.peer_…[/]'`` → ``closing tag '[/]' at position 17 has nothing to close``). This PR's ``_oneline`` helper collapses any whitespace run (incl. newlines) to a single space before the markup substitution, and ``_event_hint`` is wrapped identically as a precaution since hints can also embed arbitrary content (tool error messages, validation errors, etc.).

## Honest scope (= row 5 reproduction axis)

After landing the upstream sanitization + per-line render fallback locally and verifying ``MarkupError`` is gone from ``Text.from_markup`` for every line in the rendered string (full text and per-line both parse cleanly), the user-visible blank-panel symptom **still reproduces** at tail=200 on a fresh ``reyn chat`` boot. Cycling tail (``t`` key) to 30 / 50 / 100 still renders correctly, then cycling back to 200 stays blank. The Textual log shows ``_PanelContent`` resizing to ``height=1`` for the Events tab even after the markup fix, indicating a separate render / scroll cause that is **not** the markup parse.

This PR therefore lands the markup hardening as defense-in-depth — the corruption path is real and would re-emerge whenever any future event hint leaks a newline — but it does **not** claim to fix the wave-5 E1 visible symptom. That symptom is deferred to a focused follow-up investigation; this PR is the independently-correct upstream piece.

## Test plan

body: ## Summary Make the repo legible from the outside, self-checking on every push, and free of a separate design doc that the code has already absorbed. ### `README.md` Replaces the one-line placeholder with a concise human-facing intro: what the skill does, why HTML-as-source, the two-layer "screenshot background + native text" trick, and a quick-try snippet. Deliberately not a duplicate of `SKILL.md` (which targets the agent) — this is the GitHub front-page advertisement. ### `scripts/test-e2e.sh` End-to-end test that: 1. Installs `scripts/` npm dependencies if missing. 2. Runs `html-to-pptx.js` over every `test/*.html` fixture into `test/output.pptx`. 3. Verifies the output is a valid zip, contains the expected number of `ppt/slides/slideN.xml` entries, and embeds at least one media file (the screenshot background). Catches regressions in validation, text extraction, screenshotting, and PPTX assembly — the whole pipeline. ### `.github/workflows/ci.yml` Runs the e2e test on every push to `main` and every PR: - Installs Node 20 with `scripts/package-lock.json` caching. - Installs `fonts-wqy-microhei` + `fonts-noto-cjk` so the validator's font-resolution check passes. - Runs `scripts/test-e2e.sh`. - Uploads the generated `output.pptx` as a workflow artifact for inspection. ### Retire `DESIGN.md` Audited `DESIGN.md` section-by-section against the code: every part is implemented (1280×720 + YaHei validation, allowed-element set, bare-text check, two-layer pipeline, 5% single-line buffer, `td`/`th` as layout cells, embedded screenshots, themes/templates markdown structure, deck-viewer with arrow-key nav and `SLIDE_LIST` placeholder). The implementation actually exceeds the doc (PDF export, touch swipe, rotation, text-transform, letter-spacing) without contradicting it. Most of the non-obvious decisions were already inline-commented in `html-to-pptx.js` (why `waitUntil:"load"`, why `deviceScaleFactor:2`, why the 5% buffer, why `maxRunFontSize` for line spacing, etc.). Three small comments were added before deleting the doc: - `extractTextElements`: notes that `td`/`th` are intentionally in the text-element set so `` works as a layout mechanism rather than mapping to a native PPTX table. - The single-line heuristic: explains the `1.5×` line-height tolerance. - `deck-viewer.html`: documents the `[/* SLIDE_LIST */]` placeholder convention so the patch step is discoverable from the file itself. `DESIGN.md` is then removed and its `README.md` reference replaced with a short philosophy paragraph. ## Local verification ``` ==> Verifying /workspace/test/output.pptx ✓ file exists (2333282 bytes) ✓ valid zip archive ✓ contains 9 slide(s) ✓ embeds 10 media file(s) ✓ End-to-end test passed ``` Ran after the comment additions; no behavior change, all 9 fixture slides still convert.

body:
<!-- multi-close: approved -->

## Summary

Three small Wave-2 cleanup follow-ups — all P3, all surfaced by Rex non-blocking notes during the wave, all small enough to bundle into one PR with the `<!-- multi-close: approved -->` marker. Each fix is a single commit and closes a single ticket:

- **`440c19a` — `chore(#358): drop advertised-but-not-wired allowed_tools_override field`** — the v1 agent-routing schema advertised `allowed_tools_override` in three places (apply-agent-routing.sh parser doc comment, `agent-routing.yaml.example` schema preamble + Example F, `docs/multi-project.md:549` adopter schema table), but `parse_routing()` never emitted the field. Adopters who set it got a silent no-op. Decision per #358 AC: **DROP** for v1 rather than build the parser branch — the full impl needs parser emission across 3 parsers + a consumer-side `tools:` line rewrite + drift-guard awareness for `tools:` differences, which is 50-100 lines for a feature the docs explicitly mark "advanced — use sparingly". Adopters with a real per-fork tool-list override need can edit the agent file directly with a `# routing-config:override <reason>` comment in YAML frontmatter — the same escape-hatch pattern that already handles `model:` overrides. Closes #358.

- **`9a02e94` — `docs(#359): reconcile AgDR-0050 § Axis 4 push-gate scope with implementation`** — AgDR-0050 § Axis 4 said the pre-push guard "sweeps before any push to a public-class remote," but `block-agent-routing-drift.sh` fires on ANY push regardless of remote class. Decision per #359 AC: **update the AgDR to match the impl** (option 2, recommended in the ticket) rather than tighten the hook. The broader scope is the right design — even a push to a private tracking branch can leak later if the remote changes, and adopters staging a deliberate framework-default change should label it with the escape-hatch comment before pushing anywhere. Tightening the hook would add code + a new failure mode (silent-pass on remote-resolution failure) without removing a real failure surface. Closes #359.

- **`8f3638b` — `test(#342): add multi-line lookback pass + self-test to test_site_counts.sh`** — #342 § 2(b) flagged that the per-line grep can't catch claims where the digit and noun straddle a line break (the exact shape that bit `site/llms-full.txt:131-133` before #360 cleaned it up by hand). New `check_multiline_count()` helper flattens consecutive whitespace via `tr '\n' ' ' | tr -s '[:space:]' ' '`, re-scans for `<digits> +<noun>`, dedupes against the per-line pass to avoid double-counting, and reports drift as `file:multiline`. Self-test fixture at end of file synthesises a known-bad `52\n   slash commands` shape (the exact shape #342 names), runs the detector against it inside `$(...)` for subshell isolation, asserts the expected output line. If the detector breaks, the self-test fails the suite. Closes #342 § 2(b). § 2(a) (other noun-pattern synonyms) and § 1 (one-time hygiene sweep) are intentional carry-overs.

## Testing

- [x] `bash .claude/hooks/tests/test_site_counts.sh` — PASS at 53 skills / 31 hooks / 19 roles, multiline self-test fires on the synthetic fixture, real `site/*` files are clean.
- [x] `bash .claude/hooks/tests/test_agent_routing_sync_and_drift.sh` — PASS at 8/8 (sanity check that the apply-agent-routing.sh comment-only change didn't regress anything).
- [x] `bash .claude/agents/tests/test_agent_wrap_shape.sh` — PASS at 13 ROLE_AGENTS + 5 UTILITY_AGENTS + 19 ROLE_CLASSES.
- [ ] Manual smoke (operator, post-merge): write a deliberate cross-line drift (e.g. revert site/llms-full.txt to claim `12 sub-agents` across a line wrap), confirm the new multi-line pass surfaces it with `DRIFT: site/llms-full.txt:multiline — claims 12 sub-agents (across newline), actual is 23`. Not blocking — covered by the self-test.

## Glossary

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| **`<!-- multi-close: approved -->` marker** | HTML comment that opts a PR body into multi-ticket closure. Default rule is one `Closes #N` per PR (enforced by `validate-pr-create.sh`); the marker explicitly allows N>1 for legitimately bundled work. Used here because all 3 follow-ups are P3 cleanup chores from the same Wave 2 review residue. |
| **DROP vs add-parser-branch (#358)** | Two valid resolutions for an advertised-but-not-implemented field. DROP is simpler + has no migration tail (adopters who'd set the field were already getting a silent no-op); add-parser-branch keeps the docs honest but needs full parser + consumer + drift-guard work for a feature that's marked "use sparingly". |
| **Push-gate scope (#359)** | The pre-push guard's blast radius. Two designs: narrow ("only fire on push to public-class remote") vs broad ("fire on every push"). The broad design is what ships and what this PR makes the AgDR prose match. |
| **Multi-line lookback (#342)** | A second scanning pass over a flattened (newline → space) copy of each file. Catches `<digits>\n   <noun>` patterns the per-line pass misses. Reports `file:multiline` as the locus when triggered. |
| **Subshell-isolated self-test** | Running a function via `$(function ...)` runs the entire function in a subshell. Any state mutations inside (e.g. `DRIFT++`) stay in the subshell. Lets the self-test exercise the detector without polluting the outer DRIFT count. |

Closes #358
Closes #359
Closes #342

Refs PR #357 (the wave PR that surfaced #358 + #359 + #342's partial closure)

body:
## Summary

Floor_r001 ("A.S. | TERRACO SOCIAL | TERRACO TECNICO") merge resolved via TWO layered, opt-in fixes on `polygonize_rooms` + `rooms_from_seeds`:

1. **Near-miss soft_barrier endpoint extension** (≤ 8 pt, FP-006 + semantic guards + post-extension effectiveness validation)
2. **Voronoi sub-division of merged-seed cells** (when SB extension can't bridge the gap)

Both default OFF — production pipeline byte-equivalent until opt-in. Production exporter `consume_consensus.rb` UNTOUCHED.

## What changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `tools/polygonize_rooms.py` | +504/-7 — `extend_near_miss_sbs` flag + helpers (`_try_extend_endpoint`, `_validate_extension_effectiveness`, `extend_near_miss_soft_barriers`) |
| `tools/rooms_from_seeds.py` | +167/-12 — `voronoi_subdivide_merged_cells` flag + `_voronoi_subdivide_merged_cell` helper |
| `tools/apply_room_polygon_fixes.py` | NEW (197 lines) — CLI runner chaining both layers with provenance |
| `tests/test_room_polygon_fixes.py` | NEW (366 lines) — 25 tests: synthetic + planta_74 regression + falsification |
| `tests/test_failure_patterns_regression_catalog.py` | +18 — FP-016 catalog entry |
| `docs/adr/ADR-003-plan-shell-exporter.md` | +129 — §12 documents both layers |
| `docs/learning/failure_patterns.md` | +79 — FP-016 entry |

## What did NOT change

- `tools/consume_consensus.rb` (CLAUDE.md §1.4)
- `tools/skp_from_consensus.py` (§1.2)
- `consensus_model.json` schema (§1.3)
- Geometry thresholds (§1.3)
- CI workflows (§1.10)
- Smoke harness defaults

## Outcome on planta_74

| Metric | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Room count | 8 | **11** |
| Suspicious merges | 3 | 1 (SUITE 01 area outlier — legitimate) |
| r001 | `A.S. \| TERRACO SOCIAL \| TERRACO TECNICO` | 3 separate rooms |
| r002 | `SALA DE JANTAR \| SALA DE ESTAR` | 2 separate rooms |
| Plan-shell `with_floors` invariants | (Frente 2 baseline) | **12 PASS / 0 WARN / 0 FAIL** |
| SB extension applied | n/a | 0 applied / 1 rejected (validator vetoed sb004) |

The validator REJECTING sb004 is the honest answer: on this consensus, single-endpoint SB extension alone CAN'T resolve r001's 3-way merge. Voronoi does. **Falsification pinned by** `test_planta_74_sb_extension_alone_does_not_split_r001`.

## Validation

- 25 new tests PASS (synthetic + 4 planta_74 regression + 4 guard + 6 helper + falsification)
- 81 tests across room-fix + plan-shell + FP catalog + invariants suites — ALL PASS
- ruff check on all 5 touched/new files: clean
- `geometry_invariants_report` on `with_floors` rebuild: PASS=12 / WARN=0 / FAIL=0
- Manual evidence in `runs/floor_r001_split_before_after/`:
  - `room_polygon_diagnostic_report_{before,after}.json` (3→1 suspicious_merge)
  - `r001_overlay_{before,after}.png`
  - `with_floors_after/model_iso.png` shows 11 distinct floor colors (vs 8 before)

## Risks

- Voronoi sub-division produces equidistant bisectors, NOT real architectural divisors. Sub-areas are APPROXIMATE (e.g., A.S. Voronoi ≈ 9 m² vs true ≈ 2.5 m²). Documented as known limitation in ADR-003 §12.
- Layer 1 best for small adjustments (≤ 8 pt). Larger gaps need new SBs in the source.

## Rollback

```
git revert <this commit hash>
```

Or per-call: pass `extend_near_miss_sbs=False` and `voronoi_subdivide_merged_cells=False` (the defaults).

## Next steps (separate PRs)

- Operator paints additional CYAN human soft_barriers on planta_74 to refine A.S./TER SOC/TER TEC boundaries to real geometry (currently approximate via Voronoi)
- Cross-check sb004 + h_sb000 audit decisions (Frente 2 PR #143) — promote `warn` → `keep` if visually confirmed
- Wire `--fix-rooms` into smoke harness as opt-in pass
- Apply fix to other plantas in fixtures/ (planta_74_clean.pdf, etc.) once truth-gate baselines updated

body:
## Summary

- New **File → Export → HTML…** menu item. Two image-bundling modes: **Inline** (single self-contained `.html` with base64 data URIs — good for email/Slack/archive) and **External** (images copied to `assets/` packaged as a `.zip` — good for hosting or unpacking to edit).
- Shares the PDF print pipeline (markdown-it render + `PRINT_FONT_PLACEHOLDER` @font-face substitution) but diverges on image bundling and the trailing stylesheet. Font helpers extracted from `exportPdf` into a new shared `printFonts` module.
- HTML export uses a WYSIWYG-matching layout (centered max-width column, surface-tone code blocks); PDF path is unchanged.

## Smoke-test follow-ups baked in

- **Autofocus removed** from `ExportHtmlModal` — first focusable is a radio whose OS-native focus ring read as a confusing orange box.
- **Inline CSS minified** for HTML output only — comment + whitespace stripping drops the `<style>` block from ~20KB → ~6KB. PDF stays unminified for print-window DevTools debuggability.
- **Single-tilde strikethrough** (`~text~`) now renders consistently. Milkdown's GFM input rule accepts both `~` and `~~`; markdown-it's built-in rule only accepts `~~`. Added `expandSingleTildeStrikethrough` — a code-region-aware preprocessor that rewrites pairs before parsing. Wired into both SplitView and the export pipeline so preview, split, and export all agree with WYSIWYG.
- **JSZip timezone bug worked around** — JSZip 3.10.x encodes DOS time using `getUTC*` methods, but the ZIP spec stores DOS time as local with no timezone marker. The entry Date is pre-shifted by `getTimezoneOffset` so extracted-file mtimes match the user's wall clock.

## Test plan

- [ ] **Menu wiring** — `File → Export → HTML…` opens the modal; ESC and backdrop click both cancel.
- [ ] **Inline mode** — exports a single `.html` file; opens in any browser; images embedded as data URIs render; no external file dependencies.
- [ ] **External mode** — exports a `.zip`; extract reveals `<name>.html` + `assets/` folder with images at relative paths; opens correctly from the extracted location.
- [ ] **Selection range** — disabled when no selection; exports just the selection when active.
- [ ] **Strip comments toggle** — review-style `<!-- … -->` and `// …` lines absent from the export when on (default); preserved inside fenced code blocks regardless.
- [ ] **Open after export** — checked → file opens in default browser/viewer after writing.
- [ ] **Image-mode persistence** — re-opening the modal restores the last-chosen mode.
- [ ] **Single-tilde strikethrough** — `~text~` renders as strikethrough in preview, split view, exported HTML, and exported PDF. `~/foo` inside a fenced code block is untouched.

body:
## What

Two small, related CLI fixes:

1. **Fix broken CLI import (regression).** `cli.py` imported `GateKind` from `letta_evals.models`, but #254 ("Simplify metrics/result data model and on-disk layout") moved `GateKind` to `letta_evals.types` and stopped re-exporting it from `models`. As a result, **every `letta-evals` invocation currently fails at import** on `main`:
   ```
   ImportError: cannot import name 'GateKind' from 'letta_evals.models'
   ```
   This imports it from `letta_evals.types` instead.

2. **Add `letta-evals --version`.** A top-level eager flag that prints the installed version (e.g. `letta-evals 0.17.0`, sourced from `letta_evals.__version__`) and exits.

## Why

`--version` is generally useful, and the upcoming Modal-sandbox feature's per-suite `sandbox.letta_evals_version` pin relies on `letta-evals --version` to assert the sandbox image's version matches the host before running samples. Pulling it into its own PR (off `main`) so it can merge independently of that larger change. The import fix is bundled because the CLI can't load at all without it — `--version` is unreachable otherwise.

## Test

```
$ letta-evals --version
letta-evals 0.17.0
$ letta-evals --help     # imports cleanly, all subcommands present
```
`ruff` clean.

author: platob
body:
JWTToken parses RFC 7519 JSON Web Tokens using only stdlib base64 and
yggdrasil.pickle.json (orjson) — no third-party JWT library. Surface
covers the parsing half: split the three base64url segments, decode
header / payload JSON, expose claim accessors (alg/typ/kid, iss/sub/
aud/jti, exp/iat/nbf) and temporal checks (is_expired, is_not_yet_valid
with leeway, expires_at / issued_at / not_before_at as UTC datetimes).
signing_input surfaces the exact RFC 7515 §5.2 bytes for future
signature work.

parse() also accepts bytes and "Bearer <token>" headers transparently.
from_authorization() returns None on missing / non-Bearer values so
callers don't need a try/except wrapper. repr() redacts the signature
to keep credential bytes out of logs.

Signature verification is intentionally out of scope — it needs an
algorithm plug-in and a key resolver, which belong in the caller.

author: cor-sys
body:
﻿## Summary

**Fixes iOS scanning.** iOS Safari doesn't implement the native `BarcodeDetector` API, so iPhone users were stuck on the "this browser doesn't support live barcode scanning" banner. Since iPhones are the primary scanning device for the staff, that was a bug. This PR adds a `@zxing/browser` fallback that takes over on any browser without native detection.

## How it works now

- **Chrome / Edge / Android Chrome:** uses native `BarcodeDetector` (fast, no extra JS).
- **iOS Safari / desktop Safari:** dynamically imports `@zxing/browser` and runs the same scan loop against the video element.
- The "unsupported" banner is gone — both paths succeed.
- Permission-denied and no-camera errors are still handled clearly.

## Bundle impact

- Main JS: ~123 KB gzipped (unchanged).
- ZXing chunk: ~114 KB gzipped, code-split via `import()`. **Chrome users never download it.**
- Service-worker precache grew (more files cached offline). Acceptable for 2–5 user scale; we can exclude the ZXing chunk from precache as a follow-up if it matters.

## Test plan

- [x] Local build succeeds; two JS chunks generated (main + ZXing).
- [ ] On iPhone Safari at https://envo.corsys.workers.dev/scan, the viewfinder shows your camera and successfully reads a printed QR label or a real factory UPC.
- [ ] On desktop Chrome, scan still works using the native path (verify no extra JS chunk loads via DevTools → Network).
- [ ] Camera-permission denial still shows the red banner; no-camera devices show the new "no camera, use manual entry" message.

## Important: clearing the PWA cache to see this

The service worker may serve the cached old bundle. After merge + redeploy:

- **Installed PWA on iPhone:** fully close the Stockroom app (swipe up to dismiss it) and reopen. Auto-updater should pick up the new version.
- **Safari tab:** Settings → Safari → Clear History and Website Data, or open in Private Browsing for an instant test.

## Summary
- Remove `TodoViewModule` (`ViewModule` impl that was never instantiated or registered — there is no `ViewRegistry` in production)
- Remove `TodoIdentityModule` (`IdentityModule` impl that was never instantiated or called — there is no `IdentityRegistry` in production)
- Remove dead supporting types only reachable from those impls: `TodoIdentityDescriptor`, `TodoViewState`, `TodoDelta`, `TodoListSpec`, `TodoListView`, and the unconstructable `ViewSpec::TodoList` / `Update::TodoList` variants
- Net `-137 / +13` lines

These impls proved the substrate traits *compile* but not that they *run*, which misleads readers about the live runtime state of the fixture.

## Scope correction vs. the original brief
The brief listed `ViewSpec` and `Update` as fully dead. They are **not** — they are codegen-convention symbols. `nmp-codegen` emits `FixtureTodoCore(fixture_todo_core::ViewSpec)` and `FixtureTodoCore(fixture_todo_core::Update)` variants into the generated `nmp-app-fixture` crate (`apps/fixture/nmp-app-fixture/src/{view_spec,update}.rs`), and `lib.rs` doc comments state every app-module crate MUST export them. So:
- The `ViewSpec` enum is **kept**, now empty/uninhabited (the fixture exposes no views) — the wrapping codegen variant just never gets constructed.
- The `Update` enum is **kept** with only `ActionAccepted`, which the live `accepted()` helper returns.

Only the dead *variants* and dead *payload types* were removed.

## Verification
- `cargo check -p fixture-todo-core` — clean, no warnings
- `cargo check -p nmp-app-fixture` — clean (the real downstream consumer of these codegen symbols)
- `cargo check -p nmp-core` — clean

author: joeblackwaslike
body:
## Summary

- **6 platform adapters** implementing a unified `PlatformSDK` interface: eBay (Sell Inventory + Fulfillment APIs), Poshmark (seller SDK + HTML order parsing), Mercari (Shops GraphQL + US consumer search), Etsy (v3 REST with OAuth2 token refresh), mechmarket (snoowrap + Imgur photo upload), TheRealReal (Apify scraper, read-only comps)
- **Webhook handlers** for eBay and Etsy with constant-time HMAC-SHA256 signature verification, raw-bytes comparison, hard-fail on missing secrets
- **3 Inngest polling functions** (cron every 5 min): `sync-platform-notifications`, `sync-platform-messages`, `sync-platform-orders` — all with JSONB dedup to prevent duplicate inserts
- **MCP server** exposing all 7 platform SDK tools via stdio JSON-RPC 2.0 and an authenticated HTTP route (`/api/platforms/mcp`)
- **Credentials module** with OAuth2 token refresh + 60s safety buffer in-memory caching
- **Notification UI**: realtime bell, panel, and toasts scoped to authenticated user

## Key design decisions

- `PlatformSDK` interface gives all adapters the same surface regardless of each platform's quirks
- Webhook `user_id: null` for eBay (no session in webhook context) — a reconciliation job can match by seller account later
- mechmarket 48h cooldown enforced in DB before any Reddit post attempt
- TheRealReal is intentionally read-only (Apify-scraped comps only; TRR manages all fulfillment)
- MCP HTTP route overwrites `user_id` from authenticated session — cannot be spoofed by caller

## Test plan

- [ ] TypeScript build passes (`npx tsc --noEmit` — currently clean)
- [ ] eBay webhook: POST with valid HMAC signature → 200 + DB row; invalid sig → 401; missing secret env var → 500
- [ ] Etsy webhook: same matrix
- [ ] eBay OAuth2 refresh: confirm token cached, not re-fetched within 60s window
- [ ] Etsy adapter: `createListing` draft→activate→image-upload flow
- [ ] mechmarket: 48h cooldown check, Imgur upload, Reddit post
- [ ] Inngest jobs: trigger manually, verify no-op when `since` returns nothing, verify dedup on second run
- [ ] MCP server: `tools/list`, `tools/call` with `platform_search_comps`
- [ ] `PLATFORM_SETTING_KEYS` allowlist blocks unknown keys at API boundary

author: olesho
body:
Desktop runtime `/health` returns 200 OK even when no workspace daemon is connected.

Combined from `worker@a81a57cb` + `worker2@037ddd8d`. Took worker as the base because it carries the OpenAPI contract + generated frontend types (`api/openapi.yaml`, `internal/backend/api/gen/types.gen.go`, `internal/webui/frontend/src/types/generated/openapi.ts`, `docs/api.md`) that worker2 omits. Overlaid worker2's richer handler (189 LOC vs 118), tests (285 LOC vs 235), and `internal/cli/local/runtime.go`/`runtime_test.go` because they cover more edge cases — confirmed the worker2 response shape (`{ready, mode, workspace, reason?}`) matches worker's OpenAPI schema exactly, so no codegen re-run needed.

## Why
The desktop runtime's `/health` returned 200 unconditionally — so a workspace whose daemon had crashed/never-started looked healthy from the UI. ensure-runtime had no separate readiness signal to distinguish "process up" from "daemon connected and serving this workspace".

## Changes
- `internal/webui/handlers/health/runtime_ready.go` (new): workspace-scoped readiness handler. In daemon mode, checks workspace registration in the daemon `MultiPool` (returns `ErrWorkspaceNotRegistered` for unknown workspaces) and the daemon's `Health` RPC over its local socket. In fleet mode (`daemonExpected=false`), falls back to `IssueBackend.Stats`. The reflected `ws` path value is truncated to 64 chars before echoing into the response body, since this is an unauthenticated probe.
- `internal/cli/local/runtime.go`: probes the new endpoint from `ensure-runtime` via `WaitForWorkspaceReady`, which surfaces the last decoded `reason` on timeout instead of `context deadline exceeded`. Wraps the 503 body in `io.LimitReader(64 KiB)` and trims a trailing slash from `baseURL` before constructing the endpoint.
- `internal/webui/app/routes.go`: bypasses workspace middleware for the unauthenticated `/runtime-ready` probe. Exact-path match (not `HasSuffix`) so a future nested route ending in `/runtime-ready` does not silently skip middleware. Note: Go's ServeMux percent-decodes `%2F` before this comparison, so the bypass also fires for paths like `/api/workspaces/abc%2Fdef/runtime-ready` — downstream is safe (handler does a map lookup, not a filesystem walk).
- `internal/webui/handlermux/handlermux.go`: registers the new route on the workspace ops module.
- `api/openapi.yaml`, `internal/backend/api/gen/types.gen.go`, `internal/webui/frontend/src/types/generated/openapi.ts`, `docs/api.md`: contract additions for `/api/workspaces/{ws}/runtime-ready`. Response shape: `{ready: boolean, mode: "daemon"|"fleet", workspace: string, reason?: string}`; `required: [ready, mode, workspace]`.
- Tests in `internal/webui/handlers/health/runtime_ready_test.go` cover: daemon present + workspace registered → 200 (`_HealthRPCSucceeds`); daemon present + workspace NOT registered → 503 (`_WorkspaceNotRegistered`); no daemon / pool errors → 503 (`_PoolGetErrors`); daemon present but Health RPC fails → 503 (`_HealthRPCFails`); daemon starting up → 503 with "starting" reason (`_DaemonStarting`); fleet-mode happy path → 200 (`_FleetMode_BackendStatsOK`); fleet-mode backend errors → 503 (`_FleetMode_BackendStatsErrors`); fleet-mode nil backend → 503 (`_FleetMode_NilBackend`); missing `{ws}` path parameter → 400 with `mode` populated from `daemonExpected` (`_MissingPathValue`, `_MissingPathValue_FleetMode`); echoed `ws` truncated at 64 chars (`_ReflectedWsTruncated`).
- `internal/webui/handlermux/workspace_ops_module_test.go`: sibling-symmetric typed-nil `*MultiPool` test for `/runtime-ready` (`TestWorkspaceOpsModule_TypedNilPoolRuntimeReady`) — `normalizePool` flattening guarantees no panic.
- `internal/cli/local/runtime_test.go`: `TestWaitForWorkspaceReadyTrimsBaseURLTrailingSlash` (defensive single-slash assertion) and `TestWaitForWorkspaceReadyBoundsBodyRead` (LimitReader cap on misbehaving 503).
- Repro: `scripts/repro/loom-runtime-no-workspace-daemon.sh`. Now also asserts `mode in {daemon, fleet}` so a future regression that empties the field is caught.

## Test plan
- [x] `go test ./internal/webui/handlers/health/... ./internal/cli/local/... ./internal/webui/handlermux/...`
- [x] `make check` (full quality gate)
- [x] `bash scripts/repro/loom-runtime-no-workspace-daemon.sh` exits 0.

author: hurtener
body:
A 4-way depth audit of phases 00–09 found five real gaps in the runtime,
manifest, and protocol layers. This PR remediates all five.

## Finding 1 — Panic safety is now a toolchain-enforced guarantee (the headline fix)

Panic recovery previously covered only the *registration* path (`addToolSafe`,
`addResourceSafe`); the **handler-invocation path was unguarded**. `AddTool`,
`AddToolWithSchemas`, and `AddResource` called the app author's handler
directly, and the pinned go-sdk v1.6.0 does not recover handler panics either —
so a panicking tool/resource handler on a live `tools/call` / `resources/read`
crashed the whole server process.

**Resolution:** new `runtime/server/recover.go` adds `guardHandler`, a single
chokepoint every tool **and** resource handler invocation routes through. A
recovered panic becomes a typed `*panicError` wrapping the exported
`ErrHandlerPanic` sentinel, which the SDK turns into a clean `IsError` tool
result / resource-read error; the panic is logged with its stack via `slog`.
`runtime/tool` needs no separate guard — it installs through `AddToolWithSchemas`.
New tests register panicking handlers, call them over a real transport, and
assert the server survives and returns an error result. Recorded as **D-053**.

## Finding 2 — `AddResourceTemplate` is now exposed

The go-sdk offers `(*Server).AddResourceTemplate` and Phase 10's `ui://`
auto-discovery needs it, but Phase 07 exposed only `AddResource`.

**Resolution:** `AddResourceTemplate` added on `runtime/server` with a typed
`ResourceTemplateDef` (no raw SDK struct on the surface), the same
`ResourceFunc` handler shape, absolute-URI-template validation, duplicate
rejection, and the same D-053 panic-recovered handler invocation. Recorded as
**D-054**.

## Finding 3 — Manifest validation gaps closed

`internal/manifest` validated structure well but skipped three checks.

**Resolution** (recorded as **D-055**):
- `csp.connect`/`csp.resource` values are now checked as well-formed
  `scheme://host[:port]` origins, and a `bundle: single-file` app declaring
  external CSP origins is rejected as internally contradictory (RFC §7.4).
- An orphan `apps[]` entry referenced by no tool is now flagged — the reverse
  of the existing `tools[].ui → apps[].id` check.
- Tools that wire the **same** `apps[]` entry must agree on `task_support` — an
  App's UI is built against one task model (RFC §8.6).

The reference example manifest and the `valid-full` fixture, which carried the
single-file-plus-CSP contradiction, are corrected to `bundle: multi-file`.

## Finding 4 — `v1Codec.Version()` returned the wrong label

`internal/protocolcodec`'s `v1Codec.Version()` hardcoded `return DefaultVersion`,
so `CodecFor(VersionApps20260126).Version()` reported `2025-11-25`.

**Resolution:** `v1Codec` gains an unexported `version` field set to its
registry key; `Version()` reports it. No encode/decode method reads the field —
the wire behaviour is unchanged. Diagnostic-correctness bug fix; no decision
entry, recorded in phase plan 02.

## Finding 5 — RFC §16-item-4 ↔ D-024 reconciliation

RFC §16 item 4 stated the Tasks wire layer is "code-generated from the vendored
schema"; the implementation hand-writes it, which D-024 deliberately records.

**Resolution:** RFC §16 item 4 reworded to accurately reflect D-024 — the wire
layer is hand-written for V1 against a vendored, SHA-pinned schema with golden
tests; the schema→Go generator is deferred. (The one authorized RFC edit.)

## Validation gates

- `gofmt -l .` clean · `go vet ./...` clean · `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...` OK
- `CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -race ./...` — all packages pass
- `golangci-lint run` — **0 issues**
- `markdownlint-cli2` — **0 errors** repo-wide
- `make drift-audit`, `make check-mirror`, `make preflight` — all OK

Coverage on touched packages: `runtime/server` 96.2%, `internal/manifest`
91.6%, `internal/protocolcodec` 92.5%.

author: baseballyama
body:
## Summary
Three related changes:

### 1. Pickable runner size on `Refresh benchmark`
The 2-core default runner mutes the multi-thread story (e.g. 9× compile vs 18× on a 10-core Mac). Add a `workflow_dispatch.inputs.runner` choice covering both ARM and x64 GitHub-hosted larger runners; everything else stays on the default 2-core because **only this workflow** uses the input, and the workflow itself is manually-triggered. Costs:

| Runner | Per-minute | ~10-min run |
|---|---|---|
| `ubuntu-latest` (2-core x64) | free | free |
| `ubuntu-22.04-arm` (2-core ARM) | free | free |
| `ubuntu-22.04-arm-16-cores` (**default**) | ~$0.020 | ~$0.20 |
| `ubuntu-22.04-arm-64-cores` | ~$0.080 | ~$0.80 |
| `ubuntu-latest-16-cores` (x64) | ~$0.064 | ~$0.64 |
| `ubuntu-latest-64-cores` (x64, priciest) | ~$0.256 | ~$2.56 |

ARM larger runners are ~3× cheaper at the same core count, so the default is `ubuntu-22.04-arm-16-cores`.

⚠️ **Prerequisite**: larger runners must be enabled in Settings → Actions → Runners → Larger runners. Free-tier accounts can't use them; they only get the two free 2-core options.

### 2. Machine info captured in the JSON
`scripts/run-benchmark.mjs` now emits a `runner: { label, os, arch, cpus, cpuModel }` field via Node's `os` module + the workflow's `BENCHMARK_RUNNER_LABEL` env var (falls back to "local" off-CI).

### 3. Hero shows where the numbers came from
A new "Machine" row in the hero meta — e.g. `16-core arm64 · ubuntu-22.04-arm-16-cores` — so the speedup figures are honest about the hardware.

Also dropped the now-redundant explicit `Build Svelte compiler` / `Build svelte2tsx` steps from the workflow — `ensureBenchDeps` in the script handles bootstrap for all four upstream packages.

## Test plan
- [ ] Manually run `Refresh benchmark`, leave runner on default → PR opens with `runner.cpus === 16` and `arch === "arm64"`
- [ ] After merge of the auto-PR + next Deploy Docs, the hero shows "Machine: 16-core arm64 · ubuntu-22.04-arm-16-cores"
- [ ] Locally: `pnpm run generate-benchmark` writes `runner.label === "local"`

author: jonnyton
body:
## Summary

- Make quality-leaderboard sort keys tolerate both Unix-second and ISO timestamp values.
- Apply the same timestamp coercion to `last_successful_run_at` so legacy run metadata cannot crash parent selection.
- Mirror the packaged plugin runtime copy.
- Add a regression test for `recommended_parent_for_fork` with ISO `created_at` branch metadata.

Fixes BUG-101.

## Root cause

`recommended_parent_for_fork` calls the quality leaderboard, which sorts entries through `_entry_sort_key`. That sort key coerced `entry["created_at"]` with `float(...)`. Some branch rows store ISO timestamps like `2026-05-15T05:53:29.558425+00:00`, so the selector failed before returning a canonical parent recommendation.

## Why this matters

The M6 cutover plan depends on substrate-selected canonical Loop 2 handlers via `recommended_parent_for_fork goal_id=4ff5862cc26d`. If one legacy timestamp can crash selection for the whole Goal, Loop 1 retirement cannot safely rely on leaderboard-driven canonical selection.

## Validation

author: hurtener
body:
A 4-way depth audit of phases 00–09 found the contract-first codegen pipeline (`internal/codegen`, RFC §6, Design A) silently mishandling real Go contract shapes. This PR remediates all seven findings.

## Findings and resolutions

1. **`time.Time` dropped `format: date-time`.** The inference engine rendered it as a bare `{"type":"string"}`. Fixed via the engine's own `ForOptions.TypeSchemas` hook — `time.Time` now maps to `{type:"string", format:"date-time"}` (D-050).
2. **`json.RawMessage` rendered as a byte array.** The engine emitted `{"type":["null","array"],"items":{integer 0-255}}` — an outright wrong schema. Now maps to the unconstrained schema (`true`), accepting any JSON value (D-050).
3. **Named-constant enums lost their `enum` array.** A `type Severity string` + `const` set rendered as plain `{"type":"string"}` because reflection cannot see a `const` block, while tygo *did* emit the TS union — so schema and TS diverged. New `WithEnum` schema option stamps the `enum` array onto every property of the type (top-level, nested, slice items, map values); `EnumsFromSource` discovers the constant sets by parsing contract source, for the `generate` pipeline (D-051).
4. **Embedded structs were inconsistent.** The schema inlined an embedded struct's fields (correct), but tygo emitted the embedded type as a *named property* (`Base: Base;`). `typeDeclSource` now flattens embedded struct fields at the AST level before tygo runs — transitively, applying Go's "outer wins" shadowing rule — so the TypeScript matches the schema and Go's `encoding/json` (D-051). An embedded type from another package is left for tygo.
5. **Recursive contracts hard-failed.** *Real fix attempted first:* JSON Schema's `$ref`/`$defs` express cycles, but `google/jsonschema-go` does not emit `$defs` for recursive Go types — its cycle detection fires deep in the reflection walk before any node exists, and `ForOptions` exposes no hook to break the cycle or post-process a `$ref`. A real fix would mean forking the single schema dialect RFC §6.2 standardizes on. **Outcome: documented V1 limitation.** `SchemaForType` now detects the cycle up front and returns the specific `ErrRecursiveContract` (naming the cycle path, citing D-052) instead of leaking the engine's vague `cycle detected` string. The TypeScript half (tygo) handles recursion natively, so only the schema half is constrained (D-052).
6. **`CrossCheck` was type-blind.** It compared only property names and optionality, so it could not catch the value-type divergences findings 1–4 produce. It now also compares a coarse value-type *kind* (string/number/boolean/array/object); a same-named property whose kind diverges is reported as drift. The documented `WithNullOptional` limitation is unchanged (D-051).
7. **Test fixtures were too narrow.** Added golden schema + golden TS fixtures and unit tests covering `time.Time`, `json.RawMessage`, enums, embedded structs (incl. transitive + shadowing), and recursion — so the suite would now catch a regression in any of findings 1–5.

## Validation

- `gofmt -l .` clean; `go vet ./...`; `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...` — pass
- `CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -race ./...` — all packages pass
- `golangci-lint run` — 0 issues
- `markdownlint-cli2` repo-wide — 0 errors
- `make drift-audit`, `make check-mirror`, `make preflight` — pass
- `internal/codegen` coverage 84.4% (target 80%)

Decisions D-050, D-051, D-052 filed in `docs/decisions.md`; `internal/codegen` package docs and the phase-04/05 plan risk sections record the recursion limit. RFC §6 needs no change — the remediation is consistent with the settled Design A pipeline.

author: jzakka
body:
## Summary
- `service.go:191` — wrap `s.rdb.Expire(ctx, idxKey, rtTTL)` with `.Err()` capture + `log.Printf("auth.StoreRefreshToken: Expire error: %v (sub=%s)", expireErr, creatorID)` instead of silent swallow.
- Add doc comment explaining the lifetime-alignment intent (rt_index:{sub} TTL should mirror the underlying rt:{JTI} 7d body) and the failure mode (TTL=-1 → permanent set + RevokeAllTokens sweep cost).
- Mirrors the cycle C / F / G `RevokeRefreshToken` / `RotateRefreshToken` / `RateLimiter` additive-logging contract (PRs #70 / #81 / #85).

## Why
Without this log, an `Expire` outage silently strips the TTL from `rt_index:{sub}` and the set persists forever — `jti` additions and `SRem` cleanup keep working, so functional behaviour looks fine, but `RevokeAllTokens` (compromise-detection sweep) would walk an O(N total ever rotated) `SMembers` result and Redis leaks a small amount of memory per session. The new pair has already been returned to the caller, so we cannot fail the request, but the operator needs a timestamped trail to detect the TTL-strip window. Last in-codebase silent-swallow asymmetry after cycles C / F / G.

## Test plan
Unit test `store_refresh_test.go::TestStoreRefreshToken_NoLogOnSuccess` pins the additive-logging contract: happy path emits NO `auth.StoreRefreshToken:` log lines, leaves `rt_index:{sub}` at TTL ≈ `rtTTL` (7d), contains exactly the new jti. Expire-failure-path verification is covered by real-env QA + code inspection against cycle C / F / G (miniredis cannot fail Expire independently without a test seam beyond this cycle's scope).

### Real-env QA
- [x] T1 happy: `/api/auth/refresh` → 204 + new Set-Cookie pair; `redis-cli TTL "rt_index:{sub}"` = `604800` (≈ 7d, lifetime aligned with rt:{JTI} body); ZERO new `auth.StoreRefreshToken:` log lines.
- [x] Regression `/api/auth/me` → 200 + profile JSON.
- [x] Regression `/api/auth/logout` → 200; `rt:{JTI}` TTL=-2 (deleted); `rt_index:{sub}` SMEMBERS empty (cycle C Del+SRem contract intact).

author: thepictishbeast
body:
## Summary

Sibling axis to \`text_line_height\` (the other body-text dimension of WCAG 1.4.12 Text Spacing). SC 1.4.12 has four spacing requirements; this axis covers letter-spacing.

The SC requires that the page support a user-agent / extension override raising letter-spacing to ≥ 0.12× font-size without content loss. Operators who ship NEGATIVE letter-spacing on body text break the override path — the user's accessibility preference can't push the spacing below where the author put it without content loss.

Negative letter-spacing on body text also damages readability for low-vision users, dyslexic readers, and anyone reading at low pixel density. Flagged aggressively.

## Findings (bucketed)

| Kind | Severity | Trigger |
|---|---|---|
| \`text-spacing.negative-letter-spacing\` | strict | letter-spacing < 0 on body-text element (>= 80 chars) |
| \`text-spacing.tight-letter-spacing\` | warn | letter-spacing < 0 on short text node (>= 20 and < 80 chars) |

## Exemptions (mirror text_line_height)

- **Heading tags** (h1-h6) — display letter-spacing on titles is common design intent
- **Text nodes < 20 chars** — formatting fragments / icon-only text are not body copy
- **Runner couldn't compute letter-spacing-px** (e.g. \`letter-spacing: normal\` without numeric resolution) — bail rather than guess

## Out of scope

- Word spacing, paragraph spacing — separate future axes (the other two SC 1.4.12 dimensions; line-height already covered by \`text_line_height\`)

## AVP-2 invariants

- \`unsafe_code\` denied (inherited)
- \`#[non_exhaustive]\` on snapshot + entry structs
- Pure detector; \`TEXT_LETTER_SPACING_JS\` const is the only side-effect channel
- \`MAX_EXAMPLES = 5\` per-bucket cap

## Tests

11 new tests, all passing:
- \`empty_snapshot_yields_no_findings\`
- \`zero_letter_spacing_is_clean\`
- \`positive_letter_spacing_is_clean\`
- \`negative_body_letter_spacing_is_strict\`
- \`negative_short_text_is_warn\`
- \`headings_exempt_from_audit\` (parameterised h1-h6)
- \`below_min_text_length_is_ignored\`
- \`missing_letter_spacing_px_skips_entry\`
- \`multiple_violations_share_bucket\`
- \`preview_caps_examples_at_max\`
- \`js_const_is_iife_and_walks_text_bearing_tags\`

Full \`crawler-detectors\` suite: **1038 passed** (1027 baseline + 11 new).
