## Summary

`scripts/pg_backup.py:195` (`_send_alert_via_legacy_notification`) calls
`notification_service.send_alert("P0", title, content, category="system")`
— but `send_alert`'s signature had **no `category` parameter**. So every
pg_backup alert on the legacy path (`OBSERVABILITY_USE_PLATFORM_SDK=False`)
raised `TypeError: send_alert() got an unexpected keyword argument
'category'`. The caller's outer `except Exception` swallowed it as a
generic "告警发送失败" — a **silent failure** (铁律 33): backup-failure
alerts were never delivered on the legacy path, and the real cause was
masked.

Surfaced by the Plan AI code review as a discovered pre-existing bug.

## Fix

- Add `category: str = "alert"` as `send_alert`'s last parameter
  (keyword-friendly — all existing positional callers unaffected) and
  use it in the `notifications` INSERT instead of the hardcoded
  `"alert"`. **`pg_backup.py` needs no change** — its call was written
  anticipating the parameter; the function definition had drifted behind.
- Wire `_SyncNotificationFacade.send_sync`'s existing `category` arg
  through to `send_alert` (previously dropped), so the sync facade's
  `notifications.category` audit column is now accurate.

Backward-compatible: the default `"alert"` preserves the old hardcoded
behavior for every caller that doesn't pass `category`.

## Verification

- 2 new tests — `category` kwarg reaches the DB INSERT; default
  `"alert"` fallback.
- `test_notification_system.py` → **47/47 pass**.
- `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` → clean.

author: yashasg
body:
## Summary

Closes the **causal-binding gap** that the end-of-loop review flagged in the hero-card-wrapper-restore cycle (logged as WI-h). R1 and R2 already pin the *static* facts that `HeroTimerCard` exists as a struct and is invoked from `RootView`, but they do not by themselves prove the *causal chain* that the wrapper is what protects the toolbar gear → Settings sheet flow. R7 closes that gap at the source-text layer.

## R7a — RootView body co-location
`RootView` body must invoke `HeroTimerCard(`, must host `.sheet(isPresented: \$showSettings)`, and must contain the `showSettings = true` Button action. If a future refactor moves the sheet (or the toolbar Button action) off RootView, the identity-boundary protection R1/R2 provide becomes irrelevant because the regression mechanism is no longer the same.

## R7b — HeroTimerCard body negative space
`HeroTimerCard`'s own body must **NOT** host `.sheet(isPresented: \$showSettings)`, must **NOT** host its own `.toolbar { ... }` modifier, and must **NOT** contain a `showSettings = true` action. Inlining any of those into the wrapper would defeat the wrapper: the presentation slot would be owned by the same struct whose body contains the gear Button, which is exactly the identity collapse that 9da54cf produced.

Both R7a and R7b rely on slicer helpers that bound each struct's body by the next top-level `struct ...: View {` declaration via regex, so nested siblings (SettingsSheet, AboutView, etc.) are not falsely counted as part of RootView or HeroTimerCard.

## ADR back-citation
Updated R1, R2, and R7 `#expect` messages to cite the canonical `.squad/decisions/adr/ADR-0001-hero-card-wrapper-preserves-toolbar-hit-test.md` that PR #21 introduced, so a future failure points an engineer at the ratified ADR rather than just at the test summary.

## Test delta
- Swift Testing: **132 → 134** (+R7a, +R7b) — green locally on rebased main `4c978da`.
- XCUI: unchanged at 5 (smoke suite untouched).

## Build
`./build.sh` green locally (warnings-as-errors).

## Closes
WI-h (from .squad/log/2026-05-21T10-30-00Z-hero-card-wrapper-restore-cycle.md backlog)

author: propensive
body:
Rendering a TASTy type that contained a `RecursiveType` (a self-referential structural type, with `RecursiveThis` back-edges in its body) would loop endlessly in `Syntax.apply` until the JVM ran out of stack. The fix names each recursive binder once, on identity, and emits that name where the body references it; the cache moves into a per-call `Bindings` so cached subtrees cannot leak names from another traversal.

### Recursive type rendering no longer stack-overflows

`Syntax.name[T]` and `Syntax(typeRepr)` now terminate on types that, in TASTy, are encoded as `RecursiveType` — typically structural refinements whose member signatures back-reference the parent's `this.type`. Each recursive binder receives a deterministic, readable name derived from the underlying type (lower-cased first letter, with a numeric suffix when the same base appears more than once in a single rendering).

### Internal API change

The helpers in `stenography.Syntax` (`apply`, `signature`, `typeBounds`, `term`, `clause`, `contextBounds`) now take an additional contextual `Bindings` parameter. A default `Bindings = Bindings()` on `apply` keeps existing call sites source-compatible.

body:
## Summary

Resolves #54 (requested by @regressEdo). Adds a \`-log-level\` flag so the log volume can be tuned without dropping JSON output:

\`\`\`
gcsproxy -log-format json -log-level warn
\`\`\`

Accepted values: \`debug\`, \`info\` (default), \`warn\`, \`error\`. Case-insensitive. The flag is wired into \`slog.HandlerOptions.Level\`, so it acts as a single filter for every log call (startup, access, warnings, fatal).

## Behavior matrix

| `-log-level` | `listening` (INFO) | `access` (INFO, gated by `-v`) | If-Modified-Since parse error (WARN) | fatal errors (ERROR) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `debug` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| `info` (default) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| `warn` | — | — | ✅ | ✅ |
| `error` | — | — | — | ✅ |

Existing behavior is preserved since `info` is the default.

author: padosol
body:
## Summary

PR #109 로 도입한 page-level 캐시 (`match:list:v1:{puuid}:{season|_}:{queue|_}:{page}`) 를 **2단 캐시** 로 재설계.

| 키 | 자료구조 | 의미 | TTL |
|---|---|---|---|
| `match:v1:{matchId}` | String(JSON) | 매치 단건 (전 유저 공유) | 1h |
| `match:ids:v1:{puuid}` | ZSET (score=gameCreation) | 유저의 최근 matchId (최대 20) | 24h |

## Why

기존 page 캐시는 같은 매치 데이터가 (필터 조합 × 페이지 × 유저) 만큼 메모리에 중복 적재. 같은 게임 참가자 N 명이 다른 시점에 조회하면 메모리 ×N.

2단 분리로:
- 매치 데이터는 `matchId` 단건 1개만 (전 유저 공유)
- 유저별 키는 ZSET 하나뿐 (필터/페이지별 키 폭증 X)
- 매치 1건 + ZSET entry 10개 (참가자 수)

100만 유저 × ZSET 20 cap → 약 750 MB 추정.

## Changes

**제거:**
- `MatchCachePort` (page-level) + 어댑터 + 테스트

**추가:**
- `MatchSingleCachePort` / `MatchSingleCacheAdapter` — `match:v1:{matchId}` MGET/SET
- `MatchIdsCachePort` / `MatchIdsCacheAdapter` — `match:ids:v1:{puuid}` ZSET 조회/저장
- `MatchPersistencePort.findRecentMatchIds(puuid, limit)` + `findMatchesByIds(matchIds)` — 2-tier 읽기 경로 지원

**MatchService.getMatchesBatch 흐름:**
1. ZSET 조회 (cache miss → DB 1회 조회 + 양쪽 캐시 적재)
2. MGET 단건 매치 (cache miss → DB IN(...) 보강 + single cache saveAll)
3. queueId in-memory 필터
4. page slice 후 SliceResult 반환

## Trade-offs / Out of scope

- **season 필터는 캐시 우회, DB 직접 조회.** `season → epoch ms` 변환 헬퍼가 없어 ZRANGEBYSCORE 활용 불가. ZSET cap=20 (최근 1페이지) 라 과거 시즌은 어차피 ZSET 에 없음 → cache hit 가치 미미. 헬퍼 추가 시 활성화 가능.
- 단건 캐시의 cache hit ratio 메트릭은 후속 PR.
- 같은 게임 무한대 누적 방지는 ZSET cap (20) + 24h TTL 로만 처리. 캡 늘릴 경우 in-memory queueId 필터 효율 재검토 필요.

## Cache 수명 (반대편: lol-repository)

이 PR 은 read-through 만. **write-through 는 lol-repository feature/match-cache-v2 에서 처리** — 매치 처리 즉시 `match:v1:{matchId}` SET + 참가자 10명 ZADD (`match:ids:v1:{puuid}`) 를 1 RBatch 로 실행.

## Test plan

- [x] `./gradlew :module:core:lol-server-domain:check` GREEN
- [x] `./gradlew :module:infra:persistence:redis:check` GREEN
- [ ] 통합: ZSET hit / miss / single partial miss / queueId 필터 / season 우회 / 빈 결과 6 케이스
- [ ] 운영: ZSET cap 20 → 21번째 매치 들어왔을 때 가장 오래된 entry 제거 확인
- [ ] 운영: 24h TTL refresh 확인

## Related

- baseline: PR #109 (page cache 도입, 본 PR 에서 폐기)
- 반대편 write-through: padosol/lol-repository#66

body:
### Motivation
- Freeze BTC-based weekly market-regime labels from the Pre-1 OHLCV history before the first Historical Signal-Quality Replay using only local Parquet data and deterministic output.
- Ensure fail-fast validation for missing/insufficient BTC 1d history and avoid any network activity or changes to existing Pre-1/Pre-2 logic.
- Produce a reproducible JSON snapshot with embedded source/method metadata that can be committed only after a manual Codespace run.

### Description
- Add `scripts/generate_btc_weekly_regime_labels.py` which loads `BTCUSDT` 1d Parquet via `scanner.evaluation.history.parquet_store.load_symbol_timeframe`, validates closed bars and finite closes, computes `btc_30d_return_pct` and `btc_30d_realized_vol_annualized_pct`, groups by ISO calendar week, derives a single weekly label using the specified rules, and excludes the final incomplete ISO week.
- Emit a payload containing `schema_version=regime_labels_btc_weekly_30d_return_vol_v1`, `status=frozen`, `created_at_utc`, `source` (history manifest and symbol completeness fields), `method` (including `method_id=btc_weekly_30d_return_vol_v1` and parameters), and a deterministic `labels` array, and write deterministic JSON with `sort_keys=True` and `indent=2` to the configured output path.
- Add focused tests at `tests/scripts/test_generate_btc_weekly_regime_labels.py` that cover 30d return calculation, annualized realized vol calculation, weekly label derivation and exclusion of the final partial week, deterministic JSON ordering, and fail-fast behavior when BTC history is missing; files added are the two new files above.

### Testing
- Ran `pytest -q tests/scripts/test_generate_btc_weekly_regime_labels.py` and the suite passed: `4 passed`.
- The tests exercise the 30-day return formula, the realized-vol annualization (`std` of log returns * sqrt(365) * 100), ISO-week grouping and label rules, exclusion of incomplete final weeks, deterministic JSON ordering, and fail-fast when BTC history is absent.
- To generate the frozen JSON in Codespace run: `python scripts/generate_btc_weekly_regime_labels.py --history-root snapshots/history/ohlcv --history-manifest snapshots/history/manifests/history_manifest.json --symbol-completeness snapshots/history/manifests/symbol_completeness.json --output snapshots/history/regime_labels/regime_labels_btc_weekly_30d_return_vol_v1.json`, and the expected output path is `snapshots/history/regime_labels/regime_labels_btc_weekly_30d_return_vol_v1.json`.

author: douglashardman
body:
## Summary

Implements the "fcntl-style lock for liveness" hardening Grok flagged in QC pass #2 and Doug locked in: replaces the historical `kill(pid, 0)` liveness model with a `proper-lockfile`-based check across the supervisor daemon and every Agent. A recycled PID owned by an unrelated process can no longer be mistaken for our live daemon or Agent.

Implementation library is `proper-lockfile` (what npm itself depends on). Same correctness as native `fcntl` for our threat model; trade-off is documented in [the decision record](https://github.com/twentytwohundred/wiki/blob/main/decisions/2026-05-21-pid-file-liveness-via-lockfiles.md): we accept a ~10-second staleness window on SIGKILL in exchange for not needing a native build step. The implementation is hidden behind a small `process-lock.ts` interface so a future swap to native `fcntl` is purely internal.

## The shape

| Old | New |
|---|---|
| `kill(pid, 0)` against the PID stored in `supervisor.pid` | `isLockHeld(pidPath)` ... the lock is held by the live daemon for its lifetime |
| `kill(pid, 0)` against each Agent's recorded PID | `isLockHeld(<home>/agents/<name>/agent.pid)` ... the Agent acquires its own lock at boot |
| stranger PID fakes liveness | strangers cannot fake holdership of our lockfile |

The PID number is still stored in the file (operator inspection, signal targeting). The lock is the authoritative liveness signal; `kill(0)` survives only in the documented migration path.

## What changed

**New substrate**: `src/runtime/supervisor/process-lock.ts` — thin wrapper around `proper-lockfile`. Exposes `acquireProcessLock`, `isLockHeld`, `waitForLockRelease`, and a `ProcessLock` handle.

**Daemon path**:
- `supervisor/bootstrap.ts` acquires the lock right after `writePidFile`, releases before `removePidFile` on shutdown.
- `supervisor/daemon.ts` `startDaemon` waits up to 10s for the child to acquire its lock before returning. Tests opt out via `waitForReady: false`.
- `supervisor/daemon.ts` `killDaemon` falls back to the legacy `kill(0)` path during the migration window.
- `supervisor/pidfile.ts` `readLivePid` is now lock-based. New `readLegacyPidFile` covers the migration.

**Agent path**:
- `agent/bootstrap.ts` acquires `<home>/agents/<name>/agent.pid`. Released on graceful shutdown.
- `supervisor.ts` `scanAgentLiveness` and the revive/adopt loop check lock holdership instead of `isPidAlive(record.pid)`.
- `lifecycle.ts` `AdoptedAgentImpl` checks lock with a `kill(0)` fallback for tests/migration when no lockfile exists.

**Upgrade runner**: `waitForDaemonExit` checks both lock-release AND `kill(0)` for the fastest signal on SIGKILL.

**Storage**: `AgentPaths.pidFile` added (`<home>/agents/<name>/agent.pid`).

**Migration**: documented in the PR commit message and the decision record. `daemon start` refuses cleanly when an unlocked-but-alive PID file is found, with a specific message telling the operator how to recover.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm verify`: 1805 tests passing (1791 → 1805; 14 new). Clean lint/format/typecheck/build.
- [x] New `tests/runtime/supervisor/process-lock.test.ts` covers acquire/release/check + the **cross-process stranger-PID scenario** (a child holds the lock; parent's acquire rejects with `ELOCKED`). This is the hazard guard test.
- [x] `tests/runtime/supervisor/pidfile.test.ts` adds explicit coverage of "lock not held → stranger-PID protection" and `readLegacyPidFile` migration behavior.
- [x] Existing daemon/lifecycle tests updated for the lock-based shape and pass.

## QC brief for next pass (Grok)

To forward when you're ready:

> ## QC Pass #3: lock-based liveness model
>
> Working directory `/Users/dhardman/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox/Business/2200/hobby/code/2200`, branch `feat/process-locks-for-pid-liveness` (PR #TBD).
>
> Read deeply:
> - `src/runtime/supervisor/process-lock.ts` (new wrapper)
> - `src/runtime/supervisor/pidfile.ts` (now lock-based liveness + legacy migration path)
> - `src/runtime/supervisor/daemon.ts` (startDaemon / killDaemon migration handling)
> - `src/runtime/supervisor/bootstrap.ts` (supervisor lock-acquire)
> - `src/runtime/agent/bootstrap.ts` (per-Agent lock-acquire)
> - `src/runtime/supervisor/lifecycle.ts` (AdoptedAgentImpl lock-with-fallback)
> - `src/runtime/install/upgrade-runner.ts` (waitForDaemonExit dual signal)
>
> What to look for:
> 1. **Migration correctness**. The pre-lock → post-lock transition is a one-time hazard window. `daemon start` correctly refuses on an unlocked-but-alive PID; `daemon stop` correctly targets a legacy daemon. Verify both paths walk the operator out cleanly.
> 2. **The 10-second staleness window**. After SIGKILL, no new daemon can start until staleness expires. Verify the bound is consistent across `STALE_MS` (process-lock.ts) and any test timings.
> 3. **AdoptedAgentImpl's kill(0) fallback**. This deliberately preserves the existing test/migration shape: if no lockfile exists at all, fall back to `kill(0)`. Verify the precedence — lock-held → alive, lock-stale-or-missing-while-file-exists → dead, no-file → fallback. Edge cases?
> 4. **Lock release ordering on shutdown**. Lock release BEFORE PID-file removal. If the order ever flips, document why.
> 5. **`waitForReady: false` test escape hatch**. Used by daemon.test.ts to bypass the readiness wait when a bogus bootstrap path is used. Confirm no production caller relies on the bypass.
> 6. **proper-lockfile process-exit hook interaction**. The library auto-releases on graceful exit. Our explicit `release()` is idempotent; confirm that the auto-release path does not race the explicit one.
>
> Conventions: ellipses not em-dashes, "Agent" capitalized, no marketing speak, no per-file copyright headers. Deliverable: patch file at `/tmp/qc3.patch`, do NOT leave in-place edits on the working tree this time (deterministic apply by me). Findings write-up in the same shape as QC #1 and #2. Flag load-bearing decisions to Doug rather than guessing.

author: kerem-acer
body:
## Summary

`@insurup/sdk@0.1.15` through `0.1.18` all shipped with a stale `@insurup/contracts: 0.1.14` pin even though the contracts version had moved on. Consumers ended up with a nested older contracts copy and new fields (e.g. customer count aggregates) failed to typecheck through the SDK re-exports.

Root cause is [oven-sh/bun#24687](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/24687): `bun publish` resolves `workspace:*` against `bun.lock`, not against the current `package.json`. When the workflow bumps `.version` in `package.json` and then runs `bun install`, the lockfile's recorded workspace versions don't get refreshed, so the substitution at publish time uses the old version.

### Fix

- Add `bun update` to the publish workflow after the version bump. This is the [idiomatic fix](https://ianm.com/posts/2025-08-18-setting-up-changesets-with-bun-workspaces) and refreshes workspace versions in `bun.lock` so `bun publish` substitutes correctly.
- Convert `table-adapter-core`'s `@insurup/sdk` dep (`^0.1.13`) and peer dep (`"latest"`) to `workspace:*` so the same substitution flow handles them.

### After this lands

Cutting a `v0.1.19` release should produce:

| package | dep | published value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| sdk | @insurup/contracts | `^0.1.19` |
| table-adapter-core | @insurup/sdk (dep) | `^0.1.19` |
| table-adapter-core | @insurup/sdk (peer) | `^0.1.19` |
| table-adapter-{react,vue,svelte} | @insurup/table-adapter-core | `^0.1.19` |

## Test plan

- [x] `bun run typecheck`
- [x] `bun run lint`
- [x] `bun run format:check`

- [x] `bun run test`
- [ ] After merge: cut a `v0.1.19` GitHub release and verify `npm view @insurup/sdk@0.1.19 dependencies` shows `@insurup/contracts: ^0.1.19`

author: fedebev
body:
## Summary

When no dedicated \`cache_redis\` is configured, \`resolveCacheRedis\` aliases \`c.cacheRedis\` to the **limiter's own redis client**. The previous code then called \`c.cacheRedis.Close()\` in three places — \`NewChain\` error path, \`reloadExternalRL\`, and \`Chain.Close\` — each closing the limiter's connection out from under it.

This PR tracks ownership and only closes when owned.

## Why

The bug was uncovered while writing the test for PR #3 (\`auth-cache-reload-order\`). On the borrowed-alias path:

- Reload would silently kill the limiter's redis connection by way of "closing the dedicated cache client" that wasn't actually dedicated.
- External RL caching then operates on a closed client until the recovery loop kicks in.
- A long-running pod running without dedicated \`cache_redis\` would degrade subtly with every reload.

Stage uses a dedicated \`cache_redis\` so this bug never surfaced there. Any cluster without it was affected.

## Changes

- New \`cacheRedisOwned bool\` on \`Chain\`, set by \`resolveCacheRedis\` (true for dedicated, false for the limiter alias).
- New \`releaseCacheRedis()\` helper: closes only when owned, then clears both fields under \`c.mu\` so the racing read in \`recoveryInstall\` isn't torn.
- Three ad-hoc close blocks replaced by the helper.
- \`recoveryInstall\` reads \`c.cacheRedis\` under \`c.mu.RLock\` to pair with the lock-protected write.

## Known follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Other \`c.cacheRedis\` writes (inside \`resolveCacheRedis\`) still happen without locking. They run from \`NewChain\` (single-threaded init) and \`reloadExternalRL\` (guarded by \`Reload\`'s ordering), so they're not racing in practice — but a full lock audit is worth doing.
- \`recoveryLoop\` doesn't have a \`WaitGroup\` join in \`Chain.Close\`; the goroutine is signalled to exit via \`ctx.Done()\` but \`Close\` does not wait. With the lock-protected swap this is now race-safe, but a clean shutdown contract would be cleaner.

## Test plan

- [x] \`TestReload_BorrowedCacheRedisSurvivesExternalRLReload\`: no dedicated \`cache_redis\` → capture \`limiter.Client()\` ref → \`Reload\` → assert that captured ref still responds to \`Ping\`. Fails on \`main\`, passes here.
- [x] \`TestReload_OwnedCacheRedisIsClosedOnReload\`: dedicated \`cache_redis\` → capture the owned client → \`Reload\` → assert old client is \`Close\`d and a fresh one is in place.
- [x] Full repo race tests pass (\`go test -race ./...\`).
- [x] \`go vet ./...\` clean.

body:
## Stack
Closes #74
- Base branch: `main`
- Depends on: none (root of the new stack)
- This PR closes: #74

## Summary
The public story detail page (`/stories/[slug]`) used to render a single hardcoded editorial essay for every slug and resolve metadata from the static `STORIES` array, so CMS-authored articles never appeared on the site and any CMS-only slug 404'd.

This PR makes the detail page fetch the article from `/api/stories/:slug` (the same store the CMS and public listing already use) and render its persisted `bodyJson` through the shared `<ArticleBody />` Tiptap renderer. Cover, title, Japanese subtitle, author, category, reading time, and tag come from the fetched record. Read-completion still fires against the fetched article's id, so the reward path is unchanged.

## Implementation Plan Executed
- `apps/web/app/(site)/stories/[slug]/page.tsx` — reduced to a thin server component that hands the slug to a client `DetailReader`. Dropped `generateStaticParams` over `STORIES`; the route is fully dynamic since the source of truth is the in-browser MSW + Dexie store.
- `apps/web/app/(site)/stories/[slug]/detail-reader.tsx` — rewrote the reader as a slug-driven client component:
  - Fetches the article via react-query, with explicit loading and error states and a `not_found` sentinel that maps a 404 from the API to `notFound()`.
  - Renders the body via `<ArticleBody bodyJson={...} />`. Dropped the hardcoded TOC/quote/figure/video and the static "Letters to a slower year" essay copy.
  - Title, Japanese subtitle, author + initial, category, reading time, date, and tag now come from the fetched article.
  - "Read next" sidebar fetches live siblings via `/api/stories?kind=...&page=1&limit=3` and excludes the current story.
  - Save toggle / read-completion / `story_view` and `growth_item_level_up` tracking continue to use the fetched `article.id`.
- `apps/web/e2e/stories.spec.ts` — added two cases (see Test Plan).

## Test Plan
- [x] `bun run check`
- [x] `bun run typecheck`
- [x] `bun test` (111 pass)
- [x] `bunx playwright test` (12 pass, including the two new cases)

New e2e coverage:
- `story detail renders authored bodyJson, not a hardcoded essay` — visits `quiet-rituals-slower-morning` and asserts both its title and seeded body paragraph; then visits `spring-bowl-five-colors` and asserts a different title and body. This pins the "two slugs, two bodies" criterion.
- `unknown story slug returns the not-found page` — visits `/stories/this-slug-does-not-exist`, asserts Next's not-found page renders, and asserts the formerly-hardcoded "Letters to a slower year" essay is not present.

## Screenshots
Not captured: visual changes are constrained to the body region (replacing static essay markup with the Tiptap-rendered `bodyJson` from the seed) and the loading / not-found states; behavior is exercised by the new Playwright cases.

## Baseline fixes
None.

Note: a fresh checkout had `node_modules` missing several workspace deps (`@tanstack/react-query`, `@playwright/test`, etc.). I ran `bun install` to populate them; no lockfile changes resulted.

## Notes for Review
- Scope boundaries: this PR only changes `/stories/[slug]`. The home page hero (`apps/web/app/(site)/page.tsx`) still hardcodes "Letters to a slower year" copy and links to `quiet-rituals-slower-morning`; that's a separate teaser surface, out of scope here.
- `/readers/[slug]` has the same shape of bug and is tracked by **#75**, which depends on this PR's fetch+`ArticleBody` pattern. I'll stack #75 on this branch next.
- The detail page is now a fully client-rendered route (no `generateStaticParams`). That's consistent with the rest of the public site, which is driven by MSW + Dexie.

author: duncankmckinnon
body:
## Summary

Fixes the Claude Code marketplace install path for `claude-code-tracing@coding-harness-tracing`. Before this PR a marketplace install appeared to succeed, but every hook invocation tracebacked at runtime and zero traces emitted. After this PR a fresh install bootstraps a working venv and hooks resolve backend credentials from `~/.claude/settings.json` — no manual config-file editing required.

## Problems

1. **Plugin pyproject escaped the plugin root.** It was a symlink to the repo-root `pyproject.toml`. That worked locally (the bootstrap resolved the symlink and installed from the repo root, picking up sibling `tracing/` and `core/` packages), but marketplace fetch flattened the symlink to its target content while leaving the `tracing/` parent behind. Pip installed `core/` and silently dropped `tracing.claude_code.*` — every entry-point shim died with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tracing'`.

2. **`resolve_backend()` didn't consult env vars.** The docstring said "No fallback to environment variables" — but the plugin README told marketplace users to put `ARIZE_API_KEY` / `ARIZE_SPACE_ID` in `~/.claude/settings.json` env. The marketplace install path never writes `~/.arize/harness/config.yaml` (no interactive wizard), so backend resolution always errored with "No config entry for harness 'claude-code'" even when env was populated.

3. **Manifest registered hooks/skills twice.** `plugin.json` had `"hooks": "./hooks/hooks.json"` and `"skills": "./skills/"` pointing at default auto-discovery paths. The loader rejected the plugin on duplicate registration.

4. **Bootstrap masked pip failures.** The install command was piped through `tail -5`, hiding pip's exit code — a failed install reported "Tracing venv ready" anyway.

## Fixes

| Area | Commit | Change |
|---|---|---|
| Self-contained pyproject | 59efd7c | Real plugin-local `pyproject.toml` using setuptools `package-dir = {"tracing.claude_code" = "."}` to remap the plugin root onto the namespace; `core` symlink continues to ship the core package |
| Package rename | 042e872 | `coding-harness-tracing` → `claude-code-tracing` to avoid silent collision with the repo-root distribution |
| Backend env fallback | cff9f1e | `resolve_backend()` now consults env first (`PHOENIX_ENDPOINT` / `ARIZE_API_KEY`+`ARIZE_SPACE_ID` / `ARIZE_PROJECT_NAME`), falling through to YAML, then defaults |
| Manifest cleanup | e8e13d4 | Removed redundant `"hooks"` and `"skills"` fields — auto-discovery handles them |
| Loud install failures | 5ae1ae9 | Bootstrap script checks pip's exit code directly instead of swallowing it through a pipe; also dropped phantom `core.vscode_bridge` from packages list |
| Test maintenance | e2eb169 + cff9f1e | Updated `TestResolveBackend` for the new env-precedence contract (14 cases); deleted obsolete tests asserting removed manifest fields and removed symlink-resolution logic |

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/core/test_common.py::TestResolveBackend` — 14 cases covering YAML-only, env-only, env-overrides-YAML, and all error paths (no backend, partial creds, missing endpoint)
- [x] `pytest` — full suite passes (121 tests)
- [x] End-to-end marketplace simulation (`cp -RL` plugin → tmp dir → `run-hook` bootstrap) succeeds: 16 hook shims installed, hook invocation exits 0, second invocation skips reinstall via hash marker
- [x] Live install via `claude plugin install` from this branch: hooks fire without `ModuleNotFoundError`, env vars from `~/.claude/settings.json` resolve to an arize backend, traces visible in `~/.arize/harness/logs/claude-code.log`

## Notes

The branch history shows the debug journey (versions briefly went 1.0.0 → 1.0.1 → 1.0.2 → 1.0.3, then settled back to 1.0.1) because Claude Code's marketplace cache is keyed by manifest version — every fix needed a bump to invalidate the local cache. The final state ships as `1.0.1` to keep the externally-meaningful version clean. Squash-merge if you want a tidy main-line history.

## Summary

Fixes the iOS auto-zoom-on-focus issue plus a batch of related touch and UX gaps:

- **iOS zoom**: inputs were 14px under the 640px breakpoint, which forces Safari to zoom in on focus and never zoom back. Now 16px / 44px min-height.
- **Tooltips work on touch**: `.tip` was `::after` on `:hover` only, so explainer bubbles were completely inaccessible on phones. Tapping now toggles `.is-open`; tapping elsewhere closes any open tip.
- **Comboboxes close on outside tap**: `#symbol-combo` and `#pf-symbol-combo` only closed on `blur`, which is unreliable on iOS Safari. Added a document `pointerdown` closer.
- **Manual grader status clears on edit**: the "Graded." pill used to persist after the user changed inputs, lying about what was last graded.
- **Freshness banner stays accurate**: only rendered at load. Now re-renders on `visibilitychange` and every 5 minutes so the 36h/7d warn states trip when a tab sits idle.
- **Hero numbers scale on mobile**: equity total / perf P/L used `--fs-hero: 40px` unscaled. Switched to `clamp(22px, 7vw, 32px)` under 640px.
- **Touch targets**: site-header icon buttons bumped from 32px → 40px on phones.
- **Tickers grid** shrinks `minmax` from 168px → 140px at ≤400px so two cards still fit on iPhone SE without overflow.
- **Narratives "recently ended"** carousel cards shrunk to `78vw` (cap 280px) so a peek of the next card signals scrollability.
- **Portfolio Risk Greeks / KPIs / Perf stats** breakpoints realigned to the site's 640px (were 720/700px) for a smoother tablet→phone step.
- **13F empty-state** copy softened so it doesn't read like an error.

Edits land in both the static `styles.css` / `app.js` / `index.html` files and the corresponding `renderStylesCss` / `renderAppJs` / HTML template strings inside `scripts/build.mjs`, so the next daily build doesn't undo them. Verified the generated output byte-matches the static files.

- [x] `node --check` passes for `app.js`, `js/portfolio.js`, `scripts/build.mjs`
- [x] `python3 -m http.server` serves `index.html`, `styles.css`, `app.js`, `portfolio.css`, `js/portfolio.js` (all 200 OK)
- [x] `renderStylesCss()` and `renderAppJs()` output exactly matches the on-disk static files (no drift)
- [x] All 11 expected substrings present in the generated CSS / JS
- [ ] Manual mobile checks (Chrome DevTools 375×667 + 320×568):
  - [ ] Tap a "Grade a contract" input — Safari does **not** zoom in
  - [ ] Tap a "?" tooltip chip — bubble shows; tap elsewhere closes
  - [ ] Open the symbol combobox, tap the page background — list closes
  - [ ] Grade your own contract → status pill clears when any field is edited
  - [ ] Switch tabs / leave the page idle — freshness banner re-evaluates
  - [ ] Portfolio equity hero number fits on a 360px screen
  - [ ] Tickers grid shows 2 cards/row at 375px without horizontal overflow

body:
## Summary

Adapts the React-applicable subset of [Nutlope/hallmark](https://github.com/Nutlope/hallmark) (MIT, by Together AI) into a Soleur-native developer-tooling skill. v1 ships **15 Tier 1 ripgrep gates** over `apps/web-platform/(app|components)/**/*.{tsx,jsx,css}` plus a minimal `soleur:review` hook. v1.5 (post-calibration) adds a Tier 2 LLM-judgment reviewer agent + ts-morph gates — explicitly cut from v1 per the 3-reviewer plan panel.

The 15-gate set covers gradient-fill headlines, generic display fonts, purple→blue gradients, side-stripe cards, centred-everything heroes, pure black/white bases, `transition-all`, uniform `hover:scale-105`, bouncy easings, dimension-prop animations, placeholder names, zero-chroma OKLCH, off-scale spacing, prose-width drift, and two-icon-library imports.

Closes #4264.
Ref #4270 (operator-driven 2-week dogfood window — `deferred-automation` calibration follow-through; closure gated on ≤10% FP rate over ≥20 findings).

## Changelog

### Plugin

- **NEW skill `soleur:frontend-anti-slop`** — Bun-runnable deterministic scanner. CLI: `--paths <files-or-dirs> [--dry-run|--json] [--rule <ID>]`. Default behaviour scans staged + modified frontend files vs. the index. Per-file rule disable via `<!-- anti-slop:disable RULE_ID reason="..." -->`. Output conforms to `finding.schema.json` with `category: "anti-slop"`, `selector: "<file-path>#<RULE-ID>"`.
- **Extended `soleur:ux-audit` schema** with a 6th category `anti-slop` (drift-guarded by `category-drift.test.ts` length pin 5→6 + canonical phrase update). Selector field has no `pattern` constraint (verified at preconditions; plan claim of an existing regex was wrong) — overload of `selector` for `<file>#<rule>` requires no `Finding`-interface change. Drift-guard sweep: `dedup-hash.ts` `FINDING_CATEGORIES`, `finding.schema.json` `category.enum`, `ux-audit/SKILL.md` Constants prose, `agents/product/design/ux-design-lead.md` 6-category rubric + JSON example.
- **New `soleur:review` "Anti-slop Scanner Hook"** stanza that runs the scanner inline on frontend-diff PRs. NUL-delimited path collection + quoted argv expansion (post-review hardening — closed CWE-78 against PR-author-controlled filenames).
- **Sibling-trim sub-plan applied** to keep the 1850-word description budget green: `pencil-setup`, `test-fix-loop`, `campaign-calendar` SKILL.md descriptions trimmed ~9 words each.
- **Plan SKILL.md Sharp Edges** gains a calibration-fixture-probe bullet — generalises from this PR's plan-time fixture mis-prescription (PR called `gold-button.tsx` which uses inline-style brand gradient that no Tier 1 rule catches; swapped at /work to `setting-up-state.tsx`).

### Attribution

- Append Nutlope/hallmark stanza to `plugins/soleur/NOTICE` (mirror existing `alirezarezvani/claude-skills` block).
- New `LICENSES/hallmark.MIT.txt` with verbatim upstream MIT + Soleur provenance footer.
- Per-file `<!-- Adapted from Hallmark (MIT) — see /LICENSES/hallmark.MIT.txt -->` headers on `slop-rules.md` + `anti-patterns.md`.
- No `utm_*` URLs in any new file; upstream attribution footer not carried over.

### Tests

- 5 representative Tier 1 rules × pos/neg = 10 inline fixtures + per-file disable-comment behaviour + rule-parsing sanity + calibration baseline (precondition-asserted to fail diagnostically if the fixture file's `transition-all` token is later removed). Per-rule exhaustive deferred to v1.5.

## Summary

PR #3 of the **cbpr** arc — authors the 7 per-subject Case-Based Preview generation prompts plus the shared runtime contract that owns the 18-item validation checklist, the Uzbek register, the Flow v2 forbid rules as applied to CBP, and the canonical JSON output schema.

**Purely additive content**: +1,232 / -0 across 13 files (8 prompts + 5 test files).

## Changes

### Shared contract — `server/prompts/runtime/_cbp_contract.md` (168 LOC)
Mirrors the existing `_shared_context_contract.md` precedent in `runtime/`. Single source of truth for:
- 18-item validation checklist (CBP Generation Standard §14)
- Uzbek register (system voice = Siz; in-case character dialogue = role-natural)
- Flow v2 forbid rules #3–#6 + #19 + #20 as applied to CBP
- Required 8-section CBP structure (case_setup → ckp1 → lb1 → ckp2 → lb2 → ckp3 → simulation → feedback)
- Canonical JSON output schema with all 9 envelope fields + nested checkpoint shape
- Final rule (Standard §16) — the 5 claims a passing CBP student must be able to make

### Per-subject prompts — `server/prompts/<subject>/case-based-preview.md` (×7)

| Subject | Family | Source | LOC |
|---|---|---|---:|
| math-algebra | Math | `Infra/.../nets_cbp_prompt_math_family.md` | 81 |
| geometriya-g7-11 | Math | Math family + geometry overrides (Standard §4 strong visual demand) | 89 |
| biology | Sciences | `Infra/.../nets_cbp_prompt_sciences.md` | 82 |
| physics | Sciences | Sciences family + phenomenon-first overrides | 79 |
| kimyo-g7-11 | Sciences | Sciences family + safety-first overrides | 82 |
| english | Languages | `Infra/.../nets_cbp_prompt_languages.md` | 86 |
| history | History | Derived from Standard §9.6 (no Infra family-prompt exists) | 81 |

Each per-subject file extends the shared contract with subject-specific:
- Case archetype (math = practical-problem, sciences = phenomenon/observation, languages = communication, history = decision/source/perspective)
- Checkpoint verb examples in formal Uzbek Siz
- Concept-anchor rules (formula syntax / unit preservation / chemical formula consistency / etc.)
- Soft-retry mutation axes (math = numbers/scene; biology = organism; history = actor/event)
- Validation watch-outs

## Tests — 5-tier contract

| Tier | File | LOC | Tests | Pass time |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Unit | `tests/test_cbp_prompts_unit.py` | 112 | ~85 (param × subject) | 0.2s |
| Integration | `tests/test_cbp_prompts_integration.py` | 96 | 7 | 0.1s |
| Smoke | `tests/test_cbp_prompts_smoke.py` | 51 | 6 | 0.1s |
| Sanity | `tests/test_cbp_prompts_sanity.py` | 99 | 6 | 0.1s |
| Function | `tests/test_cbp_prompts_function.py` | 126 | 7 | 0.2s |

**Local results: 95/95 pass in 0.73s.** Structural lints only — no LLM call required (LLM-output validation is part of generation pipeline, not the prompt-file contract).

Highlights:
- Unit: each prompt has required sections, declares family, references shared contract, has anti-patterns / Bad examples
- Integration: families match expected family-string, cross-prompt consistency, history declares Standard §9.6 provenance
- Sanity: shared contract names all 8 ordered sections + 6 required schema fields + dragon-trap forbid; subject prompts defer to shared (no duplication of 18-item list)
- Function: subject-specific `case_type` values are nameable from the prompt; soft-retry mutation rule covers multi-axis vocabulary across families

## Pre-PR audit

Skipped pre-implementation swarm for this content-authoring PR. Source material (Infra zip family prompts, CBP Standard, Uzbek Foundation review) is itself the audited spec. The 5-tier test coverage validates structural integrity.

## Dependencies

Independent of PR #1 and PR #2. Tests run against prompt files via `PROMPTS_DIR` only — no schema or tutor imports. Any merge order works.

## Out of scope (deferred)

- Uzbek native-linguist review pass — per plan §"Risks" P7, ships as draft; native review is a follow-up arc
- Literature subject prompt — not in repo prompt dirs; defer to a future PR
- LLM-output validation tests (would need `requires_ai` marker and `KIMI_API_KEY`)

## Targets

Base: `cbpr` (integration branch). Reviewer bot to merge. **Do not merge manually.**

## Summary

Issue #1275 argues that the orchestrator (Codex/Kiro) should not waste
context tokens periodically running `sleep; find .signals/; git status`
while waiting for workers. Instead a single observation should give a
complete state snapshot when the orchestrator chooses to look or when a
worker wakes the orchestrator via tmux send-keys.

This PR ships the read-only watchdog that produces that snapshot, the
operator runbook for the event-driven wait policy, and 17 contract
tests pinning the snapshot/CLI behaviour.

## TDD trail

1. Wrote `tests/unit/scripts/test_swarm_watchdog.py` first (17 tests; all
   RED — script did not exist yet).
2. Implemented `scripts/swarm_watchdog.py`. First green run exposed a
   subtle bug: my dynamic-module-load fixture didn't register the module
   in `sys.modules`, so `@dataclass` machinery failed when looking up
   `cls.__module__`. Fixed the fixture (register before exec, pop after)
   and reran — 17 GREEN.
3. Cleaned ruff (unused `import os`/`import sys` dropped) and
   ruff-formatted both files.
4. End-to-end smoke against a synthetic `/tmp/swarm-wd/` tree with two
   workers (W-alpha terminal, W-beta heartbeating). Verified the
   `[ALL_DONE]` marker appears only after every worker is terminal.

## Artifacts

### `scripts/swarm_watchdog.py`
Read-only watchdog. Pure stdlib (no `uv sync` needed):

- **`load_active_workers(path)`** — parse `.signals/active-workers.jsonl`,
  silently skip blank/malformed lines, missing file → empty list.
- **`inspect_worker(worker, *, now, stale_threshold_s)`** — per-worker
  observation. Terminal signal status (`done`/`failed`/`blocked`) wins
  over heartbeat liveness; corrupt signal files surface as `failed`
  with an `error` field instead of crashing the snapshot.
- **`scan(registry, *, now, stale_threshold_s)`** — full snapshot dict
  with `timestamp`, `signals_dir`, `registry`, and a `workers` list.
- **CLI**: `--once` prints one JSON line + an `[ALL_DONE]` marker line
  when every worker is terminal (so a tmux watcher can grep without
  parsing JSON). `--watch --interval --timeout` polls until `[ALL_DONE]`
  or `[TIMEOUT]`.

### `tests/unit/scripts/test_swarm_watchdog.py` (17 tests)
- `TestLoadActiveWorkers` (3): missing registry, single entry,
  blank/malformed-JSON resilience.
- `TestInspectWorker` (8): active without heartbeat, done/failed/blocked
  status mapping, stale heartbeat detection, fresh heartbeat reported
  active, terminal status precedence over stale heartbeat, corrupt
  signal → `failed`+`error`.
- `TestScan` (2): snapshot has required fields, empty registry yields
  empty workers list.
- `TestCLI` (4): `--once` prints exactly one JSON line, `[ALL_DONE]`
  emitted only when all terminal, empty registry → `[ALL_DONE]`,
  partial done omits `[ALL_DONE]`.

### `docs/engineering/swarm-event-driven-wait.md`
Operator-facing runbook covering:

- The wait-loop antipattern and the event-driven contract.
- Active-workers registry shape (with all cold-resume fields).
- Watchdog usage (`--once` and `--watch`) with the reported phases
  table.
- Worker heartbeat JSON format and `mtime`-based age semantics.
- Worker-side wake-up etiquette using the canonical
  `send-keys -l ; sleep 0.25 ; send-keys C-m` form pinned by issue
  #1721 and `tests/contract/test_tmux_send_keys_pattern_contract.py`.
- Cross-reference to the user-runnable fixer

author: kukks
body:
## Summary

Reverse-submarine swap claims (and any VTXO settlement path that goes through `CoinService.GetCoin`) were observed at **6.8 s GetCoin / 11.5 s sweep trigger** in a live wallet — should be sub-second. Localised to two repeated CPU costs that fired on every coin and every signing operation, both fixable by caching.

### What was slow

1. **`OutputDescriptor.Parse`** — ~0.6 ms per call in isolation but called ~5× per `GetCoin` (server / sender / receiver descriptors inside `ArkContractParser`, plus the wallet account descriptor + index-resolved derivation inside `IsOurs`, **twice** when `CanTransform` and `Transform` both call `IsOurs`). Under concurrent CPU pressure from batch-session MuSig signing on the same thread pool, those sub-millisecond calls got context-switched and ballooned to wall-clock seconds.

2. **`HierarchicalDeterministicWalletSigner.DerivePrivateKey`** — runs `new Mnemonic(secret).DeriveExtKey()` on every `Sign` / `SignMusig` / `GetPubKey` / `GenerateNonces`. `Mnemonic.DeriveExtKey` is PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512 × 2048 iterations (~1.6 ms measured). A single batch-round MuSig pass calls this hundreds of times — minutes of accumulated CPU work blocking every other async task.

### What this PR does

Three caches and one removed-waste:

- **`KeyExtensions.ParseOutputDescriptor`** — `ConcurrentDictionary<(string,string), OutputDescriptor>` wraps the underlying parse. Bounded by the number of unique descriptors the wallet ever sees.
- **`HierarchicalDeterministicAddressProvider.IsOurs`** — removed the bare `OutputDescriptor.Parse(wallet.AccountDescriptor, network)` line on entry that *discarded its result*. ~0.6-1.5 ms wasted per call, fired twice per coin.
- **`HierarchicalDeterministicAddressProvider.GetDescriptorFromIndex`** — routed through the cached parser.
- **`HierarchicalDeterministicWalletSigner.DerivePrivateKey`** — static `ConcurrentDictionary<string, ExtKey>` caches the BIP-39 → BIP-32 master extKey by mnemonic. PBKDF2 fires once per mnemonic per process lifetime.

Two follow-up commits contain (a) latency probes left in across the VTXO settlement chain at `Info` level (`[sweep-probe]`, `[coin-probe]`, `[vhtlc-probe]`, `[wallet-probe]`, `[spend-probe]`) so the next "why is this slow" investigation has data immediately, and (b) `parse-bench` / `mnemonic-bench` commands in `NArk.Scratchpad` that proved the underlying primitives are sub-millisecond in isolation.

### Validation

Same code path, same live BTCPay process, same wallet:

```
Before:  [coin-probe] GetCoin Payment: parse=1875ms transformer=6171ms   (~8 s)
         [coin-probe] GetCoin HTLC:    parse=3773ms transformer=15401ms  (~19 s)

After:   [coin-probe] GetCoin Payment: parse=0ms    transformer=9ms      (9 ms)
         [coin-probe] GetCoin Payment: parse=0ms    transformer=6ms      (6 ms)
         [wallet-probe] LoadWallet: 2-4ms (consistently)
```

The four-coin batch-session setup that was previously the longest observed sweep window now completes in **24 ms total**. ~800× speedup on the hot path.

### Test plan

- [ ] `dotnet build NArk.Core` succeeds.
- [ ] `dotnet run --project NArk.Scratchpad -- parse-bench` reports sub-millisecond average parse times.
- [ ] In a wallet doing back-to-back invoice settlements / reverse-submarine claims, observe `[coin-probe]` log lines at single-digit-ms total cost.
- [ ] No regression in HD-wallet signing: the cached ExtKey is functionally identical to `new Mnemonic(secret).DeriveExtKey()`.

Both e2e concurrency groups (`bare-metal-cluster` and `k8s-integration`) had `cancel-in-progress: true`, which killed in-flight jobs whenever a new workflow run entered the queue. This caused PR runs to be cancelled when a main-branch push arrived (or vice versa).

author: scala-steward
keanji-x
body:
## Summary

Part 2 of #115. Adds a server→client delivery acknowledgement so a kernel-originated transient `DaemonClient` (PR #110's `inject_stdin`) can wait on a real PTY-write completion frame instead of a fixed `tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50))` close-grace.

- `ClientMsg::Input` migrates from tuple `Input(Vec<u8>)` → struct `Input { data: Vec<u8>, input_seq: u64 }` with `#[serde(default)]` on `input_seq`. JSON-layer backward compat (older browser / hand-rolled callers without the key decode as seq 0); bincode kernel↔daemon hop always upgrades in lockstep — same posture as `ServerHello.is_child_ready` (#128). No `FRAME_VERSION` bump.
- `DaemonMsg::InputAck { input_seq: u64 }` new variant. Emitted **to the originating connection only** (not broadcast) **AFTER** the daemon's PTY-writer thread's `write_all` returns. Channel-send is NOT the ack point.
- `Effect::WriteToPty { data, input_seq }` carries the seq end-to-end. The daemon's `stdin_tx` channel was retyped to `PtyWrite { data, input_seq, ack: Option<UnboundedSender<DaemonMsg>> }`; the per-client ack channel is attached only when `input_seq > 0`; the writer thread fires `DaemonMsg::InputAck` through it after a successful write + flush. On write failure no ack is emitted — the client times out on its outstanding seq, which is the correct semantics (and is documented on the variant itself).

## Design choice — `input_seq == 0` handling

**Option (b): daemon does NOT emit InputAck when seq == 0** (the wire default).

Rationale: browser keyboard input is the hottest frame on the up arm. The browser doesn't need delivery confirmation for individual keystrokes — the existing `RenderPatch` echo back from the PTY already tells the UI the keystroke landed. Emitting an extra `InputAck` frame for every keystroke would double the up-arm frame rate for zero browser benefit. Option (a) (\"always ack\") would burn that wire frame on every browser keystroke session-wide.

Kernel transient clients (`DaemonClient::inject_stdin`) opt into ack delivery by passing a non-zero seq starting at 1, and the existing `kernel_originated_input` trust flag already partitions them from browser traffic at handshake time.

Browser clients (`XtermView.tsx`) leave `input_seq: 0` unconditionally. The WS bridge's existing capability-strip continues to zero `kernel_originated_input`; the `ws_terminal_v2` round-trip test now also asserts `input_seq == 0` arrives at the daemon socket verbatim, as a regression guard against any future bridge-side seq rewrite.

## Ack-emission point — important

Per the issue's \"Trap to avoid\": the InputAck is emitted from `spawn_pty_writer`'s blocking thread, **after** `writer.write_all(&data)` returns `Ok(())`. Channel-send (`stdin_tx.send(PtyWrite{..})`) is **not** the ack point — that would lie about delivery because the bytes are still sitting in the mpsc queue. The writer thread is the only place that knows the syscall completed.

If `write_all` errors, the writer thread breaks the loop and drops the ack channel without sending — the client times out, which is the correct \"the daemon failed to deliver your bytes\" signal.

## PR #110 migration (out of scope here)

PR #110's `codex_auto_submit` currently has a `tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50))` close-grace after sending the auto-submit `\\r`. On rebase #110 will swap that for `await InputAck { input_seq: <expected> }` on the transient `DaemonClient`. The 600ms `SUBMIT_DELAY` in #110 is a separate concern and stays inside #110.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test --workspace` — all green (existing v2_protocol / ws_terminal_v2 / chat_e2e / protocol_error_routing / ws_terminal_e2e tests updated to the new struct variant; existing assertions preserved).
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --tests -- -D warnings` — clean.
- [x] `cargo fmt --all --check` — clean.
- [x] Web `vitest run` — 198/198 pass after `XtermView.test.tsx` updated to the new `{ Input: { data, input_seq } }` frame shape.
- [x] Web `tsc -b` — clean (no type errors on `web/src/api/generated-terminal.ts` regeneration).
- [x] New `crates/calm-session/tests/input_ack.rs` — 8 protocol-layer unit tests:
  - `owner_input_with_nonzero_seq_forwards_seq_into_write_effect`
  - `owner_input_two_frames_preserve_seq_order`
  - `owner_input_seq_zero_still_writes` (seq 0 still triggers `WriteToPty` — the shell is the gate for ack emission)
  - `input_decodes_missing_input_seq_as_zero` (JSON backward compat via `#[serde(default)]`)
  - `input_tuple_form_no_longer_decodes` (pre-#115 tuple shape is rejected; bridge drops it as malformed)
  - `input_ack_round_trips_json_and_bincode`
  - `observer_input_with_seq_is_rejected_before_ack` (authorization > ack — forged seq doesn't induce a write)
  - `kernel_input_observer_input_with_seq_writes_with_seq` (the kernel-private happy path)
- [x] New `crates/calm-session/tests/input_ack_e2e.rs` — 3 end-to-end tests against a real `calm-session-daemon` binary:
  - `input_ack_arrives_after_pty_write` (Input { seq: 42 } → InputAck { input_seq: 42 })
  - `input_ack_preserves_seq_order` (two consecutive Inputs with seqs 100, 101 → acks 100 then 101)
  - `input_seq_zero_produces_no_ack` (seq 0 produces no InputAck within a 500ms window)

Closes part of #115. Together with #128 the issue's acceptance list is now covered (the issue is closed once PR #110 adopts the new mechanism — out of scope here).

author: cpolzer
body:
## Summary

Cleanup pass on top of #3 covering: PlantUML 1.2026.2 compatibility, heading-leak fix across all 9 directives, STM SVG transition-line geometry rewrite, and a comprehensive BDD + IBD overhaul (both rendering empty pre-fix) to production-grade SysML diagrams.

## Key changes

### PlantUML 1.2026.2 compatibility
PlantUML 1.2026.2 dropped the `as ID [[link]]` alias syntax on most element types. Updated templates to use title-based references and quoted aliases where hyphens are present:
- `PKG_FULL_TEMPLATE`, `UC_FULL_TEMPLATE`, `SD_FULL_TEMPLATE`, `STM_FULL_TEMPLATE`, `ACT_FULL_TEMPLATE`
- Case fixes: `UseCase` → `usecase`, `Lifeline` → `lifeline`, `Dependency` → `dependency`, etc. (sphinx-needs stores type as lowercase directive name)
- Restored `{{ ref(id) }}` on all element declarations so SVG output retains clickable links

### Heading-leak fix
All 9 `needsysml-*` PlantUML directives passed `root_id`/`filter_expr` into `NeedumlDirective(arguments=[…])` — sphinx-needs treats that as a caption and emits it as an `<h2>`/`<h3>`. End result was bare IDs like `PD-001` or filter strings like `type == 'usecase'` rendered as section headers. Swapped to `arguments=[]`; user-facing RST headings carry the titles.

### STM SVG transition geometry
Transition line endpoints used a separate index-based position rather than the actual state shapes' bounding boxes — lines floated from arbitrary center points to arbitrary y-coordinates, parallel transitions stacked their labels. Rewrote `STM_SVG_TEMPLATE` to:
- Build a `state_pos` dict keyed by state id capturing each shape's {x, y, w, h} as drawn
- Project endpoints from source center along the direction vector to the source/target borders
- Detect parallel from→to pairs and offset endpoints perpendicularly (`spacing=14`) so labels fan out instead of stacking
- Round coordinates to 1 decimal for cleaner output

### Block Definition + Internal Block Diagrams — production-grade rework
Both `needsysml-bdd::` and `needsysml-ibd::` rendered empty (10×10 px). Five separate bugs:
1. Missing `{% set root_id = "{root_id}" %}` — `root_id` was a bare undefined Jinja variable
2. Wrong-case filter (`'Part'` vs stored `'part'`)
3. BDD composition arrow used hyphenated names but `uml()` aliases nodes with underscores → PlantUML created stray placeholder nodes from the hyphenated form
4. IBD `as P-002` rejected by PlantUML; needed quoting
5. BDD only iterated one level — Vehicle has 3-level decomposition that needed unrolling

Production-grade enhancements once the renderers worked:
- **IBD PlantUML**: direction-aware ports (`portin`/`portout`/`port`) + connector arrows from `Connection` needs whose both ports are local, labeled with item-flow title
- **BDD SVG**: bottom-up tree layout, leaves get columns, parents center above kids, composition diamonds (♦) at parent ends, 3 levels deep
- **IBD SVG**: in-ports on LEFT, out-ports on RIGHT edges of each part, port labels above squares (out of the inter-part gap where connector + connector-label sit), «ibd» italic frame stereotype

### SD message labels
`{{ m.title }} {{ ref(m.id) }}` produced two adjacent elements in PlantUML output. Switched to `{{ ref(m.id, text=m.title) }}` for a single clean `[[…title…]]` link.

### Demo cleanup
- `docs/examples/vehicle_system.rst`: replaced the 40-line handwritten IBD `needsvg` block with `.. needsysml-ibd-svg:: PD-002` (directive has existed for a while; outdated "no directive yet" note removed)
- `docs/index.rst`: added References section linking the SysML v2 Diagram Tutorial at sysml.org

## Test plan
- [x] Strict docs build (`sphinx-build -W docs docs/_build/html`) — 0 warnings
- [x] All 9 PlantUML diagrams render with non-trivial sizes (previously BDD + IBD were 10×10 placeholders)
- [x] 0 `<h[1-4] id="needuml-…">` headings leaked in `vehicle_system.html` (was 9)
- [x] STM SVG: 11 tests including 3 Playwright tests (clickable-link nav, no-overlap pairwise bbox, headless screenshot)
- [x] BDD + IBD smoke tests pass (6/6)
- [x] `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean
- [x] Visual: screenshots taken for STM, BDD (PlantUML + SVG), IBD (PlantUML + SVG) — all rendering as expected per SysML conventions

## Follow-up
Spec 003 (drop SVG-helper inline-anchor workaround once sphinx-need-svg ≥0.3.1 hits PyPI) tracked separately in `specs/003-svg-helper-cleanup/spec.md`. Blocked on upstream PR #3 release tag push.

author: firecrawl-spring[bot]
body:
## Summary

Fixes a reflected XSS in the `redirectTo` query parameter on `/login` and `/auth/callback`, reported via coordinated disclosure (Pylon ticket #29236).

The value of `redirectTo` was passed unsanitized to `router.push()` (client) and `NextResponse.redirect()` (server) after a successful sign-in. A `javascript:` URI in `redirectTo` therefore executed in the authenticated page context. Combined with the JS-readable Supabase auth cookie, this enabled one-click theft of a victim's session and exfiltration of their Firecrawl API key from `user_preferences`.

### Fix

- Add `safeRedirectPath()` in `lib/utils.ts`. It returns the input only when it begins with a single `/` and is not protocol-relative (`//host`, `/\host`); otherwise it falls back to `/`. This blocks `javascript:`, `data:`, `vbscript:`, absolute URLs, and protocol-relative URLs.
- Apply it in `app/login/page.tsx` (client redirect after sign-in/sign-up, plus the value forwarded into Supabase `emailRedirectTo` and OAuth `redirectTo`).
- Apply it in `app/auth/callback/route.ts` before `NextResponse.redirect(\`${origin}${redirectTo}\`)`.

### Out of scope (follow-ups)

The disclosure chain also relies on:

1. The Supabase session cookie being JS-readable (`createBrowserClient` default). Moving the session to an HttpOnly server-managed cookie would defense-in-depth this even if another XSS appears.
2. Firecrawl API keys stored in plaintext in `user_preferences`, reachable via the user's own Supabase token. Encrypting at rest or moving key retrieval behind a server route would prevent direct REST exfiltration.

Both should be tracked separately.

## Test plan

- [ ] `GET /login?redirectTo=javascript:alert(1)` then sign in: confirm the browser navigates to `/` instead of executing the URI.
- [ ] `GET /login?redirectTo=//evil.example.com` then sign in: confirm it falls back to `/`, not an open redirect.
- [ ] `GET /login?redirectTo=/scouts` then sign in: confirm normal in-app redirect still works.
- [ ] Google OAuth flow with `redirectTo=/settings`: confirm `/auth/callback` redirects to `/settings`.
- [ ] Google OAuth flow with `redirectTo=javascript:alert(1)`: confirm `/auth/callback` redirects to `/`.

body:
## Summary

Second of three Tier 4 features. Adds **per-org concurrent-run cap** — useful for shared/MSP deployments where any single org could otherwise monopolise the worker queue.

v1 ships with a single quota. The \`org_quotas\` table is intentionally narrow but designed to grow (monthly spend cap, state size, etc. as follow-ups).

## Changes

**Backend**
- Migration 074: \`org_quotas\` table; NULL columns mean unlimited; orgs without a row default to unlimited.
- New \`quotas\` package with \`Get\` (admin), \`Update\` (admin), and \`Status\` (member) handlers. \`Status\` returns current usage so dashboards can show "N of M in use".
- \`CheckConcurrentQuota\` helper used by every user-initiated run creation path: \`runs.Create\`, \`runs.TriggerDrift\`, \`runs.Retrigger\`, and the webhook handler's two run-insert paths.
- System-internal inserts (drift scheduler, TTL cleanup, auto-remediate from finalize) **bypass** the cap by design — we don't want quota exhaustion to silently kill scheduled work.
- 429 with a descriptive message on quota-exceeded. Webhook records \`org_quota_exceeded\` in the delivery log so missed triggers are visible.

**Counted toward cap:** \`queued\`, \`preparing\`, \`planning\`, \`applying\`, \`unconfirmed\`, \`pending_approval\`. A stack stuck awaiting confirmation still consumes a slot until discarded — intentional, prevents abuse.

**UI**
- New \`/settings/quotas\` page: current-usage card (count + progress bar at 80% / 100% thresholds), enable-cap checkbox, integer input. Admin-only edit; all members can view.
- Sidebar updated with the new "Resource Quotas" entry.

## Tier 4 plan

- ✓ PR #336 (merged): per-resource cost breakdown
- **This PR:** org concurrent-run cap
- Next: approval escalation chains (final Tier 4 feature)

- [ ] Set a cap of \`2\` on a test org, queue 3 runs — third should 429

- [ ] Verify webhook delivery log records \`org_quota_exceeded\` when triggered

author: beardedeagle
body:
## Summary

- Admit exactly one direct nested final-position runtime `if` as the terminal next-state return inside each branch of an outer final-position runtime `if`.
- Thread the terminal next-state-if depth through Strata source checking and checked IR validation while preserving the existing statement-level runtime branch-action bound.
- Mirror the same bound in Mantle artifact decode/admission and loaded-runtime admission so malformed third-level `NextState::IfElse` trees fail closed before execution.
- Add a runnable source-to-runtime example, focused source/artifact/runtime/acceptance coverage, gate wiring, and documentation for the admitted terminal shape.

## Boundary and safety

- Strata source state remains immutable: state changes still occur only through whole-value `Continue`, `Stop`, or `Panic` returns.
- Runtime-significant lowering remains typed: branch conditions, nested next states, state IDs, payload templates, effects, and trace paths flow through checked IR and Mantle artifact IDs/templates, not source aliases or debug names.
- Unsupported surfaces remain rejected: third-level terminal runtime branches, deeper statement-level branch-action nesting, nested loops, branch-local `spawn`, branch-local process-reference binding, statement-branch returns, divergent final-position results, and missing effect authority.
- Programmatic checked IR, decoded artifacts, and loaded runtime programs all enforce the terminal next-state branch bound independently.

author: 9prady9
body:
Closes [#697](https://github.com/sirius-db/sirius/issues/697). Phase 4 of the 11-phase expression-framework rework tracked in [#666](https://github.com/sirius-db/sirius/issues/666).

Phases 1 ([#707](https://github.com/sirius-db/sirius/pull/707)), 2 ([#715](https://github.com/sirius-db/sirius/pull/715)), and 3 ([#716](https://github.com/sirius-db/sirius/pull/716)) are merged — this PR is **additive and standalone**.

## What this lands

Introduces `sirius::ast::from_duckdb(duckdb::Expression const&)` — the single point that consumes `duckdb::Bound*Expression` shapes and produces Sirius-native AST nodes. The translator is the seam through which the executor will eventually stop touching DuckDB expression types. The header itself is DuckDB-include-free; only the impl pulls in DuckDB headers, isolating the dependency.

**Implementation (`src/expression/from_duckdb.cpp`)** — handles the `Bound*Expression` shapes the GPU executor actually evaluates today:

- `BoundReferenceExpression` → `ast::reference`
- `BoundConstantExpression` → `ast::constant` (via `sirius::value::from_duckdb` from Phase 2)
- `BoundComparisonExpression` → `ast::comparison`
- `BoundConjunctionExpression` → `ast::conjunction` (AND/OR)
- `BoundBetweenExpression` → `ast::between`
- `BoundCaseExpression` → `ast::case_`
- `BoundCastExpression` → `ast::cast`
- `BoundOperatorExpression` → `ast::operator_`
- `BoundFunctionExpression` → `ast::function_call` (with `sirius::function_id` resolved via `from_duckdb_function_name` from Phase 3)

author: dmerrick
body:
## What

When the bot's Twitch token can't be used, the logs carry a `reauth_url` attribute pointing at `/auth/init` so re-auth is a click instead of running the bootstrap CLI from a laptop. Surfaces:

1. **Boot** — `loadTwitchToken`'s non-fatal "no usable Twitch token" warning (`cmd/tripbot/tripbot.go`).
2. **Polling** — the `pollForTwitchToken` "still waiting" log (recurs every 15s so the link stays findable while waiting).
3. **Hourly refresh** — `refreshOne` terminal failure (empty access token → revoked/`invalid_grant`) in `pkg/twitch/authentication.go`.
4. **IRC connect** — `connectToTwitch` when `ErrLoginAuthenticationFailed` fires and there's no valid in-memory token to retry with.

Both the **bot and broadcaster** links are surfaced (the broadcaster's missing-token path — `LoadFromDB` + `startEventSub` — previously logged no link). Every reauth surface also logs a `login_as` attribute = the exact Twitch account to sign in as (bot username or channel name), and the **auth-bootstrap CLI** logs the same up front before opening the browser. With three envs and up to six bot/broadcaster accounts, `login_as` removes the "which login?" guesswork.

New `mytwitch.AuthInitURL(account)` helper builds the URL; `accountLabel(username)` maps the refresh row's username to the `bot`/`broadcaster` selector.

Rebased onto #624 (start-degraded-instead-of-crashlooping), so the `reauth_url` now rides the non-fatal token-missing path + background poller rather than the old `os.Exit(1)`.

## Makes the link clickable: depends on the infra EXTERNAL_URL change

`AuthInitURL` builds the URL from `EXTERNAL_URL`. Today that's `http://localhost:8080` in the cloud envs, so the logged link only works via port-forward. The companion infra change ([infra#557](https://github.com/adanalife/infra/pull/557/changes), **merged**) repointed `EXTERNAL_URL` at the internal Traefik Ingress host (`https://tripbot.{prod,stage,dev}.whereisdana.today`), so the logged link becomes **clickable from any on-LAN browser** — no port-forward, no CLI. The OAuth round-trip (`/auth/init` → Twitch → `/auth/callback`) then completes against the Ingress and the poller picks up the freshly-written token.

This code is independent of that value (it logs whatever `EXTERNAL_URL` is), and infra#557 is now merged with the Twitch redirect URIs registered, so the logged link is live (pending a `kubectl rollout restart deploy/tripbot` to pick up the new config). dev is forward-prepared but waits on cert-manager on the bees cluster.

## Security tradeoff (the caveat from the TODO)

We log the **`/auth/init` indirection URL**, not the fully-formed Twitch authorize URL:

- The Twitch authorize URL embeds a single-use CSRF `state` with a 5-minute TTL (`oauthstate.TTL`) — stale by the time anyone reads the log, and it would land in Loki/Sentry.
- `/auth/init` carries **no secret**: `client_id` isn't sensitive, and no `state` exists until the redirect is generated server-side on click. A test asserts the URL contains no `state=`/`client_id=`.

## Test

`task test:macos` — full suite green, including `TestAuthInitURL_BuildsInitPath`, `TestAccountLabel_BotUsernameIsBot`, `TestAccountLabel_UnknownDefaultsToBot`.

Closes the "Surface the OAuth login link(s) in the logs" TODO.

author: chromium-wpt-export-bot
body:
SVG2.0[1] supports media fragments identifiers.

This CL introduces support for spatial media fragments in SVG
images, enabling the use of the `xywh=x,y,width,height` fragment
syntax as defined by the Media Fragments URI specification[2].

With this support, authors can control the displayed region of an
SVG image directly via the image URL, allowing a specific
rectangular area of the SVG canvas to be selected and rendered.

The implementation leverages the existing `MediaFragmentURIParser`,
which already includes spatial fragment parsing logic. The parsed
spatial fragment data is then used to configure the SVG image
viewport accordingly, restricting rendering to the specified region.

In this CL, we also refactor `MediaFragmentURIParser` so that it
can store fragment string directly, instead of `KURL`.

[1] https://svgwg.org/svg2-draft/linking.html#LinksIntoSVG
[2] https://www.w3.org/TR/media-frags

author: henry-creatoryoufirst
body:
## Summary

NVR-SPEC-034 Phase 1a: structural scaffold for the funding-rate arbitrage sleeve. First Tier 2 capability beyond the +5% Option B floor — a delta-neutral yield stream that runs alongside the quality-rotation strategy.

- **Paper-only.** Sleeve is installed only when `FUNDING_ARB_PAPER_ENABLED=true`. Hard-pinned to `mode='paper'` in the registry regardless of any other env var. Live promotion is a separate code change gated on the §8 Phase 2 Henry-greenlit 30-day review.
- **No live capital.** Default allocator unchanged. `MIN_DRY_POWDER_PCT` untouched. Token registry (cohort lock window) untouched.
- **Stubbed funding-rate input.** Phase 1a proves the sleeve plumbing, not the rate quality. The real aggregator integration (OKX / Hyperliquid / Bitfinex per spec §0.1 venue pivot) ships as a separate funding-rate-monitor service.

## Strategic frame

Per `project_nvr_capability_roadmap`: +5% over BTC/ETH 60/40 is the floor, not the ceiling. Funding arb is the single highest-leverage addition because it earns in regimes where quality-timing struggles. Spec §1 ("Why now") for the full rationale.

This PR opens the plumbing; the real venue work happens after Option B clears day 30.

## What's in the diff

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/core/sleeves/funding-arb.ts` | New sleeve. `decide()` implements entry (funding > 3.4 bps/8h, ~+10% APR), exit (funding < 1.7 bps/8h, ~+5% APR, or max-hold 30d), HOLD reasoning on every cycle for audit visibility. |
| `src/core/sleeves/__tests__/funding-arb.test.ts` | 41 new tests covering decide() shape, entry/exit gating, paper-budget enforcement, multi-cycle funding-rate sweep, default sine-wave sanity, and the registry kill-switch behavior. |
| `src/core/sleeves/registry.ts` | Adds opt-in installation gated on `FUNDING_ARB_PAPER_ENABLED === 'true'`. New `getFundingArbOwnership` option. |
| `src/core/sleeves/migration.ts` | Documents that funding-arb inherits the existing $1000 non-core paper-budget default; explicitly notes the sleeve doesn't use generic `SleeveExitOverride` knobs (its exits are funding-rate-driven). |
| `src/core/sleeves/index.ts` | Barrel re-exports for `FundingArbSleeve`, `fundingArbSleeve`, `FundingArbSleeveOptions`. |

## Kill switch

```bash
# Default: sleeve is NOT installed.
unset FUNDING_ARB_PAPER_ENABLED          # sleeve absent
export FUNDING_ARB_PAPER_ENABLED=1       # sleeve absent (exact string match)
export FUNDING_ARB_PAPER_ENABLED=true    # sleeve installed, mode='paper'
```

Setting the flag false / unset entirely removes the sleeve from `registry.sleeves()` — the bot's sleeve roster is bit-for-bit identical to pre-SPEC-034.

## Day-30 review gate (per spec §8)

Live promotion (Phase 2) requires:
1. Option B has cleared the +5% alpha floor on its own merits.
2. Paper-trade harness has confirmed the funding-arb math falls in the expected +5% to +15% APR band.
3. Vertex / Hyperliquid / aggregator venue depth + slippage is acceptable at the $300 notional target.

If any is no → fix that piece first; funding-arb stays paper. There is no flag in this PR that flips it to live.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm test -- --run` — 944 baseline → 985 (+41), all green.
- [x] `npm run typecheck:strict` — clean.
- [x] Sleeve absent in default registry with no env flag set.
- [x] Sleeve installed and `mode='paper'` when `FUNDING_ARB_PAPER_ENABLED=true`.
- [x] Entry / exit / HOLD reasoning emitted with `ALPHA_FUNDING_ARB_V1` audit tag.
- [x] Existing sleeve tests (core / alpha-hunter / alpha-rotation / paper-sim) unchanged and green.
- [ ] Staging soak with `FUNDING_ARB_PAPER_ENABLED=true` — capture decision-log cadence for the day-30 review.

Branch name is `claude/spec-034-*` per CLAUDE.md Rule 2 (automated agents stay on `claude/*` branches; human merges to shared branches). Original feat branch `feat/spec-034-phase-1a-funding-arb-paper` can be fast-forwarded from this if Henry prefers that ref name on the PR.

author: f-trycua
body:
## Summary

PR #1630 made `install.ps1 -AutoStart` self-elevate when registering the autostart task at `RunLevel=Highest`. But the standalone CLI subcommand `cua-driver autostart enable` was left as-is — it just calls `Register-ScheduledTask` directly from whatever IL the user's shell is at, which fails with `0x80070005 Access is denied` from a typical non-admin PowerShell.

This patch adds the same self-elevation flow to the Rust CLI: first attempt at current IL, on access-denied trigger a UAC prompt via `Start-Process -Verb RunAs` and re-run `cua-driver autostart enable` inside the elevated child shell.

## UX before/after

| Where | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `install.ps1 -AutoStart` from Medium IL | UAC prompt → registers at Highest ✅ | unchanged ✅ |
| `cua-driver autostart enable` from Medium IL | "Access is denied" error → user has to manually open admin PowerShell ❌ | UAC prompt → registers at Highest ✅ |
| `cua-driver autostart enable` from High IL (admin shell) | Registers at Highest ✅ | unchanged ✅ |

## Implementation

`crates/cua-driver/src/autostart.rs::enable`:
1. First attempt: register directly. Works for any caller already at High IL.
2. If the stderr matches access-denied signatures (`0x80070005`, `"Access is denied"`, `"permission"`, `"requires elevation"`), spawn `powershell -Command "Start-Process -Verb RunAs ..."` which fires the UAC prompt and re-invokes `cua-driver autostart enable` inside the elevated child. The elevated child hits branch (1) and registers cleanly.
3. If the UAC prompt is dismissed → exit non-zero in the child → parent surfaces an actionable error.

The PowerShell `-Verb RunAs` invocation uses `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` so the elevated child's console doesn't flash up.

## Repro / verification

Surfaced during the cuademo fresh-install dogfood: a standard admin user (BUILTIN\Administrators, NOT RID 500, UAC-split-token) ran `cua-driver autostart enable` from their non-elevated PowerShell and got the `0x80070005` error. With this patch, the same invocation triggers a UAC prompt → accept → task registered at `RunLevel=Highest`.

- [x] `cargo check -p cua-driver` clean on the VM (11.26s)
- [ ] End-to-end fresh-install on cuademo with v0.2.11 (requires a follow-up release bump)

## Related

- #1630 (RunLevel=Highest)
- #1631 (OSArchitecture / StrictMode fix)

author: jared-dz
body:
## Summary

- Every Auto-translate run since 2026-03-31 has failed at the final `git push` step — `main` is branch-protected (`GH013: Changes must be made through a pull request`), so the bot can't push translations directly. Four PRs of doc edits (#164, #168, #169, #170) merged without their translations.
- Switches the trigger from `push: main` to `pull_request`, so translations land *inside* the same PR as the English changes and never touch the protected branch.
- Adds a concurrency group, a fork-PR guard, and a loop guard that works for `pull_request` events (the old `head_commit.author` check is null on PR events).

## What changed in `.github/workflows/translate.yml`

- Trigger: `push: main` → `pull_request` (opened, synchronize, reopened) on `docs/**.md`
- Checkout: `ref: ${{ github.head_ref }}` + `fetch-depth: 0` to access the PR base SHA
- Diff base: `HEAD~1` → `${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}`
- Loop guard: `github.event.head_commit.author.name` → `github.actor`
- Added: `github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository` to skip fork PRs (secrets aren't exposed there)
- Added: `concurrency: { group: translate-${{ github.head_ref }}, cancel-in-progress: true }`
- Final step pushes to `HEAD:${{ github.head_ref }}` instead of `main`

`scripts/translate.py` is unchanged — it's already env-driven.

## Test plan

The workflow's `paths:` filter is `docs/**.md`, so this PR won't trigger it. After merge, the first real test is the next PR that touches a doc file.

- [ ] Merge this PR
- [ ] Open a follow-up PR with a one-line edit to any `docs/*.md` file
- [ ] Confirm the "Auto-translate docs" check runs (~7 min for 1 source file × 7 languages)
- [ ] Confirm a `chore: auto-translate docs` commit by `github-actions[bot]` lands on the PR branch with the `.zh/.ja/.ko/.pt/.es/.fr/.it` files
- [ ] Confirm the bot's commit does NOT re-trigger the workflow (`gh run list --workflow=translate.yml` should show only one run for the PR)
- [ ] Push a second commit within ~30s and confirm the first run is cancelled (concurrency)

## Out of scope

- Backlog: `architecture.md` (stale translations) and `contribute-ops-management.md` (no translations) will self-heal next time someone edits them.
- No `workflow_dispatch` manual trigger added — can be retrofitted later if catch-up becomes painful.
- Fork PRs are skipped, not supported via `pull_request_target` (security risk for an internal docs repo).
