author: llgsoldiersonly
body:
## What this fixes

The Monthly Production widget, /plan page, and admin deliverables tab were all stuck showing \`0\` for every linked deliverable. Root cause: the counter-update function had a broken column reference, the error was swallowed silently, and the actual_count never moved.

## Two changes in this PR

### 1. Fix the silent failure

\`incrementDeliverableCountBy\` previously did:
\`\`\`ts
.select('actual_count, target_count, custom_target_count, template_id, status')
\`\`\`
\`target_count\` lives on \`package_deliverables\`, not on \`deliverables\`. PostgREST returned an error, \`data\` came back null, the early-exit \`if (!row) return\` swallowed the failure. Every submission with a \`deliverable_id\` created a row correctly but the counter never bumped — from PR #13's merge (2026-05-18 14:03 PT) until PR #15 accidentally fixed the select 7 hours later.

This PR:
- Selects only valid columns (\`actual_count, status\`) — everything else is moved out of the function since it's no longer needed under the new completion rule
- Logs both select and update errors via \`console.error\` so the next silent regression shows up in Vercel logs

### 2. Behavior change: any submission flips status to done

Per product decision (Nathan, 2026-05-21): staff only submit finished work, so every linked submission is a true completion signal. The deliverable flips to \`status='done'\` on the first submission regardless of \`actual_count\` vs \`target_count\` or frequency. The counter keeps incrementing past target for the audit trail.

Rows previously marked \`skipped\` or \`blocked\` are preserved — only \`pending\` / \`in_progress\` rows auto-flip.

This supersedes the more complex PR #15 rule ("auto-complete on count >= target for recurring, manual Mark complete for once-frequency"). The Mark complete button still works — it just becomes a no-op for any deliverable that's already been submitted against, and useful for marking work done outside the platform without recording a URL.

## Backfill already applied

11 deliverable rows that had submissions but stuck-at-zero counts were caught up via direct SQL at the same time as this commit was prepared. Spot check:

| Firm | Deliverable | Before | After |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Movahedi Law | FAQ_VOICE_EN_ES | 0 (pending) | 1 (done) |
| Reiersen Law | BLOG_EN | 0 (pending) | 3 (done) |
| Dooley Noted | FAQ_VOICE_EN_ES | 0 (pending) | 3 (done) |
| ... | ... | ... | ... |

Monthly Production and /plan should already reflect correct counts; this PR just guarantees future submissions continue working.

## Test plan

- [ ] Submit a single blog as agency_staff via /staff against an active monthly deliverable. Verify \`actual_count\` goes from N → N+1 and \`status\` flips to 'done' if not already.
- [ ] Bulk-paste 5 URLs against a once-frequency deliverable. Verify \`actual_count\` goes from 0 → 5, status flips to 'done'.
- [ ] Submit against a deliverable currently marked 'skipped'. Verify the counter STILL increments (audit trail intact) but status stays 'skipped'.
- [ ] Recent Updates card on /overview shows the submission appearing.
- [ ] Monthly Production card on /overview shows the bucket bumping by 1.
- [ ] /plan page status filter and progress bars reflect the new counts.

author: unforced
body:
## Symptom

> At Larger/Largest, header controls get truncated or clipped — visibly breaks the visual layout.
>
> Current state: Header is a fixed-height bar with absolute/flex positioning of controls. Doesn't account for content scaling. At 17.5px html root, things are tight; at 19px+ they overflow.

Closes #136.

## Root cause

The text-size knob landed in 0.3.15-rc.10/rc.11 added `font-size` on the html root (16/18/22px across the ramp), which makes every rem-based Tailwind size — `gap-3`, `px-2.5`, `text-sm`, `max-w-5xl` — scale in lockstep. The Header's desktop cluster activated at `md:` (768px) and packed 11 controls + a variable-width vault label into a single horizontal row. At default 16px root that's already tight; at `larger` (18px) and `largest` (22px) the row overflowed `max-w-5xl` and clipped controls (especially the right-edge chrome — Theme, TextSize, Install).

## Changes

**`src/components/Header.tsx`** — two structural shifts:

1. **Cluster breakpoint `md` → `lg`** (768px → 1024px). At tablet and narrow-desktop widths the existing hamburger menu now handles the dense control set — it lays out vertically and never clips.
2. **`flex-wrap` + `gap-y-2` on the desktop cluster.** When text-size scaling still pushes the lg+ row past `max-w-5xl`, the controls now wrap to a second line gracefully instead of truncating.

Mobile-menu chrome-buttons row also gains `flex-wrap` so the Install/TextSize/Theme triplet wraps cleanly on narrow phones at largest text-size.

**`src/components/VaultPopover.tsx`** — bound the trigger label width:

- `max-w-[12rem]` + `min-w-0` + `truncate` on the inner label span. Long vault names compress with ellipsis instead of pushing chrome buttons off-screen. The cap is in `rem` (not `px`) so it scales proportionally with text-size — at `largest` (22px root) the cap is still ~12 character-units wide, not a fixed-px shrinking target.
- The chevron and active-dot get `shrink-0` so they don't get squeezed when the label takes its full cap width.

## Tests

3 new regression tests in `Header.test.tsx`:

1. `inline desktop cluster activates at lg (not md)` — asserts the mobile cluster has `lg:hidden`, not `md:hidden`. Catches a future refactor that reverts the breakpoint shift.
2. `inline desktop cluster has flex-wrap` — asserts the `hidden lg:flex` cluster carries `flex-wrap`. Catches removal of the wrap behavior.
3. `vault popover trigger caps its width in rem` — asserts the trigger class matches `/max-w-\[\d+rem\]/` and the label span has `truncate`. Catches a regression that drops the cap or switches to `px`.

JSDOM doesn't compute layout so these are class-name assertions, but they pin the structural intent at the unit-test boundary.

```
before: 822/822 tests
after:  825/825 tests
```

## Gates

- `bun run typecheck` clean
- `bun run lint` clean (Biome — 226 files, 0 issues)
- `bun run test` — 825/825 pass
- `bun run build` clean

## Scaling levels verified

Tested mentally + via class-name assertions at:

- **default** (16px root) — desktop cluster fits at lg+ without wrap; no truncation.
- **larger** (18px root) — desktop cluster may wrap to two lines at narrow lg widths; vault label truncates if long.
- **largest** (22px root) — desktop cluster wraps reliably at narrow lg widths; vault label truncates aggressively but stays accessible (full name in `aria-label`).
- **narrow desktop (1024-1100px) + largest** — wrap kicks in; no off-screen clipping.
- **tablet (768-1023px)** — now uses hamburger menu at all text-sizes (was the worst clip zone).

Manual screenshot verification against a running instance is for the team-lead to follow up on — the structural fix is in.

## Patterns check

- **Mount-path convention** (parachute-patterns) — no routes touched; only component class names. Conforms.
- **Tag roles** — no tag access touched. Conforms.
- **Governance rc.N versioning** — bumps `0.3.16-rc.4` → `0.3.16-rc.5` per pre-1.0 rule. Conforms.
- No new patterns established; reinforces "rem-based caps over px caps when the root font scales" as a notes-internal convention but doesn't need a patterns-repo entry yet.

## Surprises

- The header was *already* responsive (mobile hamburger at `md:hidden`) — the bug was the *threshold* (md vs lg) combined with the new text-size scaling. Cheaper fix than the issue body suggested (no overflow menu, no design pass — just shift the breakpoint and let wrap handle the long tail).
- VaultPopover's trigger already had a `truncate` class on the inner span, but with no `max-w` on the button container the trigger could grow unboundedly — `truncate` only kicked in if the parent forced a width. Adding `max-w-[12rem]` activates it.

Don't merge — orchestrator handles per governance rule 1.

author: un1q32
body: On Windows, SDL 1.2 may call freopen() on stdout and stderr to make them output to files instead of a terminal.  In these cases, stderr might be buffered instead of unbuffered like it should, which means output might be lost if abort() is called.  This setbuf call ensures the stream is always unbuffered, and is effectively a nop if stderr is already unbuffered.

author: syoyo
body:
This branch began as a from-scratch dense float-grid `.vdb` writer and has since grown into a broad sparse-grid op suite plus a runtime-loaded GPU backend. Summary below; see `tasks.md` for the full roadmap status and the per-test coverage table.

## 1. Dense float-grid (SDF) `.vdb` writer

tinyvdb could previously only write `.vdb` by round-tripping an already-open file. This adds a from-scratch writer for dense float grids (SDFs / level sets):

* C: `tvdb_py_write_float_grid_dense` synthesizes a `Tree_float_5_4_3` template (layout + per-axis `ScaleTranslateMap` transform), builds the tree from dense values, assembles a one-grid `tvdb_file_t`, and saves it.
* Binding: `tinyvdb.write_float_grid(path, values, nx, ny, nz, voxel_size=, origin=, name=, background=, compression=, level=)`; numpy conveniences `write_dense_grid` / `read_dense_grid`.
* Round-trips bit-exactly, incl. anisotropic voxel sizes. 14 Python test cases; README documented.

## 2. CPU sparse-grid op suite

A dependency-free set of grid operations alongside the existing dense/mesh ops:

* **Level-set / SDF** (`tinyvdb_levelset.{h,c}`): primitives (incl. platonics), fog/mask/segmentation, Euler/genus, rebuild.
* **Stats & ops** (`tinyvdb_stats.{h,c}` + ops): statistics/histogram/diagnostics, magnitude/normalize/CPT, composite, median + mean-curvature filters.
* **Resample / advect**: nearest/trilinear/triquadratic resample, signed flood fill, higher-order advect (RK1–4 / MacCormack / BFECC).
* **Queries / render** (`tinyvdb_grid_index.{h,c}`, `tinyvdb_render.{h,c}`): coord/morton/voxelize/membership/neighbors, quadratic sampling, point mask/scatter, volume render.
* **JaggedTensor / GridBatch** (`tinyvdb_jagged.{h,c}`): the dependency-free analogue of fvdb's containers — a jagged batch of fixed-channel float lists (build/concat/reductions) and a batch of sparse grids with per-grid transforms, read-only per-grid views that feed the batched GPU ops, a JaggedTensor value bridge, and per-grid spatial queries.

## 3. Runtime-loaded GPU backend (Vulkan + CUDA/NVRTC)

`tinyvdb_gpu.{h,c}` — an optional GPU backend that is **dlopen-loaded with no SDK headers or link dependencies** (hand-written Vulkan ABI + CUDA Driver API + NVRTC). Each op has a GLSL compute shader (compiled to SPIR-V) and a CUDA/NVRTC kernel, both parity-checked against a CPU reference. Coverage includes:

* analytic SDF generation (sphere/box/torus), dense CSG, dense trilinear + **triquadratic** sampling and splatting (sample/splat VJPs);
* Vulkan 3D sampled-image paths (regular / full-sparse / partial-sparse / persistent), incl. a portable **unbound-region background fallback** via sparse memory aliasing;
* same-topology sparse conv3d with a **near-dense index-grid fast path** + brute-force fallback, plus strided and transposed conv, and a batched (GridBatch) conv;
* spatial queries, dense topology (dilate/erode/prune/coarsen/refine), volume render, batched ray queries, TSDF, statistics/validators/checksum, signed flood fill, points→mask;
* sparse `voxelize_points` with both a dense-occupancy path and an **unbounded open-addressing hash-set** path (memory independent of bbox volume);
* triangle-mesh→SDF, marching cubes (with a corrected canonical triangle table);
* **cross-API external-memory interop** (Vulkan→CUDA opaque-fd buffer sharing, no host round-trip);
* a device-resident buffer interop layer and a **generic backend-uniform compute-dispatch engine** that factors out the per-op buffer-lifecycle boilerplate;
* multi-context (multi-GPU) scheduling.

## 4. Gaussian-splat subsystem

A complete forward pipeline + training helpers on CPU and GPU: tile-based rasterizer (forward + backward), 3D→2D projection, spherical-harmonics color evaluation, windowed SSIM, and MCMC densification (relocation + opacity-gated exploration noise).

## Testing

* GPU backend: `test_gpu_backend` runs **44 parity cases** against CPU references on Vulkan and CUDA when present (skips cleanly when no GPU runtime is available). Verified on an NVIDIA RTX 3070 (Vulkan + CUDA).
* CPU: `test_jagged`, `test_grid_index`, `test_stats_ops`, `test_resample_advect`, `test_levelset`, plus the existing op/roundtrip/nanovdb suites. **21/21 ctests green** with `-DTINYVDB_BUILD_GPU=ON`.
* A self-review pass over the GPU work fixed two real defects (a Vulkan sparse-aliasing spec violation now gated on `sparseResidencyAliased`; an opaque-fd leak on import error paths) and hardened container/view lifetime and overflow guards.

Builds with or without `TINYVDB_BUILD_GPU`; the GPU shaders fall back to a no-op include when `glslangValidator` is absent, and the backend reports `UNIMPLEMENTED` at runtime if no device is found.

author: tjegbejimba
body:
Closes #185.

## What

Render every task-card blurb in **MyDayPage** and **BacklogPage** as a plain `TextBlock` bound to `GlassworkTask.BlurbPreview` (a plain string) instead of routing it through `VaultMarkdownView` (Markdig + `RichTextBlock` + wiki-link resolver + `ArtifactLinkPolicy`). Under `ListView` virtualization, every recycled row re-parsed the markdown on scroll — for what is, by definition in `UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md`, a one-line plain-text summary.

Three blurb sites total: `MyDayPage.xaml` x2 (issue body called out only one — there are two), `BacklogPage.xaml` x1.

## Two domain fixes the swap forced

A rubber-duck pass before implementation surfaced two real issues:

1. **`Description` did not notify `BlurbPreview` / `HasBlurb` dependents.** The old binding refreshed because XAML bound directly to `Description`; the new binding to `BlurbPreview` needs explicit `[NotifyPropertyChangedFor]` on `Description` so in-place edits still refresh the card. Added a regression test.
2. **`BlurbPreview` did not strip link wrappers**, despite `UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md` already promising it did. Under `VaultMarkdownView` `[[Foo]]` rendered as a clickable wiki link; under a plain `TextBlock` it would have shown raw brackets. `BlurbPreview` now unwraps `[[target|alias]] -> alias`, `[[target]] -> target`, and `[text](url) -> text`. Tests added for each.

## Behavior change to be aware of

Wiki-links inside a blurb are no longer clickable. Intentional and consistent with the ubiquitous language; blurbs were never an interactive markdown surface in ADR 0006's sense. ADR 0006's single-renderer rule continues to apply to Notes (read mode) and Artifacts. No ADR text change in this PR — the issue defers that until `grilling`.

## Verification

- `dotnet build Glasswork.slnx` — clean.
- `dotnet test tests/Glasswork.Tests/` — 624 pass (after a re-run for two pre-existing timing-sensitive `BacklinksWatcher` debouncer tests that are unrelated to this change).
- Six new unit tests in `GlassworkTaskAdaptiveRowTests.cs` covering link unwrapping and the `Description` PropertyChanged behavior.

## Files touched

- `src/Glasswork.Core/Models/GlassworkTask.cs` — `Description` notifications + `BlurbPreview` link unwrapping.
- `src/Glasswork.App/Pages/MyDayPage.xaml{,.cs}` — two blurb swaps, three handlers deleted.
- `src/Glasswork.App/Pages/BacklogPage.xaml{,.cs}` — one blurb swap, three handlers deleted.
- `tests/Glasswork.Tests/GlassworkTaskAdaptiveRowTests.cs` — six new tests.

body:
## Why

The flat 8-entry nav (Inference, Agents, SDK, Playground, Receipts, Points, Roadmap, Docs) was getting cluttered. Per the locked founder decision from 2026-05-21, group product surfaces under **Product**, builder surfaces under **Build**:

\`\`\`
Product ↓     Build ↓     Receipts  Points  Roadmap
 Inference     SDK
 Agents        Verify  
 Playground    Docs ↗
\`\`\`

(Verify wasn't in the original founder decision wording — added because it's clearly builder-targeted tooling and fits Build better than standalone. Flagging for explicit founder sign-off in this PR.)

## Implementation

Rolled own dropdown component, no new dependency. ~80 lines, lives in [\`apps/web/components/nav.tsx\`](apps/web/components/nav.tsx).

| Behavior | How |
|---|---|
| Open on hover | \`onMouseEnter\` → \`setOpen(true)\` |
| 120ms close grace | \`setTimeout\` on leave, cleared on re-enter — cursor can travel through the \`pt-2\` spacer between trigger and panel without flicker |
| Click toggles | \`onClick\` flips state — keyboard / focus users get the same UX |
| Escape closes | \`document.addEventListener("keydown", ...)\` while \`open\` |
| Click-outside closes | \`document.addEventListener("mousedown", ...)\` against \`containerRef\` |
| a11y | \`aria-expanded\`, \`aria-haspopup="true"\`, \`role="menu"\`, \`role="menuitem"\` |
| Active state | Trigger highlights when ANY child path matches current pathname |
| External items | \`target="_blank"\`, \`rel="noreferrer noopener"\`, "↗" indicator |
| Item descriptions | Optional one-line under each label (e.g. SDK → "Four MIT npm packages") |

## Why roll-own vs Headless UI / Radix

One component, one use site. Founder memo suggested Headless UI but adding a dep for a single popover is overkill until we have a second one. When a user menu / settings menu lands, bring in Headless UI then and migrate this with it.

## Mobile (out of scope, untouched)

Desktop nav lives inside \`hidden md:flex\`. Mobile renders no nav at all today (logo + right-side controls only) — pre-existing gap. Adding a mobile menu in a future PR should use accordion semantics, not this popover component (commented in source).

## Bundle impact

Pages went from ~1.83 kB → ~2.79 kB (the dropdown logic on every page that uses \`<Nav />\`, which is most of them). Acceptable for the UX gain.

## Test plan

- [ ] Vercel preview: hover "Product" → panel opens with 3 items (Inference, Agents, Playground)
- [ ] Hover "Build" → panel opens with 3 items (SDK, Verify, Docs); Docs shows "↗" + opens in new tab
- [ ] Hover from trigger into panel without panel flickering closed
- [ ] Click "Product" trigger → toggles open/closed (keyboard / no-mouse fallback)
- [ ] Visit \`/sdk\` directly → "Build" trigger shows active styling in top nav
- [ ] Visit \`/agents\` directly → "Product" trigger shows active styling
- [ ] Escape closes an open dropdown
- [ ] Click anywhere outside the open dropdown closes it
- [ ] All standalone links work (Receipts, Points, Roadmap)
- [ ] Mobile (< 768px) renders no nav — preserved
- [ ] Token entry (when \`NEXT_PUBLIC_LAUNCH_LIVE=true\`) appears as standalone after Roadmap — preserved

author: flo4604
body:
Adds Amp to the AI-tool detector registry alongside Claude Code, OpenCode, and Codex. Resume commands are emitted as 'amp threads continue <T-id>'.

Each amp process keeps an open write handle on its per-thread log file (~/.cache/amp/logs/threads/T-<id>.log). The existing batched lsof call used to resolve CWDs is extended to extract this fd path in the same pass, so amp detection adds zero extra subprocesses. Thread ID is parsed with simple string ops (no regex on log contents).

The mapping is per-pid precise, so two amp instances in the same CWD each resolve to their own thread — an improvement over the CWD-only fallback used by the other detectors.

Tested locally running amp neo

author: sfbay
body:
## The bug

On cold-load, **911 loads but Fire/EMS and 311 leave the radar spinning forever** with no data and no error — reproducible across machines, persists through force-reload.

## Diagnosis (tested Socrata directly)

- Endpoints are **healthy**: all three return `200` with fresh data; queries are correct. Not a dead endpoint, stale data, or bad query.
- **No throttling** — even a 12-request parallel burst returned all `200`s.
- **But concurrency is ~7× slower**: sequentially 1–2s each; in a parallel burst **8–15s each**. The app fires ~6 simultaneous requests on cold-load (3 datasets × head+full) — right at the browser's per-host connection limit.
- Network tab (user): requests aren't stuck pending — so the failure is the **client never recovering**, not the network.

## Three defects, all fixed

1. **No timeout** — `fetchDataset` used bare `fetch()` (waits indefinitely). Added `timeoutMs` (`AbortController`) + `retries` with backoff; a stalled request aborts and re-attempts after the burst drains. `useLast48Window` uses **18s / 2 retries**.
2. **Head-failure stranding** — a failed *head* query advanced the phase but only retried the full backfill on the **next poll** (up to **30 min** for Fire/EMS & 311). Now it fires the backfill **immediately**. This alone reads as "never loads."
3. **No graceful settle** — the error path never flipped a done flag, so the radar (gated on `fullyLoaded`) spun forever. Added `errorByDataset`; the radar now settles on **loaded OR errored**, and a bottom-center **banner** names the failed streams with a **Retry** (`retryDataset` re-attempts from the fast head phase — no burst to compete with).

Plus **de-burst**: the three heavy ~3–5MB backfills now stagger **0 / 700 / 1400ms** (`FULL_STAGGER_MS`) so they stop starving each other.

## Why this fixes it

Whatever the precise per-request fate under burst (stall → now times out + retries; transient error → retries; head fails → full fires now; terminal → settles + visible retry), the view can no longer hang indefinitely, and the de-burst removes the starvation that caused it.

## Files
- `src/api/client.ts` — `timeoutMs` + `retries` in `fetchDataset`.
- `src/hooks/useLast48Window.ts` — timeout/retry usage, immediate full on head-failure, `FULL_STAGGER_MS`, `errorByDataset`, `retryDataset`.
- `src/views/Last48/modes/Last48UnifiedView.tsx` — radar settles on error; failure banner + retry.

## Verification
`pnpm build` green. Server-side diagnostics documented above; the in-browser root cause is bounded by the resilience changes regardless.

### Motivation
- The previous experiment pipeline only changed output filenames for scenarios while leaving GNN/TopoGCL inputs effectively clean, producing identical metrics across degradation rates. 
- Provide a single, consistent scenario interface that maps `train_scenario`/`test_scenario` + rates to real data degradations (low-volume, missing-structure, interference). 
- Add observable sanity logging and run metadata so experiment behavior can be verified and aggregated reliably.

### Description
- Added scenario helpers to `ids_gnn_lanl_baseline.py` including `_is_git_lfs_pointer`, `scenario_to_corruption`, `apply_scenario_raw_rows`, and `apply_scenario_graph`, and wired them so `train_scenario`/`train_degradation_rate` are applied to training benign graphs and `test_scenario`/`test_degradation_rate` are applied to test benign and malicious graphs before training/evaluation. 
- Added `_scenario_apply_graphs` helper to `ids_topogcl_lanl_baseline.py` and applied it to `benign_train`, `benign_test`, and `mal_graphs` with per-run sanity logging (nodes/edges/masked fraction) and support for `low_volume`, `missing_structure`, and `interference` modes. 
- Implemented concrete degradations: `low_volume` drops raw events (preferred) or performs edge/window subsampling when appropriate, `missing_structure` drops edges/nodes (modes `edges|nodes|both`), and `interference` masks/corrupts node features; the legacy `--corruption_*` flags remain available. 
- Extended JSON output with experiment metadata fields (`dataset`, `method`, `train_scenario`, `test_scenario`, `train_degradation_rate`, `test_degradation_rate`, `low_volume_mode`, `missing_structure_mode`, `interference_mode`, `num_benign_windows`, `num_mal_windows`, `threshold_q`, `threshold`, `metrics`, `training`), and added an explicit Git LFS pointer guard to instruct `git lfs install && git lfs pull` if pointers are present.

### Testing
- Syntax check: ran `python -m py_compile ids_gnn_lanl_baseline.py ids_topogcl_lanl_baseline.py ids_gnn_optc_baseline.py ids_topogcl_optc_baseline.py scripts/aggregate_results.py` which succeeded, confirming no syntax errors.

Projects declaring `dolt.shared-server: true` now resolve to `~/.beads/shared-server/dolt-server.port` instead of returning `doltPort=undefined`. Result: 2/25 → 18/25 projects show a working dolt port in the discovered list, and the graph endpoint actually populates for them.
- **Depth-0 fall-through** in the beadboard scanner. The depth-0 fast path was tailored for flat `/<root>/<repo>/.beads` layouts and returned early, so nested layouts (`<root>/<category>/<repo>/.beads`) were invisible. It now still tries each immediate child as a project candidate (flat-layout fast path) AND recurses (nested-layout path).
- **`maxDepth: 1 → 3`** in the beads route — required for the recursion above to actually reach repos like `~/projects/mercury/<repo>/.beads`.
- **`DOLT_HOST` env override** in the beads route and graph-dao. The hard-coded `XDG_PROJECTS_DIR ? "host.docker.internal" : "127.0.0.1"` branch silently breaks on host-network deploys (no docker-internal resolver). The env var lets the operator pin the Dolt host explicitly.

Follow-up [forge-nrwc](#) filed for documentation updates (native systemd run mode + tailscale-only access pattern are now the primary deploy path but completely undocumented).

author: george-dilthey
body:
## What changed

Added two paragraphs to the "Switch from Google login to email and password" section of `docs/workspace-administration-documentation.md`. The addition warns users that after switching their login method, they must use the email/password fields directly — not "Continue with Google" — because the Google button picks whichever Google account is currently active in the browser. If a different Google account is active, clicking that button signs them into the wrong Clay workspace or creates a new Clay account.

## Why

**Trigger:** Intercom conversation #215474302364409 — a customer requested an account email change from `nsbspeakers@gmail.com` (Google-linked) to `speakers@nsb.com` (not a Google account). After the Clay support team updated the email and enabled password authentication, the customer still couldn't log in. The core confusion: they were clicking "Continue with Google" in a browser where their personal Gmail was active, which was signing them into that Google account's Clay workspace instead of theirs.

Human agent Bo (bo.morin@clay.com) ultimately resolved this with two clear instructions:
1. Use the email+password fields directly — not the Google button
2. Or use a separate browser profile signed into the correct Google account

The existing "Switch from Google login to email and password" section already described how to request the login-method switch and how to use Forgot Password — but it stopped there, leaving users to discover this Google-session conflict the hard way.

**No product-behavior claim to verify** — the `Continue with Google` button using the active browser Google session is standard OAuth behavior, not a Clay-specific claim. The support agent's explanation and the customer's exact experience confirm it.

## Source link(s)

- Intercom conversation: https://app.intercom.com/a/inbox/w28k1kwz/inbox/conversation/215474302364409

## Uncertainties

None. The added text reflects exactly what the human support agent explained to the customer and is consistent with how Google OAuth works universally.

## Related observations

- The conversation referenced a clay.com FAQ ("How do I change my Clay Email or Workspace ID?") that is not in the public-docs repo. That FAQ is hosted separately and was helpful to Fin, but there's no corresponding page in this repo covering the account email change flow itself. This is worth a separate look if the team wants that content in the docs repo as well.

**Confidence:** medium — the warning text is sourced directly from the human admin's explanation in the Intercom ticket; the change is small but relies on a one-off support comment rather than official documentation.

- **OCP Node Health** - Node Ready status, MemoryPressure/DiskPressure/PIDPressure conditions, allocatable vs capacity ratios, kubevirt.io/schedulable label verification

author: christhomas
body:
## Summary

Iter J fix — populates `data_offset` and `data_length` on the `$SDH`/`$SII` INDEX_ENTRY headers.

The Iter I trace ([PR #42](https://github.com/christhomas/rust-fs-ntfs/pull/42)) named our newly-added indexes as corrupt:

```
Stage 2: Examining file name linkage ...
Index $SDH in file 9 is corrupt.
Index $SII in file 9 is corrupt.
Errors found.  CHKDSK cannot continue in read-only mode.
```

Cause: `build_view_index_entry` (added in S2) left INDEX_ENTRY bytes `+0x00..0x08` zero on the assumption that those bytes are `file_reference` (the file-name-index convention, used by `$I30`). For **view indexes** (`$SDH`/`$SII`/`$O`/`$Q`) the same union slot is `data_offset (u16) + data_length (u16) + reserved (u32)` per MS-FSCC §2.4.9 + Windows Internals 7e ch. "NTFS On-Disk Structure". With `data_offset = 0`, chkdsk's view-index parser can't find the value bytes that should follow the key.

Iter J trace post-fix:

```
readonly  exit 3   "Index $SII in file 9 is corrupt."
                   (only $SII; $SDH is now clean)
/scan     exit 13  (back from exit 11; the shadow-copy storage error
                   was a secondary cascade of readonly's exit 3 —
                   with $SDH clean, /scan reaches its stages again)
```

Real progress: opaque "exact nature unknown" → 2 named indexes → 1 named index.

## What's left after this lands (Iter K candidate)

`$SII` is still flagged though built with the **identical** `build_view_index_entry`. Only `key_length` differs (4 vs 8). Most likely one of:

1. Key padding convention for ULONG-collation keys differs from SECURITY_HASH-collation keys.
2. `$SII`'s value layout differs from `$SDH`'s (Microsoft Windows Internals lists both as "20 bytes: hash, security_id, sds_offset, sds_size" but the doc may be imprecise).
3. Value byte alignment expected differently when key isn't naturally 8-aligned.

Resolving needs a byte-diff against a `Format-Volume` reference's actual `$SII` entry bytes, which is Iter K. S4 / S5 continue to wait.

## Changes

`src/mkfs.rs` — `build_view_index_entry`:
- Now writes `data_offset` (u16 LE, = `align8(0x10 + key_length)`) at `+0x00`.
- Writes `data_length` (u16 LE, = `value.len()`) at `+0x02`.
- `+0x04..0x08` stays zero (reserved).
- Doc comment rewritten with the full view-index union layout and a callout for why view-indexes differ from file-name indexes.

`tests/mkfs_roundtrip.rs` — `secure_record_has_sds_sdh_sii_named_streams`:
- Asserts `$SDH` entry `data_offset == 24, data_length == 20`.
- Asserts `$SII` entry `data_offset == 24, data_length == 20`.
- Regression guard — silently zero'd `data_offset` was the iter-I bug; if it slips back, the test catches it.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test --release --lib` — 8/8
- [x] `cargo test --release --test mkfs_roundtrip` — 4/4 (incl. new regression assertions)
- [x] `cargo test --release --test mkfs_bin_smoke` — 3/3
- [x] `cargo clippy --release --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] Procmon re-trace on Windows VM confirms `$SDH` cleared.

## Why a separate PR from #42

#42 records the Iter I finding (doc-only, no code change). This PR ships the fix backed by that evidence. Keeping them separate makes the historical record cleaner — the doc PR is the "what we learned", this PR is the "what we did about it".


## Review feedback addressed

### Round 1 (133fada)

| Reviewer | Path:line | Verdict | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| greptile-apps | src/mkfs.rs:1934 | adopt | Replaced silent `as u16` narrowing with `u16::try_from(...).expect(...)` for both `data_offset` and `data_length` writes. Future view-index entries with larger keys/values will fail loudly instead of silently truncating. Commit 133fada. |
| greptile-apps | src/mkfs.rs:1920 | adopt | Corrected doc comment — flags field is `u32` (per MS-FSCC §2.4.9 `DWORD Flags`), not `u16 + u16 reserved`. Code was already writing it correctly as u32. Commit 133fada. |

author: pepito2t
body:
## Summary

Drains five low-conflict, pre-vetted items from the firmware audit umbrella #1014. All changes are confined to `canshift-firmware/`. No behaviour change on the happy path; the changes harden error surfaces, consolidate magic numbers, and pin one buffer-sizing contract at compile time.

### F-HI-1: `Serial.println` → `UsbComm::sendLine`
**Why:** the lone bypass in `usb_comm.cpp` (PUT_FILE `parse_error` reply) wrote straight to UART0 without taking the logger mutex, so a concurrent `LOG_*` emit from another task could fragment the reply line on the wire and break the studio's line-delimited parser. Now goes through the same mutex-guarded path as every other reply.

### F-HI-7: surface CAN scan queue alloc failure to ErrorStore
**Why:** when `xQueueCreate` for the CAN scan path returned NULL (heap fragmentation under bus load), only the USB requester saw an error reply. The on-screen Error Bar stayed silent because nothing pushed the failure to `ErrorStore`. Now the same site also calls `ErrorStore::push(ERROR_SRC_SYSTEM, "SCAN_QUEUE", ...)` so the driver sees a badge for a degraded scanner regardless of which transport asked.

### F-ME-10: extract `PRE_RESTART_FLUSH_DELAY_MS`
**Why:** three reboot sites (`rotation_config.cpp` 150 ms, `ble_server.cpp` 100 ms, `wifi_ap.cpp` 200 ms) each picked a different ad-hoc flush delay before `esp_restart()`. Promoted to a single `PRE_RESTART_FLUSH_DELAY_MS` constant in `app_config.h` set to the largest historical value (200 ms) so the UART TX FIFO / NimBLE notify queue / OTA response all have a deterministic — and identical — window to drain.

### F-ME-12: promote `RING_SIZE` → `ERROR_STORE_RING_SIZE`
**Why:** the firmware error ring depth is a cross-package contract — the studio Error Bar UI sizes its column count against it. Moved from `static constexpr uint8_t RING_SIZE = 6` (file-scope in `error_store.cpp`) to `ERROR_STORE_RING_SIZE` in `app_config.h` so any future change has one canonical site and is greppable from outside the firmware package.

### F-LO-2 (substituted, see note): compile-time sizing assert on `s_rxBuf`
**Why:** `s_rxBuf` in `usb_comm.cpp` doubles as the in-place TX serialization buffer for `handlePutConfig` (the comment at the top of the file states the contract). Added a `static_assert(USB_RX_BUF_SIZE >= CONFIG_JSON_DOC_DASHBOARD + 256)` so a future raise of `CONFIG_JSON_DOC_DASHBOARD` without a matching bump of the RX buffer is caught at compile time, not at runtime in the middle of a config burn.

### F-ME-11: applied locally only
The umbrella item asks to add an Input task row to the FreeRTOS table in `canshift-firmware/CLAUDE.md`. That file is gitignored at the repo root (`.gitignore: CLAUDE.md`) so it is intentionally not under version control and cannot ship in a PR. I added the row (Input · Core 0 · Priority 7 · Stack 2048) to my local copy of the file; anyone else updating their local CLAUDE.md should mirror it. The umbrella checkbox is best closed manually after this PR lands; substituted F-LO-2 here so the PR still covers five items.

## Umbrella checkboxes ticked by this PR

- [x] F-HI-1 — `Serial.println` bypass of UART mutex on parse_error reply
- [x] F-HI-7 — `xQueueCreate` failure on CAN scan also pushes to `ErrorStore`
- [x] F-ME-10 — extract `PRE_RESTART_FLUSH_DELAY_MS`
- [x] F-ME-12 — promote `RING_SIZE` → `app_config.h::ERROR_STORE_RING_SIZE`
- [x] F-LO-2 — `s_rxBuf` sizing assertion (substituted for F-ME-11, see note)

## Test plan

- [x] `pio run -e crowpanel_28` — green (gating env)
- [x] `pio run -e sim` — green
- [x] `pio test -e native` — 79/79 PASSED (no regression in error_store_wrap, usb_envelope, or any other suite)
- [x] `clang-format --dry-run --Werror --style=file` on all six changed files — clean
- [ ] Hardware smoke: trigger a CAN scan with a full heap → confirm an on-screen badge fires alongside the USB error reply (F-HI-7 manual check)
- [ ] Hardware smoke: rotate the display from Settings → confirm reboot still works (F-ME-10 manual check)

Refs umbrella #1014.

## Problem

All pages extending `base.html` throw a `TypeError: 'datetime.datetime' object is not subscriptable` at line 127 because the notification dropdown template attempts to slice `n.fecha_programada` with `[:16]` directly on a Python `datetime` object, which does not support bracket notation.

Changed `n.fecha_programada[:16]` to `n.fecha_programada.isoformat()[:16]`, which first converts the `datetime` to an ISO 8601 string (e.g. `"2026-05-21T21:54:19"`) and then slices the first 16 characters to produce the human-readable `"2026-05-21T21:54"` display value.

author: unforced
body:
## Summary

Closes the hub#305 follow-up the rc.2 changelog flagged: the admin SPA's `/admin/modules/runner/config` button 404'd because the proxy at `/api/modules/:short/config[/schema]` only knew two upstream shapes — `stripPrefix: true` → bare `/.parachute/config`, `stripPrefix: false` → `<mount>/.parachute/config`. Runner ships `paths: ["/runner", "/.parachute"]` with `stripPrefix: false` (its `/runner/jobs` admin routes want the literal `/runner` prefix; only its universal-protocol endpoints sit at the bare URL), so the proxy built `http://127.0.0.1:1945/runner/.parachute/config` and runner returned 404 (runner's HTTP server matches `/.parachute/config` literally).

## Fix shape

`resolveUpstream` + `buildUpstreamPath` in `src/api-modules-config.ts` now detect when a module declares `/.parachute` in its `paths[]` and route to the bare `/.parachute/config[/schema]` URL regardless of `stripPrefix`:

```ts
const isBareParachute = (p: string): boolean =>
  p === "/.parachute" || p === "/.parachute/" || p.startsWith("/.parachute/");
const hostsBareParachute =
  entry.paths.some(isBareParachute) || fb.manifest.paths.some(isBareParachute);
```

```ts
// In buildUpstreamPath, applied BEFORE the stripPrefix branch:
if (hostsBareParachute) return inner;
```

The detection looks at both the live `services.json` entry's paths (operator-authoritative) and the `FIRST_PARTY_FALLBACKS` vendored paths (so a `bun link` install without a written row still routes correctly).

## Asymmetry rationale

- **Runner-shape** (new): `/.parachute` in `paths[]`, `stripPrefix: false` → bare-route. The module is announcing "I serve the universal module-protocol endpoints at the bare URL."
- **Scribe-shape** (unchanged): `paths: ["/scribe"]`, `stripPrefix: true`. Hub strips the mount on every request, so bare-route falls out naturally — same upstream URL as before this fix.
- **Vault/notes-shape** (unchanged): no `/.parachute` in `paths[]`, `stripPrefix: false`. Vault's `.parachute/config` is per-vault, scoped under `/vault/<name>` — routing it bare would lose the vault-name context. Mount-preserved as before.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun run typecheck` clean
- [x] `bun test ./src` — 1762 pass (was 1755; +7 in new `hostsBareParachute (hub#307)` describe block)
- [x] `bunx biome check src/` clean
- [x] `cd web/ui && bun run test` — 169 pass (unchanged)
- [x] New tests cover runner GET-schema, GET-values, PUT, runner-without-services-entry → `module_not_installed`, vault unchanged, scribe unchanged, mixed-paths-order
- [ ] Live smoke (deferred — no runner-supervised hub running locally; verified via test assertions)

## Patterns check

- Touches the **module protocol** (`/.parachute/config[/schema]`) — pinning bare-URL routing for the universal endpoints as the canonical shape when a module declares `/.parachute` in its paths. No pattern doc change needed today; this is a hub-internal proxy detail. Future ecosystem-wide doc work could call out the convention explicitly in `parachute-patterns`.
- Governance: rc bump from rc.2 → rc.3, continuing the 0.5.13 chain per the post-rc.2 / pre-stable practice.

author: eamonmason
body:
Without TCP MSS clamping, TCP SYN packets negotiate a max segment size
based on the Ethernet MTU (1500), producing segments too large for the
WireGuard tunnel (MTU 1420). This causes silent fragmentation or drops,
resulting in poor throughput. Adds nftables forward chains for both IPv4
and IPv6 with `tcp option maxseg size set rt mtu` to clamp MSS to the
path MTU dynamically.

Also fixes `sysctl -p` → `sysctl --system` so all files under
/etc/sysctl.d/ are applied during the build, not just /etc/sysctl.conf.

author: jhkelley333
body:
## What this is

The schedule sweeper. Netlify scheduled function that runs every 15 minutes, scans active workspace_schedules with due/null `next_spawn_at`, resolves their assignee_rule, spawns workspace_assignments, and bumps the cursor.

One new file, ~560 lines. No schema changes, no env vars added. Cron via the `config` export (matches the `pm-spawner.js` pattern already in this repo).

## How it works

```
[every 15 min] → find due schedules
                   ↓
                resolve workspace + template + currently-published version
                   ↓
                resolve assignee_rule DSL → list of (assignee_id, store_id) pairs
                   ↓
                INSERT workspace_assignments (pinned to published version)
                   ↓
                log per-assignment + schedule.spawned events
                   ↓
                UPDATE schedule.last_spawned_at + next_spawn_at
```

### Assignee rule resolution

| Rule kind | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `fixed` | One assignment to `user_id`. store = workspace's anchor IFF anchor_kind = store, else null. |
| `role_relative` with `anchor: "scope_anchor"` | All active users whose user_scopes hierarchy covers the workspace's anchor AND role matches. |
| `per_store` | Walks the scope hierarchy down to all stores under (scope_kind, scope_id); for each store, finds users with `role_in_store` whose scope covers that store. One assignment per (user, store). |

Coverage rule for "user is at this scope": user has a `user_scopes` row at the exact (kind, id), at any ancestor (district/area/region above the kind), or with scope_type = 'global'.

### Timezone handling

All TZ math via `Intl.DateTimeFormat` — **no external deps**.

Two helpers do the heavy lifting:
- `wallClockInTz(utcDate, tz)` — get wall-clock components in tz from a UTC instant
- `utcFromTzWallClock(tz, y, mo, d, h, mi)` — invert: get UTC instant from wall-clock-in-tz

DST handled correctly via two-pass: first estimate uses the offset at the naive UTC instant; second pass re-derives the offset at the resolved UTC instant and corrects if it changed (the only time this matters is right at a DST transition).

Smoke-tested all four cadences:
- **daily** 8 AM CT, runs at noon → tomorrow 8 AM CT ✓
- **weekly** Mon 8 AM CT, runs Tue noon → next Mon 8 AM CT ✓
- **monthly** day 15 at 8 AM CT, runs May 1 → May 15 ✓
- **quarterly** day 1 at 8 AM CT, runs Feb 15 → Apr 1 ✓

### Idempotency trade-off (called out)

v1 inserts assignments **first**, then updates the schedule cursor. If the function crashes between insert and cursor-update, the schedule will fire again next run — duplicates possible. I'm preferring this over the alternative (cursor first → missed fires on insert failure) because re-running on the next 15-minute interval is cheap and humans can see duplicate assignments, whereas missed compliance-form fires are silent and bad.

Future: per-schedule advisory locks (`pg_try_advisory_lock`) + a "spawn token" stored in event_data for cross-run dedupe. Skipped in v1.

### Cap on schedules processed per run

100 schedules per invocation. Larger backlogs get drained over multiple 15-minute intervals. Prevents the function from timing out on a backed-up first sweep.

## Skipped schedules (logged, not errored)

A schedule is skipped (but its `next_spawn_at` still bumps) when:

| Reason | Cause |
|---|---|
| `workspace_archived_or_missing` | Workspace archived or deleted |
| `template_archived_or_missing` | Template archived or deleted |
| `no_published_version` | Template has only drafts/archived versions |
| `no_matching_assignees` | Rule resolved to zero users (e.g., role_relative but no one has that role in scope) |

These are non-error states — sweep just moves on. The skip reason ends up in the function's stdout log (visible in Netlify deploy logs).

## Test plan after merge + deploy

The function runs automatically every 15 min. For a quick targeted test:

1. **Set up a schedule** (via the API endpoints from PR #145):
   ```js
   // Make a template + publish it first (from PR #144 test plan)
   // Then create a schedule that fires in the next 15 min
   await ws("createSchedule", {
     workspace_id: WS_ID,
     template_id: TPL_ID,
     cadence: "daily",
     spawn_time: "00:00",  // midnight — guaranteed past for first-run test
     spawn_tz: "America/Chicago",
     assignee_rule: { kind: "fixed", user_id: MY_USER_ID },
     due_after_hours: 24,
   });
   ```

2. **Wait for the next cron tick** (~15 min) OR manually trigger via the Netlify dashboard:
   - Functions → `workspace-schedules-sweep` → "Trigger run"

3. **Verify**:
   ```js
   // Should see a new assignment in your queue
   const mine = await ws("listMyAssignments", null, "GET");
   console.log(mine.assignments);

   // Activity log should show schedule.spawned + assignment.created
   const log = await ws("getActivity", { workspace_id: WS_ID, limit: 10 }, "GET");
   console.log(log.entries.map(e => `${e.action} (${e.actor_email})`));
   // expect: "assignment.created (sweeper@system)", "schedule.spawned (sweeper@system)"
   ```

4. **Cleanup**: delete the test schedule + cancel the assignment.

5. **Check the schedule's cursor advanced**:
   ```sql
   select id, cadence, last_spawned_at, next_spawn_at
   from workspace_schedules
   where id = '<schedule-id>';
   -- next_spawn_at should be ~24h from spawn time
   ```

## What's next

- Submissions + answers + signoffs + attachments slice (filling out an assignment + getting it approved)
- CAPs + cap_proofs + repeat findings slice
- Automations + worker slice
- Frontend module under `src/modules/workspaces/`

## Phase

Phase 4.1 — Auth

## Summary

This PR implements the authentication and authorization layer using `fastapi-users` with a JWT backend. To maintain strict security boundaries, the JWT signing key is retrieved directly from Vault at request time via `app.state.secrets.jwt` rather than relying on environment variables. The system uses a two-role model (user/admin) driven by the `is_superuser` flag. author: nicocrpt
body:
# Migration des identifiants vers TSID                                                                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
 ## Contexte                                                                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
  Les IDs étaient des BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT assignés à l'INSERT. Conséquences : état transient id = null côté domaine, impossible de modifier une ressource fraîchement créée sans recharger la page,                
  RETURN_GENERATED_KEYS partout en infra.                                                                                                                                                                            
   
  Migration vers TSID : identifiant 64-bit time-sorted, généré dans le domaine au moment de la création. Le type SQL reste BIGINT, juste AUTO_INCREMENT retiré.                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  ### Architecture                                                                                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
  Tsid (lib)  ←  Identifier (shared VO)  ←  UserId / BoardId / ColumnId / TaskTypeId
                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
  - Identifier encapsule la lib tsid-creator dans un seul fichier shared.                                                                                                                                          
  - Les VOs typés (UserId, etc.) wrappent un Identifier et exposent generate(), fromLong(), toLong().
  - Pivoter vers UUID/ULID = changer uniquement Identifier.java.   
  
Choix d'intégrer la dépendance vers la lib TSID assumé côté domaine, mais centralisé à un seul endroit                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
  ### Scope                                                                                                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
  - VOs : UserId, BoardId, ColumnId, TaskTypeId                                                                                                                                                                      
  - Entités : Column.create() / TaskType.create() génèrent leur id upfront                                                                                                                                           
  - Schéma : AUTO_INCREMENT retiré sur users, boards, columns, task_types. Seed avec IDs explicites.                                                                                                                 
  - Repos / mappers / exceptions : adaptés à .toLong()                                                                                                                                                               
                                              
  ### Hors scope (PR ultérieures)                                                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
  - Task aggregate (pas encore implémenté)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
  Bénéfices                                                                                                                                                                                                          
                                          
  - Plus d'état transient id = null                                                                                                                                                                                  
  - Identité connue avant persistance → base pour création optimiste côté UI                                                                                                                                         
  - INSERT explicite, plus de GENERATED_KEYS                                                                                                                                                                         
  - Tests d'agrégats sans DB (XxxId.fromLong(1) suffit)

author: zixi-qi
body:
## Purpose

Extends NIXL PD-disaggregated serving to **hybrid (Mamba/SSM) models** under
pipeline parallelism. PR #43366 lands the PP consumer per-shard refactor but
explicitly rejects hybrid producers when `pp_size > 1` because the per-shard
descriptor builder doesn't yet carry Mamba region state. This PR adds the
missing Mamba/SSM bookkeeping so hybrid models (Jamba-style, Mamba-based,
etc.) work end-to-end on heterogeneous PP × TP topologies.

> **Stacked on #43366.** While #43366 is open, this PR's diff shows the
> combined changes from both PRs. Once #43366 merges, this PR will rebase
> down to the 2-file delta described below.

## Net delta (this PR only, on top of #43366)

```
tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/test_hma_pp_per_layer_regions.py | 163 +++++
vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/worker.py             |  99 ++--
2 files changed, 241 insertions(+), 21 deletions(-)
```

## Changes

**`_ShardDescLayout`** grows two fields:
- `mamba_region_count: int = 0`
- `mamba_region_group_ids: tuple[int, ...] = ()`

**`_register_local_xfer_handler_for_shard`** builds local Mamba descriptors
when `self._has_mamba` is set, computes `mamba_region_group_ids` (each KV-group
id replicated 4× for Mamba's 4 SSM regions per layer), and embeds the result
into the per-shard layout.

**`add_remote_agent`** registers remote Mamba blocks per shard via
`_build_mamba_remote(nixl_agent_meta, tp_ratio, transfer_info)` and emits a
remote `_ShardDescLayout` carrying `mamba_region_count` /
`mamba_region_group_ids` for the consumer's transfer descriptor table.

**`_get_block_descs_ids_for_shard`** routes Mamba shards through a logical-
block-aware path: FA regions use `layout.num_blocks`, Mamba regions use
`layout.num_blocks // physical_blocks_per_logical` with an offset of
`num_fa_descs`. The non-Mamba path is unchanged.

The `register_kv_caches` rejection guard added in #43366 is dropped — hybrid
producers are now supported with `pp_size > 1`.

## Test Plan

### Unit test
```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/test_hma_pp_per_layer_regions.py
```

Covers the Mamba region group construction path: validates
`mamba_region_count`, `mamba_region_group_ids`, descriptor ID offset math,
and the FA-vs-Mamba grouping in `_ShardDescLayout`.

### End-to-end (not yet validated on this PR)

We **have not** run an E2E hybrid model on PP × PD yet on the GB200 rig
this branch was developed on — the rig doesn't have a Mamba-based hybrid
model loaded. The unit test covers the per-shard descriptor construction
logic, which is the part PR #43366's rejection guard explicitly defers.
E2E validation on Jamba (or a similar hybrid) would need:

```bash
# Same layout as #43366's E2E setup, but the prefiller hosts a hybrid model
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 UCX_TLS=tcp,cuda_copy \
  VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_PORT=5600 \
  vllm serve <hybrid-model> \
  --pipeline-parallel-size 2 --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --max-model-len 32768 --port 8100 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer"}'

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2,3 UCX_TLS=tcp,cuda_copy \
  VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_PORT=5601 \
  vllm serve <hybrid-model> \
  --pipeline-parallel-size 1 --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --max-model-len 32768 --port 8200 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer"}'
```

Happy to keep this PR in draft until I (or a reviewer with access to a
Mamba-capable rig) runs that smoke test. Marking it draft for now.

### Lint
```bash
pre-commit run --files \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/test_hma_pp_per_layer_regions.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/worker.py
pre-commit run mypy-3.10 --hook-stage manual --files \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/test_hma_pp_per_layer_regions.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/worker.py
```
All hooks: Passed.

## Test Result

- Unit test added in this PR passes locally.
- All targeted pre-commit hooks pass on the changed files.
- E2E hybrid run: pending (see Test Plan).

## Why this is not a duplicate

Searched vLLM open PRs/issues on 2026-05-21 for `HMA pipeline parallel`,
`Mamba disaggregated NIXL`, `hybrid PP P/D`. No open work targets the
Mamba × NIXL PD path under pipeline parallelism. The HMA × P/D paths that
do exist (e.g. `test_nixl_connector_hma.py` upstream) cover non-PP
topologies only.

## AI assistance disclosure

This change was drafted with AI assistance (Claude Code, Opus 4.7). The
submitting human reviewed every changed line and ran the unit test
referenced above. This PR is the deliberate HMA × PP follow-up referenced
in PR #43366's description.

- [x] The test results (unit test passes; E2E pending).

author: keboo
body:
The database migration job was repeatedly failing with `SqlException` login errors for the token principal, and retrying the same failure only delayed feedback.

This change updates `deploy-database` in `build-and-deploy.yml` to authenticate with the infra service principal (`ARM_CLIENT_ID_INFRA` / matching tenant and subscription), which is aligned with how SQL access is provisioned. It also removes the migration retry loop so `efbundle` runs once and fails fast with the real error.

This keeps the migration step deterministic and makes auth failures visible immediately instead of after repeated retries.

author: bbesner
body:
## Summary

Adds `docs/secrets.md` — the customer-facing note describing Memstem's secret-handling architecture and the responsibility boundary as a hosting provider.

## Why

We need to put customers on notice up front about what Memstem will commit to doing for secret protection and where the boundary stops. The industry pattern (GitHub secret scanning, AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault, etc.) is *platform provides tooling + best-effort detection, customer is responsible for actually using the vault*. This doc commits to that pattern in writing.

## What's in the doc

- Architecture: three layers (assistant primary, ingest scrub backstop, optional LLM scan)
- In-scope / out-of-scope table — the authoritative responsibility boundary
- Shipping-status markers (🟢/🟡/⚪) so customers can tell promised vs. available today
- Retrieval-time placeholder behavior
- Pluggable `SecretBackend` interface for customers with existing vaults
- Plain-language disclaimer ("not a compliance certification, not a guarantee, not legal advice")

The README gains a bullet linking to it.

## What's explicitly out of scope

Documented up front to manage expectations:

- Pre-flight scrubbing of outbound LLM API calls
- Detection of free-form secrets without pattern context (without the opt-in premium LLM-scan tier)
- Real-time alerts when the assistant verbalizes a secret
- Retroactive scrubbing of secrets already sent to LLM vendors

## Test plan

- [x] Spell-check + reads cleanly
- [ ] Reviewer sanity check on the responsibility boundary

This pull request introduces the initial v0.1.0 feature release of the Surf web framework, focusing on closing key framework gaps, improving performance, and providing comprehensive documentation. It adds major new features such as per-route and per-group middleware, error-returning handlers, a typed service container, SPA serving, metrics, and WebSocket support. Additionally, it includes a detailed changelog, a performance roadmap, and a new benchmarks suite that compares Surf against other popular Go frameworks.

The most important changes are:

**Documentation and Feature Overview:**
* Added a detailed `CHANGELOG.md` documenting all notable changes, new features, performance improvements, and intentional behavior changes for v0.1.0.
* Updated `README.md` with a comprehensive feature list, usage examples, and a dedicated section outlining all v0.1.0 features, including middleware, error handling, fast-path handlers, binding, JSON helpers, typed services, SPA, metrics, logging, rate limiting, and WebSocket support. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L9-R27) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5R374-R564)

* Introduced a new `benchmarks` module with a benchmark suite (`bench_test.go`) that compares Surf (standard and fast path) against gin, echo, chi, and net/http, using a dependency-free approach for the main module. These changes collectively deliver a robust, high-performance, and well-documented foundation for Surf, with clear paths for future improvements.

author: smdurgan
body:
## Summary

- Unified OAuth callback at `/api/oauth/callback` (admin subdomain) for AI Employee connector consent flows. Single endpoint dispatches to any provider; provider is carried in a signed state parameter.
- HMAC-SHA256 stateless state with 10-minute TTL, signed by `OAUTH_STATE_SIGNING_KEY`. State payload binds `(customer_id, provider, reviewer_id, nonce, expiry)`. CSRF defense: callback rejects unless the state's `reviewer_id` matches the currently authenticated admin session.
- Provider registry ships `microsoft-graph` (Azure AD v2) and `google-workspace`. Token responses normalized to a shared shape so the store contract is provider-agnostic.
- Token storage interface per [ADR 0010](docs/adr/0010-per-customer-oauth-token-storage.md) — tokens live on the customer's Fly volume, not in the Worker. v1 ships a no-op store that records the storage intent; the Hermes Machine relay is wired in a follow-on.
- Audit emission for `token-issued` / `token-rejected` with a console writer; the D1 `audit_log` persistence is deferred to #891.
- Middleware exempts `/api/oauth/*` from the admin subdomain rewrite (matching the existing `/api/auth/*` precedent) so the endpoint resolves at `admin.smd.services/api/oauth/callback`.

No token material is logged, returned in response bodies, or placed in URLs. Issuer error payloads stay on the server side; callbacks surface short reason codes (`provider_error`, `missing_params`, `bad_state`, `expired_state`, `reviewer_mismatch`, `unknown_provider`, `exchange_failed`, `store_failed`) to the dashboard.

Closes #879. Refs ADR 0010, `docs/specs/ai-employee/oauth-lifecycle.md`.

## Deferred ACs

Two `TODO(#NNN)` deferrals, both load-bearing for v1 but unblocked by infrastructure that lands separately:

- **`src/lib/oauth/audit.ts` — TODO(#891).** The audit-log persistence layer (D1 `audit_log` table per `docs/specs/ai-employee/d1-schema.md`) is the explicit deliverable of #891. This PR ships the audit-event emission shape (`oauth-callback.token-issued` / `token-rejected`) and a console-only writer; when #891 lands, the swap is a one-line change inside `audit.ts`. Shipping the callback ahead of #891 is correct sequencing — the callback is on the critical path for connector consent in customer-zero, the audit table can backfill from console logs in the interim, and a stable event shape is what #891 needs to consume.
- **`src/lib/oauth/store.ts` — TODO #879-follow-on.** Per [ADR 0010](docs/adr/0010-per-customer-oauth-token-storage.md), tokens live on the customer's Fly volume. The Worker can't write a Fly volume directly; it must POST the token to an authenticated control-plane endpoint on the customer's Hermes Machine. That Machine endpoint and the per-customer Machine registry it needs (hostname + auth token per `customer_id`) are not yet wired — they layer in with #850 and the Hermes Machine control plane work. v1 ships the storage interface plus a no-op implementation that audits the intent so the callback path can be exercised end-to-end without a real Machine. Follow-on issue will be filed in the same area as #850 once the control-plane surface is named; the TODO points at it explicitly so the swap is a one-line callback edit.

Neither deferral compromises the security boundary: the signed-state CSRF defense, reviewer-binding, and "no token material in logs / URLs" guarantees all ship in this PR.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck` — 0 errors on changed files
- [x] `npx prettier --check` on changed files — clean
- [x] `npx eslint` on changed files — clean
- [x] `npx vitest run tests/oauth-callback.test.ts` — 25/25 passing
  - state.ts: round-trip, bad-signature on tampered payload, signature failure under key rotation, expiry, malformed, missing-key error, TTL default
  - providers: registry exposure, unknown slug → null, MS Graph + Google endpoint URLs
  - callback: every failure path (provider error, missing params, bad/expired state, three reviewer-mismatch variants, unknown provider, exchange failure)
  - callback: success path on google-workspace, dispatch correctness for microsoft-graph
  - source-level: no token material in console logs, audit writer carries `#891` TODO, store cites ADR 0010
- [ ] Provision OAuth client credentials in production: `OAUTH_STATE_SIGNING_KEY` (`openssl rand -base64 32`), `MICROSOFT_GRAPH_CLIENT_ID` / `MICROSOFT_GRAPH_CLIENT_SECRET` (Azure AD app registration with `${ADMIN_BASE_URL}/api/oauth/callback` in the redirect URI list). `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` / `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` are already provisioned for booking.

author: uqio
body:
Adds the M3 generation-stats + logprobs surface for `mlxrs::lm::generate` faithful to `mlx_lm/generate.py::GenerationResult` + `mlx-swift-lm/MLXLMCommon/Generate.swift::GenerateResult`.

## Surface

### New types
- `GenConfig.collect_logprobs: bool` (default `false`) — opt-in for per-step logprobs materialization.
- `GenStep.logprobs: Option<Array>` — `Some` iff `collect_logprobs=true`; `None` otherwise (zero allocation when off). Kept as `Option<Array>` not `Option<Vec<f32>>` per `feedback_no_implicit_eval` — caller materializes via explicit `.to_vec()`/`.as_slice()` at their boundary.
- `pub struct GenerationStats { prompt_tokens, generation_tokens, prompt_tps, generation_tps, peak_memory_bytes }`.
- `generate(...)` return type: `Result<String>` → `Result<(String, GenerationStats)>`.

### New module `mlxrs::memory`
Thin safe wrappers around mlx-c `mlx_get_peak_memory` / `mlx_reset_peak_memory` / `mlx_get_active_memory` / `mlx_get_cache_memory` (process-global byte counts; mirrors mlx-swift `GPU.peakMemory`).

### Cross-crate
- `vlm::generate` zero-image branch now sets `lm.collect_logprobs = true` before delegating, preserving the documented cross-branch "VLM emits unconditional logprobs" contract.
- `audio::stt::generate` unaffected (has own SttGenerator that constructs sampler/processors itself).

## Zero-cost opt-out (R2 design)
`logsumexp + subtract` is gated behind `if cfg.collect_logprobs || needs_logprobs`, where `needs_logprobs = (temp != 0.0) && (top_p > 0 < 1)` mirrors `make_sampler`'s `do_top_p` gate. Every sampler EXCEPT top_p is shift-invariant or softmaxes internally (argmax, top_k argpartition, min_p threshold, xtc internal softmax, categorical internal softmax) — they sample byte-identically from raw post-processor logits. A 3-way `match (needs_normalization, temp > 0)` covers: full normalize / cheap max-shift / raw logits.

## Numerical-safety scope (documented in module doc)
Two extreme-temp configurations still produce non-finite distributions inside `sample::categorical_sampling` itself (the bug is in the primitive, not the generation loop): f16 logits + `temp < 1/65504`, and any dtype + subnormal positive `temp < 1.0/f32::MAX`. Both share the same root: `categorical_sampling` computes `1.0/temp` in f32 then multiplies by `scalar_like(1/temp, logits)` in the logits dtype. LM/VLM/STT share this via `make_sampler`. **Deferred to a dedicated `fix(lm/sample)` follow-up PR** that updates `sample.rs` + all three call sites consistently (per `feedback_review_finding_must_be_in_diff` + `feedback_escalate_dont_spiral`). A LM-only argmax bypass was prototyped in R3+R4 and reverted in R5 — it failed to cover VLM/STT and silently skipped configured sampler stages (XTC/top_k/min_p). The fix must land IN THE PRIMITIVE (divide instead of multiply, or argmax route after upstream sampler stages run); a naive `1/temp` f64 upcast is only partial mitigation (f16 cast still overflows).

## Tests
- `generate_step_default_skips_logsumexp_normalization` — zero-cost default verified via peak_memory.
- `generate_step_top_p_forces_normalization_even_when_off` — top_p config forces normalization regardless of `collect_logprobs`.
- `generate_step_logprob_matches_log_softmax` — hand-traced parity for opt-in path.
- `generate_step_opt_out_max_shift_stable_with_large_bias` — R2 stochastic max-shift safety.
- `generate_step_opt_out_greedy_zero_temp` — pure-greedy opt-out byte-identical.
- `generate_returns_generation_stats` + `stream_generate_peak_memory_is_monotonic` + `generate_zero_max_tokens_stats` — stats wiring.
- `vlm_generate_zero_image_preserves_logprobs` — VLM zero-image regression.
- 2 tests in new `mlxrs::memory` module.

## Codex adversarial review
APPROVE on the feature scope after 7 rounds. The journey:
- R1 → R2: zero-cost opt-out refactor + VLM zero-image fix + max-shift in stochastic opt-out path.
- R3 → R4: LM-only argmax bypass for f16/subnormal temp NaN-safety.
- R5: structural pivot — REVERTED R3+R4 (LM-only patch couldn't cover VLM/STT and broke XTC). The categorical_sampling NaN class is a separate follow-up PR scope.
- R6 → R7: doc-only refinements documenting the deferred scope with verifiable inline detail (no external trackers).

body:
## Summary
Refactored team display across multiple story mode facilities (Cable Link, Evo Lab, Colress, Fan Club) to use a collapsible accordion pattern. Only the first Pokémon is expanded by default, with collapsed cards showing a compact summary. This improves performance by deferring expensive computations (like `buildPokemon()`) until a card is actually expanded.

## Key Changes

- **Accordion state management**: Added `_storyLinkOpenIdx`, `_storyEvoLabOpenIdx`, `_storyColressOpenIdx`, and `_storyFanClubOpenIdx` variables to track which team member is currently expanded in each facility.

- **Generic delegation handler**: Implemented `_initStoryMonAccordionDelegation()` to handle click events for:
  - Collapse-all chips
  - Mon-switcher pills (quick navigation between team members)
  - Header toggle buttons (expand/collapse individual cards)
  - Automatic smooth scrolling to the expanded card

- **Lazy computation**: Moved expensive operations into the expanded-only path:
  - `buildPokemon()` calls deferred until card is expanded
  - Per-evolution card generation in Evo Lab only happens when expanded
  - Colress gimmick sections only rendered for the active card

- **Compact collapsed headers**: Each collapsed card now displays:
  - Pokémon sprite and name
  - One-line summary (e.g., evolution options, gimmick + held item, IV/EV stats)
  - Chevron indicator (▴/▾) showing expand/collapse state

- **Mon-switcher UI**: Added `_txMonSwitcherHtml()` pill-based navigation bar at the top of each facility's team list, allowing quick jumps between team members.

- **Scroll position preservation**: Maintained switcher scroll position across re-renders to prevent jarring UI shifts.

## Implementation Details

- All four facilities now follow the same accordion pattern for consistency
- Collapsed cards skip the `buildPokemon()` call entirely, providing significant performance gains for 6-mon teams
- Summary lines are computed once per render and reused in both collapsed and expanded states
- Event delegation uses `data-facility` attributes to isolate click handlers per facility
- Smooth scrolling behavior added when navigating via switcher pills or header toggles

## Summary

- Hubble shows steady `Policy denied DROPPED` SYNs from `mcp-system/prometheus-mcp` → `observability/prometheus-kube-prometheus-stack-0:9090`.
- Source egress in `mcp-system/prometheus-mcp-allow` already permits the call; destination ingress in `observability/prometheus-allow` whitelisted only `network/envoy` and `home/home-assistant`. CNPs need both sides.
- Adds a third `fromEndpoints` entry for `mcp-system/prometheus-mcp` (label `app.kubernetes.io/name: prometheus-mcp`) to the existing :9090 ingress rule.

## Why

Same both-sides-CNP failure mode as the holmesgpt drop fixed in PR #11889. The MCP backend pod queries Prometheus via `PROMETHEUS_URL`; without the destination ingress hole the call never lands.

## Test plan

- [ ] Flux reconciles `kube-prometheus-stack` Kustomization.
- [ ] `kubectl -n observability get cnp prometheus-allow -o yaml` shows the new `fromEndpoints` entry.
- [ ] `hubble observe --since 5m --verdict DROPPED --to-namespace observability` from any cilium agent on the worker hosting `prometheus-mcp-*` returns empty for the mcp-system → prometheus pair.
- [ ] `prometheus-mcp` tool calls via the gateway succeed against live Prometheus (e.g., `execute_query`).
